✖ bites – V1+s (present); bitten – V3 (past participle); bited – incorrect form.

q: Fill in the blank: There ___ a letter on the table.
exp:
✔ 'There + be' संरचना में verb अपने बाद आने वाले noun के अनुसार चलता है; यहाँ 'a letter' एकवचन है, इसलिए 'is' सही है।
📌 नियम: There is + singular noun (There is a book.); There are + plural noun (There are many books.)। Uncountable noun के साथ 'is' – There is some water.
✖ 'am' केवल 'I' के साथ आता है; 'has/have' यहाँ 'be' का स्थान नहीं ले सकते; गलत वचन वाला is/are अशुद्ध है।
expe:
✔ In the 'There + be' structure the verb agrees with the noun that follows; here 'a letter' is singular, so 'is' is correct.
📌 Rule: There is + singular noun (There is a book.); There are + plural noun (There are many books.). With uncountable nouns use 'is' – There is some water.
✖ 'am' goes only with 'I'; 'has/have' cannot replace 'be' here; is/are of the wrong number is incorrect.

q: Fill in the blank: ___ Suresh watch a film twice a week?
exp:
✔ Simple Present के प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य में third person singular subject ('Suresh') के साथ 'Does' आता है और मुख्य verb मूल रूप (V1) में रहता है ('twice a week' आदत/नियमित क्रिया दर्शाता है)।
📌 नियम: Does + He/She/It/एकवचन + V1 …?; Do + I/You/We/They/बहुवचन + V1 …? उदाहरण – Does she cook daily? / Do they play?
✖ 'Do' plural subjects के लिए; 'Is' के साथ V-ing चाहिए; 'Has' के साथ V3 चाहिए।
expe:
✔ In a Simple Present question, a third person singular subject ('Suresh') takes 'Does' and the main verb stays in base form (V1) ('twice a week' shows a habitual action).
📌 Rule: Does + He/She/It/singular + V1 …?; Do + I/You/We/They/plural + V1 …? E.g. Does she cook daily? / Do they play?
✖ 'Do' is for plural subjects; 'Is' needs V-ing; 'Has' needs V3.

q: Fill in the blank: Seema ___ the windows every Sunday.
exp:
✔ Subject 'Seema' third person singular है और 'every Sunday' आदत/नियमित क्रिया दर्शाता है, इसलिए Simple Present में V1+s/es = 'cleans' आएगा।
📌 नियम: He/She/It/एकवचन नाम + V1+s/es; जैसे – She reads daily. -o, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x पर -es लगता है (goes, watches)।
✖ बिना -s वाला रूप plural subject के लिए है; -ing रूप बिना is/are के गलत है; 'been + -ing' के लिए has चाहिए।
expe:
✔ The subject 'Seema' is third person singular and 'every Sunday' shows a habitual action, so Simple Present takes V1+s/es = 'cleans'.
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; e.g. She reads daily. Verbs ending in -o, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x take -es (goes, watches).
✖ The form without -s is for plural subjects; the -ing form without is/are is wrong; 'been + -ing' needs has.

q: Fill in the blank: Last month, they ___ bread.
exp:
✔ 'Last month' बीते हुए निश्चित समय को दर्शाता है, इसलिए Simple Past (V2) 'baked' आएगा।
📌 Past time markers – yesterday, ago, last week/month/year, the day before yesterday, in 2020। ध्यान दें: निश्चित भूतकाल शब्द के साथ Present Perfect (has/have + V3) का प्रयोग नहीं होता।
✖ will + V1 – Future; V1/V1+s – Present; has/have + V3 – Present Perfect, जो निश्चित past time के साथ गलत है।
expe:
✔ 'Last month' indicates a definite past time, so Simple Past (V2) 'baked' is used.
📌 Past time markers – yesterday, ago, last week/month/year, the day before yesterday, in 2020. Note: Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is not used with a definite past time expression.
✖ will + V1 – Future; V1/V1+s – Present; has/have + V3 – Present Perfect, wrong with a definite past time.

q: Fill in the blank: The boys ___ the birds at the moment.
exp:
✔ 'at the moment' अभी चल रही क्रिया दर्शाता है, इसलिए Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing) आएगा; subject 'The boys' के साथ 'are feeding' सही है।
📌 नियम: I – am; He/She/It/एकवचन – is; You/We/They/बहुवचन – are + V-ing। संकेत शब्द – now, right now, at this moment, at the moment, Look!, Listen!
✖ Simple Present (V1/V1+s) आदत दर्शाता है; was/were + -ing – Past Continuous; गलत subject-verb agreement (is/are) वाला विकल्प भी अशुद्ध है।
expe:
✔ 'at the moment' shows an action going on now, so Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing) is used; with subject 'The boys', 'are feeding' is correct.
📌 Rule: I – am; He/She/It/singular – is; You/We/They/plural – are + V-ing. Signal words – now, right now, at this moment, at the moment, Look!, Listen!
✖ Simple Present (V1/V1+s) shows habit; was/were + -ing – Past Continuous; the option with wrong subject-verb agreement (is/are) is also incorrect.

q: Fill in the blank: Manoj ___ the books next week.
exp:
✔ 'next week' भविष्य का समय दर्शाता है, इसलिए Simple Future – will + V1 = 'will print' आएगा।
📌 नियम: Subject + will + V1 (सभी subjects के साथ); भविष्य संकेत शब्द – tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon, in future।
✖ was/were + -ing – Past Continuous; V2 – Simple Past; has/have + V3 – Present Perfect – ये भविष्य के समय-संकेत से मेल नहीं खाते।
expe:
✔ 'next week' indicates future time, so Simple Future – will + V1 = 'will print' is used.
📌 Rule: Subject + will + V1 (with all subjects); future signal words – tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon, in future.
✖ was/were + -ing – Past Continuous; V2 – Simple Past; has/have + V3 – Present Perfect – none fits a future time marker.

q: What is the past (V2) form of the verb 'swim'?
exp:
✔ 'Swim' irregular verb है; इसके रूप – V1 swim, V2 swam, V3 swum। अतः past (V2) रूप 'swam' है।
📌 i–a–u पैटर्न के अन्य verbs – sing–sang–sung, drink–drank–drunk, begin–began–begun, ring–rang–rung।
✖ swum – V3 (past participle); swims – V1+s (present); swimed – अशुद्ध रूप।
expe:
✔ 'Swim' is an irregular verb: V1 swim, V2 swam, V3 swum. So the past (V2) form is 'swam'.
📌 Other i–a–u verbs – sing–sang–sung, drink–drank–drunk, begin–began–begun, ring–rang–rung.
✖ swum – V3 (past participle); swims – V1+s (present); swimed – incorrect form.

q: Fill in the blank: There ___ ten players in the ground.
exp:
✔ 'There + be' संरचना में verb अपने बाद आने वाले noun के अनुसार चलता है; यहाँ 'ten players' बहुवचन है, इसलिए 'are' सही है।
📌 नियम: There is + singular noun (There is a book.); There are + plural noun (There are many books.)। Uncountable noun के साथ 'is' – There is some water.
✖ 'am' केवल 'I' के साथ आता है; 'has/have' यहाँ 'be' का स्थान नहीं ले सकते; गलत वचन वाला is/are अशुद्ध है।
expe:
✔ In the 'There + be' structure the verb agrees with the noun that follows; here 'ten players' is plural, so 'are' is correct.
📌 Rule: There is + singular noun (There is a book.); There are + plural noun (There are many books.). With uncountable nouns use 'is' – There is some water.
✖ 'am' goes only with 'I'; 'has/have' cannot replace 'be' here; is/are of the wrong number is incorrect.

q: Fill in the blank: My friends ___ not lock the door every day.
exp:
✔ Simple Present के negative वाक्य में plural subject ('My friends') के साथ 'do not + V1' आता है – My friends do not lock the door every day।
📌 नियम: I/You/We/They/बहुवचन + do not + V1; He/She/It/एकवचन + does not + V1 (जैसे – He does not lock …)। does/do के बाद verb हमेशा मूल रूप में।
✖ 'are' के साथ V-ing चाहिए; 'does' singular subject के लिए; 'have' के साथ V3 (locked) चाहिए।
expe:
✔ In a Simple Present negative sentence a plural subject ('My friends') takes 'do not + V1' – My friends do not lock the door every day.
📌 Rule: I/You/We/They/plural + do not + V1; He/She/It/singular + does not + V1 (e.g. He does not lock …). After do/does the verb is always in base form.
✖ 'are' needs V-ing; 'does' is for singular subjects; 'have' needs V3 (locked).

q: Fill in the blank: Our neighbour ___ the door twice a week.
exp:
✔ 'twice a week' आदत/नियमित कार्य बताता है → Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान)। कर्ता 'Our neighbour' third-person singular है, इसलिए V1 + s/es = 'locks': "Our neighbour locks the door twice a week."
📌 नियम: He/She/It/एकवचन संज्ञा + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/बहुवचन + V1। -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o वाली क्रियाओं में -es लगता है (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries)।
✖ locking – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता। lock – मूल रूप (V1) I/we/you/they या बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Our neighbour' के साथ नहीं। been locking – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'twice a week' shows a habitual/repeated action → Simple Present. The subject 'Our neighbour' is third-person singular, so V1 + s/es = 'locks': "Our neighbour locks the door twice a week."
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ locking – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were. lock – base form (V1) is used with I/we/you/they or plural subjects, not with 'Our neighbour'. been locking – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it.

q: Fill in the blank: Manoj ___ a novel last Sunday.
exp:
✔ 'last Sunday' निश्चित भूतकाल का समय-सूचक है → Simple Past (सामान्य भूत) (कर्ता + V2)। 'read' क्रिया का V2 रूप है: "Manoj read a novel last Sunday."
📌 भूतकाल सूचक: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2। इनके साथ Present Perfect (has/have + V3) गलत है। Simple Past में सभी कर्ताओं के साथ क्रिया का एक ही रूप आता है।
✖ reads – Simple Present का रूप; आदत/वर्तमान तथ्य के लिए, भूतकाल के लिए नहीं। will read – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। has read – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'last Sunday' जैसे निश्चित भूतकाल-सूचक के साथ प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ 'last Sunday' is a definite past time marker → Simple Past (subject + V2). 'read' is the V2 form: "Manoj read a novel last Sunday."
📌 Past markers: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2. With such words Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is wrong. In Simple Past the verb form is the same for all subjects.
✖ reads – Simple Present form; used for habits/present facts, not past time. will read – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. has read – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); cannot be used with a definite past time like 'last Sunday'.

q: Fill in the blank: Look! We ___ these sums.
exp:
✔ 'Look!' बताता है कि कार्य अभी चल रहा है → Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) (is/am/are + V-ing)। कर्ता 'We' के साथ 'are' आएगा, अतः 'are solving' सही है: "Look! We are solving these sums."
📌 संकेत शब्द: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment। I → am; He/She/It/एकवचन → is; We/You/They/बहुवचन → are।
✖ solve – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं। is solving – 'is' एकवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है; 'We' के साथ 'are' चाहिए। were solving – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए।
expe:
✔ 'Look!' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'We' takes 'are', so 'are solving' is correct: "Look! We are solving these sums."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.
✖ solve – Simple Present; shows habit, not an action in progress now. is solving – 'is' goes with a singular subject; 'We' needs 'are'. were solving – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past.

q: Fill in the blank: Harish ___ these books the day after tomorrow.
exp:
✔ 'the day after tomorrow' भविष्य का समय बताता है → Simple Future (सामान्य भविष्य) (will + V1)। अतः 'will read' सही है: "Harish will read these books the day after tomorrow."
📌 भविष्य सूचक: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon। 'will' के बाद हर कर्ता के साथ क्रिया का मूल रूप (V1) आता है (will go, will write)।
✖ was reading – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। has read – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); निश्चित समय-सूचक (yesterday/next/every day) के साथ नहीं आता। read – Simple Past (V2); पूर्ण हो चुके भूतकालीन कार्य के लिए, 'the day after tomorrow' के साथ नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'the day after tomorrow' refers to future time → Simple Future (will + V1). So 'will read' is correct: "Harish will read these books the day after tomorrow."
📌 Future markers: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon. 'Will' is followed by the base verb (V1) for every subject (will go, will write).
✖ was reading – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past. has read – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); not used with a definite time like yesterday/next/every day. read – Simple Past (V2); used for completed past actions, not 'the day after tomorrow'.

q: What is the past (V2) form of the verb 'ring'?
exp:
✔ 'ring' के रूप हैं: ring – rang – rung। इसका past (V2) रूप 'rang' है, जो Simple Past में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 यह irregular verb है – इसी तरह के रूप: sing – sang – sung, drink – drank – drunk, swim – swam – swum।
✖ rung – यह V3 (past participle) है, has/have/had के साथ आता है। ringing – present participle (V-ing), continuous tense में प्रयोग होता है। rings – third-person singular का वर्तमान काल रूप।
expe:
✔ The forms of 'ring' are ring – rang – rung. The past (V2) form is 'rang', used in Simple Past.
📌 Irregular verb – similar pattern: sing – sang – sung, drink – drank – drunk, swim – swam – swum.
✖ rung – this is V3 (past participle), used with has/have/had. ringing – present participle (V-ing), used in continuous tenses. rings – present tense form for third-person singular.

q: Fill in the blank: There ___ some shops in the market.
exp:
✔ 'There + be' वाक्यों में क्रिया बाद में आने वाली संज्ञा के अनुसार होती है। 'some shops in the market' बहुवचन है, इसलिए 'are' आएगा: "There are some shops in the market."
📌 There is + a/an/one + एकवचन संज्ञा (There is a pen); There are + बहुवचन संज्ञा / a few / some / many + बहुवचन (There are some shops)। अगणनीय संज्ञा के साथ: There is some milk।
✖ is – एकवचन संज्ञा से पहले आता है, जबकि यहाँ संज्ञा बहुवचन है। has – अधिकार/स्वामित्व बताता है; 'There ___' संरचना में 'be' का रूप (is/are) चाहिए। am – केवल कर्ता 'I' के साथ आता है।
expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'some shops in the market' is plural, so 'are' is used: "There are some shops in the market."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.
✖ is – used before a singular noun, but here the noun is plural. has – shows possession; 'There ___' structure needs a form of 'be' (is/are). am – used only with the subject 'I'.

q: Fill in the blank: Amit ___ not read these books every day.
exp:
✔ Simple Present का निषेधात्मक वाक्य: कर्ता + does/do + not + V1। 'Amit' third-person singular है, इसलिए 'does not' + V1 'read': "Amit does not read these books every day."
📌 does/doesn't के बाद मुख्य क्रिया में -s/-es नहीं लगता: 'She does not play' ('plays' नहीं)। I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't)।
✖ has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं। do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Amit' के साथ नहीं। is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं।
expe:
✔ Simple Present negative: subject + does/do + not + V1. 'Amit' is third-person singular, so 'does not' + V1 'read': "Amit does not read these books every day."
📌 After does/doesn't the main verb loses -s/-es: 'She does not play' (not 'plays'). I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't).
✖ has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1. do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'Amit'. is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is.

q: Fill in the blank: They ___ the car every morning.
exp:
✔ 'every morning' आदत/नियमित कार्य बताता है → Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान)। कर्ता 'They' बहुवचन है, इसलिए क्रिया का मूल रूप (V1) 'wash' बिना -s/-es के आएगा: "They wash the car every morning."
📌 नियम: He/She/It/एकवचन संज्ञा + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/बहुवचन + V1। -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o वाली क्रियाओं में -es लगता है (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries)।
✖ washes – -s/-es वाला रूप केवल third-person singular कर्ता के साथ आता है। washing – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता। been washing – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'every morning' shows a habitual/repeated action → Simple Present. The subject 'They' is plural, so the base verb (V1) 'wash' is used without -s/-es: "They wash the car every morning."
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ washes – -s/-es form is used only with a third-person singular subject. washing – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were. been washing – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it.

q: Fill in the blank: My mother ___ a cake last Sunday.
exp:

q: Fill in the blank: There ___ a few windows in this room.

expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'a few windows in this room' is plural, so 'are' is used: "There are a few windows in this room."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.

q: Fill in the blank: There ___ a computer in the office.
exp:
✔ 'There + be' वाक्यों में क्रिया बाद में आने वाली संज्ञा के अनुसार होती है। 'a computer in the office' एकवचन है, इसलिए 'is' आएगा: "There is a computer in the office."
📌 There is + a/an/one + एकवचन संज्ञा (There is a pen); There are + बहुवचन संज्ञा / a few / some / many + बहुवचन (There are some shops)। अगणनीय संज्ञा के साथ: There is some milk।
✖ are – बहुवचन संज्ञा से पहले आता है, जबकि यहाँ संज्ञा एकवचन है। have – अधिकार/स्वामित्व बताता है; 'There ___' संरचना में 'be' का रूप (is/are) चाहिए। am – केवल कर्ता 'I' के साथ आता है।
expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'a computer in the office' is singular, so 'is' is used: "There is a computer in the office."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.
✖ are – used before a plural noun, but here the noun is singular. have – shows possession; 'There ___' structure needs a form of 'be' (is/are). am – used only with the subject 'I'.

q: Fill in the blank: ___ Usha cook dinner every evening?
exp:
✔ Simple Present का प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य: Does/Do + कर्ता + V1? 'Usha' third-person singular है, इसलिए 'Does' + V1 'cook': "Does Usha cook dinner every evening?"
📌 Does वाले प्रश्न में मुख्य क्रिया V1 में रहती है: 'Does he play?' ('plays' नहीं)। Do → I/we/you/they/बहुवचन; Does → he/she/it/एकवचन संज्ञा।
✖ Do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Usha' के साथ नहीं। Has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं। Is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं।
expe:
✔ Simple Present question: Does/Do + subject + V1? 'Usha' is third-person singular, so 'Does' + V1 'cook': "Does Usha cook dinner every evening?"
📌 In questions with Does, the main verb stays in V1: 'Does he play?' (not 'plays'). Do → I/we/you/they/plural; Does → he/she/it/singular noun.
✖ Do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'Usha'. Has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1. Is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is.

q: Fill in the blank: My mother ___ mathematics twice a week.
exp:

✖ teaching – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता। teach – मूल रूप (V1) I/we/you/they या बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'My mother' के साथ नहीं। been teaching – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'twice a week' shows a habitual/repeated action → Simple Present. The subject 'My mother' is third-person singular, so V1 + s/es = 'teaches': "My mother teaches mathematics twice a week."
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ teaching – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were. teach – base form (V1) is used with I/we/you/they or plural subjects, not with 'My mother'. been teaching – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it.

✖ prepare – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं। were preparing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। is preparing – 'is' एकवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है; 'The boys' के साथ 'are' चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'at the moment' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'The boys' takes 'are', so 'are preparing' is correct: "The boys are preparing the notes at the moment."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.

q: What is the past participle (V3) form of the verb 'fly'?
exp:
✔ 'fly' के रूप हैं: fly – flew – flown। इसका past participle (V3) रूप 'flown' है, जो has/have/had और passive voice में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 यह irregular verb है – इसी तरह के रूप: draw – drew – drawn, grow – grew – grown, know – knew – known।
✖ flyed – ऐसा कोई रूप नहीं; 'fly' irregular है, इसमें -ed नहीं लगता। flying – present participle (V-ing), continuous tense में प्रयोग होता है। flew – यह V2 (simple past) है, past participle नहीं।
expe:
✔ The forms of 'fly' are fly – flew – flown. The past participle (V3) is 'flown', used with has/have/had and in the passive voice.
📌 Irregular verb – similar pattern: draw – drew – drawn, grow – grew – grown, know – knew – known.
✖ flyed – no such word; 'fly' is irregular and does not take -ed. flying – present participle (V-ing), used in continuous tenses. flew – this is V2 (simple past), not the past participle.

q: Fill in the blank: There ___ a chair in the room.
exp:
✔ 'There + be' वाक्यों में क्रिया बाद में आने वाली संज्ञा के अनुसार होती है। 'a chair in the room' एकवचन है, इसलिए 'is' आएगा: "There is a chair in the room."
📌 There is + a/an/one + एकवचन संज्ञा (There is a pen); There are + बहुवचन संज्ञा / a few / some / many + बहुवचन (There are some shops)। अगणनीय संज्ञा के साथ: There is some milk।
✖ have – अधिकार/स्वामित्व बताता है; 'There ___' संरचना में 'be' का रूप (is/are) चाहिए। am – केवल कर्ता 'I' के साथ आता है। are – बहुवचन संज्ञा से पहले आता है, जबकि यहाँ संज्ञा एकवचन है।
expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'a chair in the room' is singular, so 'is' is used: "There is a chair in the room."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.
✖ have – shows possession; 'There ___' structure needs a form of 'be' (is/are). am – used only with the subject 'I'. are – used before a plural noun, but here the noun is singular.

q: Fill in the blank: ___ Sita open the gate every day?
exp:
✔ Simple Present का प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य: Does/Do + कर्ता + V1? 'Sita' third-person singular है, इसलिए 'Does' + V1 'open': "Does Sita open the gate every day?"
📌 Does वाले प्रश्न में मुख्य क्रिया V1 में रहती है: 'Does he play?' ('plays' नहीं)। Do → I/we/you/they/बहुवचन; Does → he/she/it/एकवचन संज्ञा।
✖ Do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Sita' के साथ नहीं। Is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं। Has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं।
expe:
✔ Simple Present question: Does/Do + subject + V1? 'Sita' is third-person singular, so 'Does' + V1 'open': "Does Sita open the gate every day?"
📌 In questions with Does, the main verb stays in V1: 'Does he play?' (not 'plays'). Do → I/we/you/they/plural; Does → he/she/it/singular noun.
✖ Do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'Sita'. Is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is. Has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1.

q: Fill in the blank: Geeta ___ the shoes on Mondays.
exp:
✔ 'on Mondays' आदत/नियमित कार्य बताता है → Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान)। कर्ता 'Geeta' third-person singular है, इसलिए V1 + s/es = 'polishes': "Geeta polishes the shoes on Mondays."
📌 नियम: He/She/It/एकवचन संज्ञा + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/बहुवचन + V1। -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o वाली क्रियाओं में -es लगता है (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries)।
✖ polishing – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता। been polishing – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए। polish – मूल रूप (V1) I/we/you/they या बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Geeta' के साथ नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'on Mondays' shows a habitual/repeated action → Simple Present. The subject 'Geeta' is third-person singular, so V1 + s/es = 'polishes': "Geeta polishes the shoes on Mondays."
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ polishing – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were. been polishing – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it. polish – base form (V1) is used with I/we/you/they or plural subjects, not with 'Geeta'.

q: Fill in the blank: My friends ___ photographs yesterday.
exp:
✔ 'yesterday' निश्चित भूतकाल का समय-सूचक है → Simple Past (सामान्य भूत) (कर्ता + V2)। 'took' क्रिया का V2 रूप है: "My friends took photographs yesterday."
📌 भूतकाल सूचक: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2। इनके साथ Present Perfect (has/have + V3) गलत है। Simple Past में सभी कर्ताओं के साथ क्रिया का एक ही रूप आता है।
✖ take – Simple Present का रूप; आदत/वर्तमान तथ्य के लिए, भूतकाल के लिए नहीं। will take – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। have taken – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'yesterday' जैसे निश्चित भूतकाल-सूचक के साथ प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ 'yesterday' is a definite past time marker → Simple Past (subject + V2). 'took' is the V2 form: "My friends took photographs yesterday."
📌 Past markers: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2. With such words Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is wrong. In Simple Past the verb form is the same for all subjects.
✖ take – Simple Present form; used for habits/present facts, not past time. will take – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. have taken – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); cannot be used with a definite past time like 'yesterday'.

q: Fill in the blank: Seema ___ the answer sheets right now.
exp:
✔ 'right now' बताता है कि कार्य अभी चल रहा है → Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) (is/am/are + V-ing)। कर्ता 'Seema' के साथ 'is' आएगा, अतः 'is checking' सही है: "Seema is checking the answer sheets right now."
📌 संकेत शब्द: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment। I → am; He/She/It/एकवचन → is; We/You/They/बहुवचन → are।
✖ was checking – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। checks – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं। are checking – 'are' बहुवचन कर्ता/you के साथ आता है; 'Seema' के साथ 'is' चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'right now' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'Seema' takes 'is', so 'is checking' is correct: "Seema is checking the answer sheets right now."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.
✖ was checking – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past. checks – Simple Present; shows habit, not an action in progress now. are checking – 'are' goes with plural subjects/you; 'Seema' needs 'is'.

q: Fill in the blank: My brother ___ the car next Sunday.
exp:
✔ 'next Sunday' भविष्य का समय बताता है → Simple Future (सामान्य भविष्य) (will + V1)। अतः 'will drive' सही है: "My brother will drive the car next Sunday."
📌 भविष्य सूचक: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon। 'will' के बाद हर कर्ता के साथ क्रिया का मूल रूप (V1) आता है (will go, will write)।
✖ has driven – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); निश्चित समय-सूचक (yesterday/next/every day) के साथ नहीं आता। had driven – Past Perfect (had + V3); भूतकाल की दो घटनाओं में पहले वाली के लिए। drove – Simple Past (V2); पूर्ण हो चुके भूतकालीन कार्य के लिए, 'next Sunday' के साथ नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'next Sunday' refers to future time → Simple Future (will + V1). So 'will drive' is correct: "My brother will drive the car next Sunday."
📌 Future markers: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon. 'Will' is followed by the base verb (V1) for every subject (will go, will write).
✖ has driven – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); not used with a definite time like yesterday/next/every day. had driven – Past Perfect (had + V3); used for the earlier of two past actions. drove – Simple Past (V2); used for completed past actions, not 'next Sunday'.

expe:
✔ The forms of 'run' are run – ran – run. The past (V2) form is 'ran', used in Simple Past.

q: Fill in the blank: They ___ not study science every Sunday.
exp:
✔ Simple Present का निषेधात्मक वाक्य: कर्ता + do/does + not + V1। 'They' के साथ 'do' आता है, इसलिए 'do not' + V1 'study': "They do not study science every Sunday."
📌 does/doesn't के बाद मुख्य क्रिया में -s/-es नहीं लगता: 'She does not play' ('plays' नहीं)। I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't)।
✖ are – 'be' क्रिया, V-ing (continuous) के साथ आती है; V1 के साथ do/does चाहिए। does – केवल third-person singular कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'They' के साथ नहीं। have – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं।
expe:
✔ Simple Present negative: subject + do/does + not + V1. 'They' takes 'do', so 'do not' + V1 'study': "They do not study science every Sunday."
📌 After does/doesn't the main verb loses -s/-es: 'She does not play' (not 'plays'). I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't).
✖ are – a 'be' verb used with V-ing (continuous); with V1 we need do/does. does – used only with third-person singular subjects, not with 'They'. have – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1.

q: Fill in the blank: The day before yesterday, the children ___ the windows.
exp:
✔ भूतकाल की दो घटनाएँ: जो पहले पूरी हुई उसमें Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) (had + V3), बाद वाली में Simple Past ('yesterday, the children ___ the windows')। अतः 'cleaned' सही है: "The day before yesterday, the children cleaned the windows."
📌 'before' → पहले वाली घटना had + V3 में; 'after' वाले उपवाक्य में had + V3 आता है: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' सभी कर्ताओं के साथ आता है।
✖ will clean – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। have cleaned – Present Perfect; भूत को वर्तमान से जोड़ता है, दूसरी भूतकालीन घटना से नहीं। clean – Simple Present; भूतकालीन घटनाओं वाले वाक्य में उपयुक्त नहीं।
expe:
✔ Two past actions: the one completed first takes Past Perfect (had + V3), the later one Simple Past ('yesterday, the children ___ the windows'). So 'cleaned' is correct: "The day before yesterday, the children cleaned the windows."
📌 'Before' → earlier action in had + V3; 'after' → had + V3 comes in the 'after' clause: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' is used with all subjects.
✖ will clean – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. have cleaned – Present Perfect; links the past with the present, not with another past action. clean – Simple Present; does not fit a sentence about past events.

q: Fill in the blank: There ___ a pen in the bag.
exp:

exp:

q: Fill in the blank: Our neighbour ___ the truck last night.

✔ Two past actions: the one completed first takes Past Perfect (had + V3), the later one Simple Past ('yesterday'). So 'made' is correct: "Lata made tea the day before yesterday."
📌 'Before' → earlier action in had + V3; 'after' → had + V3 comes in the 'after' clause: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' is used with all subjects.
✖ has made – Present Perfect; links the past with the present, not with another past action. makes – Simple Present; does not fit a sentence about past events. will make – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time.

📌 does/doesn't के बाद मुख्य क्रिया में -s/-es नहीं लगता: 'She does not play' ('plays' नहीं)। I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't)।
✖ is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं। has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं। do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Divya' के साथ नहीं।
expe:
✔ Simple Present negative: subject + does/do + not + V1. 'Divya' is third-person singular, so 'does not' + V1 'clean': "Divya does not clean the windows every evening."
📌 After does/doesn't the main verb loses -s/-es: 'She does not play' (not 'plays'). I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't).
✖ is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is. has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1. do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'Divya'.

q: Fill in the blank: Gopal ___ the answer sheets on Mondays.

✖ check – मूल रूप (V1) I/we/you/they या बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Gopal' के साथ नहीं। been checking – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए। checking – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता।
expe:

📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ check – base form (V1) is used with I/we/you/they or plural subjects, not with 'Gopal'. been checking – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it. checking – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were.

q: Fill in the blank: Sanjay ___ the shoes last night.
exp:
✔ 'last night' निश्चित भूतकाल का समय-सूचक है → Simple Past (सामान्य भूत) (कर्ता + V2)। 'polished' क्रिया का V2 रूप है: "Sanjay polished the shoes last night."
📌 भूतकाल सूचक: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2। इनके साथ Present Perfect (has/have + V3) गलत है। Simple Past में सभी कर्ताओं के साथ क्रिया का एक ही रूप आता है।
✖ will polish – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। polishes – Simple Present का रूप; आदत/वर्तमान तथ्य के लिए, भूतकाल के लिए नहीं। has polished – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'last night' जैसे निश्चित भूतकाल-सूचक के साथ प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ 'last night' is a definite past time marker → Simple Past (subject + V2). 'polished' is the V2 form: "Sanjay polished the shoes last night."
📌 Past markers: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2. With such words Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is wrong. In Simple Past the verb form is the same for all subjects.
✖ will polish – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. polishes – Simple Present form; used for habits/present facts, not past time. has polished – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); cannot be used with a definite past time like 'last night'.

q: Fill in the blank: My brother ___ dinner at the moment.
exp:
✔ 'at the moment' बताता है कि कार्य अभी चल रहा है → Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) (is/am/are + V-ing)। कर्ता 'My brother' के साथ 'is' आएगा, अतः 'is cooking' सही है: "My brother is cooking dinner at the moment."
📌 संकेत शब्द: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment। I → am; He/She/It/एकवचन → is; We/You/They/बहुवचन → are।
✖ are cooking – 'are' बहुवचन कर्ता/you के साथ आता है; 'My brother' के साथ 'is' चाहिए। cooks – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं। was cooking – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए।
expe:
✔ 'at the moment' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'My brother' takes 'is', so 'is cooking' is correct: "My brother is cooking dinner at the moment."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.
✖ are cooking – 'are' goes with plural subjects/you; 'My brother' needs 'is'. cooks – Simple Present; shows habit, not an action in progress now. was cooking – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past.

q: Fill in the blank: Ramesh ___ the wall next month.
exp:

✖ was painting – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। has painted – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); निश्चित समय-सूचक (yesterday/next/every day) के साथ नहीं आता। painted – Simple Past (V2); पूर्ण हो चुके भूतकालीन कार्य के लिए, 'next month' के साथ नहीं।

📌 Future markers: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon. 'Will' is followed by the base verb (V1) for every subject (will go, will write).
✖ was painting – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past. has painted – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); not used with a definite time like yesterday/next/every day. painted – Simple Past (V2); used for completed past actions, not 'next month'.

q: What is the past (V2) form of the verb 'speak'?

✖ speaked – ऐसा कोई रूप नहीं; 'speak' irregular है, इसमें -ed नहीं लगता। speaks – third-person singular का वर्तमान काल रूप। spoken – यह V3 (past participle) है, has/have/had के साथ आता है।
expe:
✔ The forms of 'speak' are speak – spoke – spoken. The past (V2) form is 'spoke', used in Simple Past.

q: Fill in the blank: There ___ a few cars in the market.
exp:
✔ 'There + be' वाक्यों में क्रिया बाद में आने वाली संज्ञा के अनुसार होती है। 'a few cars in the market' बहुवचन है, इसलिए 'are' आएगा: "There are a few cars in the market."
📌 There is + a/an/one + एकवचन संज्ञा (There is a pen); There are + बहुवचन संज्ञा / a few / some / many + बहुवचन (There are some shops)। अगणनीय संज्ञा के साथ: There is some milk।

expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'a few cars in the market' is plural, so 'are' is used: "There are a few cars in the market."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.
✖ has – shows possession; 'There ___' structure needs a form of 'be' (is/are). am – used only with the subject 'I'. is – used before a singular noun, but here the noun is plural.

q: Fill in the blank: ___ the students prepare a plan every morning?
exp:
✔ Simple Present का प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य: Do/Does + कर्ता + V1? 'the students' बहुवचन है, इसलिए 'Do' + V1 'prepare': "Do the students prepare a plan every morning?"
📌 Does वाले प्रश्न में मुख्य क्रिया V1 में रहती है: 'Does he play?' ('plays' नहीं)। Do → I/we/you/they/बहुवचन; Does → he/she/it/एकवचन संज्ञा।
✖ Are – 'be' क्रिया, V-ing (continuous) के साथ आती है; V1 के साथ do/does चाहिए। Does – केवल third-person singular कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'the students' के साथ नहीं। Have – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं।
expe:
✔ Simple Present question: Do/Does + subject + V1? 'the students' is plural, so 'Do' + V1 'prepare': "Do the students prepare a plan every morning?"
📌 In questions with Does, the main verb stays in V1: 'Does he play?' (not 'plays'). Do → I/we/you/they/plural; Does → he/she/it/singular noun.
✖ Are – a 'be' verb used with V-ing (continuous); with V1 we need do/does. Does – used only with third-person singular subjects, not with 'the students'. Have – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1.

q: Fill in the blank: My brother ___ the wall the day before yesterday.
exp:
✔ भूतकाल की दो घटनाएँ: जो पहले पूरी हुई उसमें Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) (had + V3), बाद वाली में Simple Past ('yesterday')। अतः 'painted' सही है: "My brother painted the wall the day before yesterday."
📌 'before' → पहले वाली घटना had + V3 में; 'after' वाले उपवाक्य में had + V3 आता है: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' सभी कर्ताओं के साथ आता है।
✖ paints – Simple Present; भूतकालीन घटनाओं वाले वाक्य में उपयुक्त नहीं। has painted – Present Perfect; भूत को वर्तमान से जोड़ता है, दूसरी भूतकालीन घटना से नहीं। will paint – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ।
expe:
✔ Two past actions: the one completed first takes Past Perfect (had + V3), the later one Simple Past ('yesterday'). So 'painted' is correct: "My brother painted the wall the day before yesterday."
📌 'Before' → earlier action in had + V3; 'after' → had + V3 comes in the 'after' clause: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' is used with all subjects.
✖ paints – Simple Present; does not fit a sentence about past events. has painted – Present Perfect; links the past with the present, not with another past action. will paint – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time.

q: Fill in the blank: She ___ not teach mathematics twice a week.
exp:

q: Fill in the blank: Rahul ___ the door twice a week.

q: Fill in the blank: Last year, Shalini ___ the books.
exp:
✔ 'last year' निश्चित भूतकाल का समय-सूचक है → Simple Past (सामान्य भूत) (कर्ता + V2)। 'arranged' क्रिया का V2 रूप है: "Last year, Shalini arranged the books."
📌 भूतकाल सूचक: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2। इनके साथ Present Perfect (has/have + V3) गलत है। Simple Past में सभी कर्ताओं के साथ क्रिया का एक ही रूप आता है।
✖ has arranged – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'last year' जैसे निश्चित भूतकाल-सूचक के साथ प्रयोग नहीं होता। arranges – Simple Present का रूप; आदत/वर्तमान तथ्य के लिए, भूतकाल के लिए नहीं। will arrange – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ।
expe:
✔ 'last year' is a definite past time marker → Simple Past (subject + V2). 'arranged' is the V2 form: "Last year, Shalini arranged the books."
📌 Past markers: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2. With such words Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is wrong. In Simple Past the verb form is the same for all subjects.
✖ has arranged – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); cannot be used with a definite past time like 'last year'. arranges – Simple Present form; used for habits/present facts, not past time. will arrange – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time.

q: Fill in the blank: Look! We ___ trees.
exp:
✔ 'Look!' बताता है कि कार्य अभी चल रहा है → Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) (is/am/are + V-ing)। कर्ता 'We' के साथ 'are' आएगा, अतः 'are planting' सही है: "Look! We are planting trees."
📌 संकेत शब्द: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment। I → am; He/She/It/एकवचन → is; We/You/They/बहुवचन → are।
✖ plant – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं। is planting – 'is' एकवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है; 'We' के साथ 'are' चाहिए। were planting – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए।
expe:
✔ 'Look!' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'We' takes 'are', so 'are planting' is correct: "Look! We are planting trees."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.
✖ plant – Simple Present; shows habit, not an action in progress now. is planting – 'is' goes with a singular subject; 'We' needs 'are'. were planting – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past.

q: Fill in the blank: They ___ bread the day after tomorrow.
exp:
✔ 'the day after tomorrow' भविष्य का समय बताता है → Simple Future (सामान्य भविष्य) (will + V1)। अतः 'will bake' सही है: "They will bake bread the day after tomorrow."
📌 भविष्य सूचक: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon। 'will' के बाद हर कर्ता के साथ क्रिया का मूल रूप (V1) आता है (will go, will write)।
✖ have baked – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); निश्चित समय-सूचक (yesterday/next/every day) के साथ नहीं आता। baked – Simple Past (V2); पूर्ण हो चुके भूतकालीन कार्य के लिए, 'the day after tomorrow' के साथ नहीं। were baking – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए।
expe:
✔ 'the day after tomorrow' refers to future time → Simple Future (will + V1). So 'will bake' is correct: "They will bake bread the day after tomorrow."
📌 Future markers: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon. 'Will' is followed by the base verb (V1) for every subject (will go, will write).
✖ have baked – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); not used with a definite time like yesterday/next/every day. baked – Simple Past (V2); used for completed past actions, not 'the day after tomorrow'. were baking – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past.

q: What is the past participle (V3) form of the verb 'keep'?
exp:
✔ 'keep' के रूप हैं: keep – kept – kept। इसका past participle (V3) रूप 'kept' है, जो has/have/had और passive voice में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 यह irregular verb है – इसी तरह के रूप: sweep – swept – swept, weep – wept – wept, sleep – slept – slept।
✖ keeping – present participle (V-ing), continuous tense में प्रयोग होता है। keeps – third-person singular का वर्तमान काल रूप। keeped – ऐसा कोई रूप नहीं; 'keep' irregular है, इसमें -ed नहीं लगता।
expe:
✔ The forms of 'keep' are keep – kept – kept. The past participle (V3) is 'kept', used with has/have/had and in the passive voice.
📌 Irregular verb – similar pattern: sweep – swept – swept, weep – wept – wept, sleep – slept – slept.
✖ keeping – present participle (V-ing), used in continuous tenses. keeps – present tense form for third-person singular. keeped – no such word; 'keep' is irregular and does not take -ed.

q: Fill in the blank: There ___ some buses at the bus stand.
exp:
✔ 'There + be' वाक्यों में क्रिया बाद में आने वाली संज्ञा के अनुसार होती है। 'some buses at the bus stand' बहुवचन है, इसलिए 'are' आएगा: "There are some buses at the bus stand."
📌 There is + a/an/one + एकवचन संज्ञा (There is a pen); There are + बहुवचन संज्ञा / a few / some / many + बहुवचन (There are some shops)। अगणनीय संज्ञा के साथ: There is some milk।
✖ has – अधिकार/स्वामित्व बताता है; 'There ___' संरचना में 'be' का रूप (is/are) चाहिए। am – केवल कर्ता 'I' के साथ आता है। is – एकवचन संज्ञा से पहले आता है, जबकि यहाँ संज्ञा बहुवचन है।
expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'some buses at the bus stand' is plural, so 'are' is used: "There are some buses at the bus stand."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.
✖ has – shows possession; 'There ___' structure needs a form of 'be' (is/are). am – used only with the subject 'I'. is – used before a singular noun, but here the noun is plural.

q: Fill in the blank: He ___ not make a kite every day.
exp:
✔ Simple Present का निषेधात्मक वाक्य: कर्ता + does/do + not + V1। 'He' third-person singular है, इसलिए 'does not' + V1 'make': "He does not make a kite every day."
📌 does/doesn't के बाद मुख्य क्रिया में -s/-es नहीं लगता: 'She does not play' ('plays' नहीं)। I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't)।
✖ is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं। has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं। do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'He' के साथ नहीं।
expe:
✔ Simple Present negative: subject + does/do + not + V1. 'He' is third-person singular, so 'does not' + V1 'make': "He does not make a kite every day."
📌 After does/doesn't the main verb loses -s/-es: 'She does not play' (not 'plays'). I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't).
✖ is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is. has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1. do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'He'.

q: Fill in the blank: Usha ___ chess twice a week.
exp:
✔ 'twice a week' आदत/नियमित कार्य बताता है → Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान)। कर्ता 'Usha' third-person singular है, इसलिए V1 + s/es = 'plays': "Usha plays chess twice a week."
📌 नियम: He/She/It/एकवचन संज्ञा + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/बहुवचन + V1। -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o वाली क्रियाओं में -es लगता है (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries)।
✖ playing – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता। play – मूल रूप (V1) I/we/you/they या बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Usha' के साथ नहीं। been playing – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'twice a week' shows a habitual/repeated action → Simple Present. The subject 'Usha' is third-person singular, so V1 + s/es = 'plays': "Usha plays chess twice a week."
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ playing – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were. play – base form (V1) is used with I/we/you/they or plural subjects, not with 'Usha'. been playing – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it.

q: Fill in the blank: ___ our neighbour read a novel daily?
exp:
✔ Simple Present का प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य: Does/Do + कर्ता + V1? 'our neighbour' third-person singular है, इसलिए 'Does' + V1 'read': "Does our neighbour read a novel daily?"
📌 Does वाले प्रश्न में मुख्य क्रिया V1 में रहती है: 'Does he play?' ('plays' नहीं)। Do → I/we/you/they/बहुवचन; Does → he/she/it/एकवचन संज्ञा।
✖ Has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं। Do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'our neighbour' के साथ नहीं। Is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं।
expe:
✔ Simple Present question: Does/Do + subject + V1? 'our neighbour' is third-person singular, so 'Does' + V1 'read': "Does our neighbour read a novel daily?"
📌 In questions with Does, the main verb stays in V1: 'Does he play?' (not 'plays'). Do → I/we/you/they/plural; Does → he/she/it/singular noun.
✖ Has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1. Do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'our neighbour'. Is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is.

q: Fill in the blank: Look! The teacher ___ new roads.
exp:
✔ 'Look!' बताता है कि कार्य अभी चल रहा है → Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) (is/am/are + V-ing)। कर्ता 'The teacher' के साथ 'is' आएगा, अतः 'is building' सही है: "Look! The teacher is building new roads."
📌 संकेत शब्द: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment। I → am; He/She/It/एकवचन → is; We/You/They/बहुवचन → are।
✖ are building – 'are' बहुवचन कर्ता/you के साथ आता है; 'The teacher' के साथ 'is' चाहिए। builds – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं। was building – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए।
expe:
✔ 'Look!' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'The teacher' takes 'is', so 'is building' is correct: "Look! The teacher is building new roads."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.
✖ are building – 'are' goes with plural subjects/you; 'The teacher' needs 'is'. builds – Simple Present; shows habit, not an action in progress now. was building – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past.

q: Fill in the blank: Komal ___ a kite next Sunday.
exp:
✔ 'next Sunday' भविष्य का समय बताता है → Simple Future (सामान्य भविष्य) (will + V1)। अतः 'will fly' सही है: "Komal will fly a kite next Sunday."
📌 भविष्य सूचक: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon। 'will' के बाद हर कर्ता के साथ क्रिया का मूल रूप (V1) आता है (will go, will write)।
✖ has flown – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); निश्चित समय-सूचक (yesterday/next/every day) के साथ नहीं आता। flew – Simple Past (V2); पूर्ण हो चुके भूतकालीन कार्य के लिए, 'next Sunday' के साथ नहीं। had flown – Past Perfect (had + V3); भूतकाल की दो घटनाओं में पहले वाली के लिए।
expe:
✔ 'next Sunday' refers to future time → Simple Future (will + V1). So 'will fly' is correct: "Komal will fly a kite next Sunday."
📌 Future markers: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon. 'Will' is followed by the base verb (V1) for every subject (will go, will write).
✖ has flown – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); not used with a definite time like yesterday/next/every day. flew – Simple Past (V2); used for completed past actions, not 'next Sunday'. had flown – Past Perfect (had + V3); used for the earlier of two past actions.

q: What is the past (V2) form of the verb 'know'?
exp:
✔ 'know' के रूप हैं: know – knew – known। इसका past (V2) रूप 'knew' है, जो Simple Past में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 यह irregular verb है – इसी तरह के रूप: grow – grew – grown, throw – threw – thrown, blow – blew – blown।
✖ knowed – ऐसा कोई रूप नहीं; 'know' irregular है, इसमें -ed नहीं लगता। knows – third-person singular का वर्तमान काल रूप। known – यह V3 (past participle) है, has/have/had के साथ आता है।
expe:
✔ The forms of 'know' are know – knew – known. The past (V2) form is 'knew', used in Simple Past.
📌 Irregular verb – similar pattern: grow – grew – grown, throw – threw – thrown, blow – blew – blown.
✖ knowed – no such word; 'know' is irregular and does not take -ed. knows – present tense form for third-person singular. known – this is V3 (past participle), used with has/have/had.

q: Fill in the blank: There ___ a mirror on the wall.
exp:
✔ 'There + be' वाक्यों में क्रिया बाद में आने वाली संज्ञा के अनुसार होती है। 'a mirror on the wall' एकवचन है, इसलिए 'is' आएगा: "There is a mirror on the wall."
📌 There is + a/an/one + एकवचन संज्ञा (There is a pen); There are + बहुवचन संज्ञा / a few / some / many + बहुवचन (There are some shops)। अगणनीय संज्ञा के साथ: There is some milk।
✖ have – अधिकार/स्वामित्व बताता है; 'There ___' संरचना में 'be' का रूप (is/are) चाहिए। are – बहुवचन संज्ञा से पहले आता है, जबकि यहाँ संज्ञा एकवचन है। am – केवल कर्ता 'I' के साथ आता है।
expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'a mirror on the wall' is singular, so 'is' is used: "There is a mirror on the wall."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.
✖ have – shows possession; 'There ___' structure needs a form of 'be' (is/are). are – used before a plural noun, but here the noun is singular. am – used only with the subject 'I'.

q: Fill in the blank: Neha ___ not speak English twice a week.
exp:
✔ Simple Present का निषेधात्मक वाक्य: कर्ता + does/do + not + V1। 'Neha' third-person singular है, इसलिए 'does not' + V1 'speak': "Neha does not speak English twice a week."
📌 does/doesn't के बाद मुख्य क्रिया में -s/-es नहीं लगता: 'She does not play' ('plays' नहीं)। I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't)।
✖ is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं। has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं। do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Neha' के साथ नहीं।
expe:
✔ Simple Present negative: subject + does/do + not + V1. 'Neha' is third-person singular, so 'does not' + V1 'speak': "Neha does not speak English twice a week."
📌 After does/doesn't the main verb loses -s/-es: 'She does not play' (not 'plays'). I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't).
✖ is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is. has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1. do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'Neha'.

q: Fill in the blank: The student ___ the dog regularly.
exp:
✔ 'regularly' आदत/नियमित कार्य बताता है → Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान)। कर्ता 'The student' third-person singular है, इसलिए V1 + s/es = 'feeds': "The student feeds the dog regularly."
📌 नियम: He/She/It/एकवचन संज्ञा + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/बहुवचन + V1। -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o वाली क्रियाओं में -es लगता है (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries)।
✖ feeding – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता। feed – मूल रूप (V1) I/we/you/they या बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'The student' के साथ नहीं। been feeding – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'regularly' shows a habitual/repeated action → Simple Present. The subject 'The student' is third-person singular, so V1 + s/es = 'feeds': "The student feeds the dog regularly."
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ feeding – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were. feed – base form (V1) is used with I/we/you/they or plural subjects, not with 'The student'. been feeding – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it.

q: Fill in the blank: My sister ___ some apples last night.
exp:
✔ 'last night' निश्चित भूतकाल का समय-सूचक है → Simple Past (सामान्य भूत) (कर्ता + V2)। 'bought' क्रिया का V2 रूप है: "My sister bought some apples last night."
📌 भूतकाल सूचक: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2। इनके साथ Present Perfect (has/have + V3) गलत है। Simple Past में सभी कर्ताओं के साथ क्रिया का एक ही रूप आता है।
✖ buys – Simple Present का रूप; आदत/वर्तमान तथ्य के लिए, भूतकाल के लिए नहीं। will buy – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। has bought – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'last night' जैसे निश्चित भूतकाल-सूचक के साथ प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ 'last night' is a definite past time marker → Simple Past (subject + V2). 'bought' is the V2 form: "My sister bought some apples last night."
📌 Past markers: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2. With such words Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is wrong. In Simple Past the verb form is the same for all subjects.
✖ buys – Simple Present form; used for habits/present facts, not past time. will buy – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. has bought – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); cannot be used with a definite past time like 'last night'.

q: Fill in the blank: The students ___ cricket at this moment.
exp:
✔ 'at this moment' बताता है कि कार्य अभी चल रहा है → Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) (is/am/are + V-ing)। कर्ता 'The students' के साथ 'are' आएगा, अतः 'are playing' सही है: "The students are playing cricket at this moment."
📌 संकेत शब्द: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment। I → am; He/She/It/एकवचन → is; We/You/They/बहुवचन → are।
✖ play – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं। were playing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। is playing – 'is' एकवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है; 'The students' के साथ 'are' चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'at this moment' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'The students' takes 'are', so 'are playing' is correct: "The students are playing cricket at this moment."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.
✖ play – Simple Present; shows habit, not an action in progress now. were playing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past. is playing – 'is' goes with a singular subject; 'The students' needs 'are'.

q: What is the past participle (V3) form of the verb 'buy'?
exp:
✔ 'buy' के रूप हैं: buy – bought – bought। इसका past participle (V3) रूप 'bought' है, जो has/have/had और passive voice में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 यह irregular verb है – इसी तरह के रूप: bring – brought – brought, think – thought – thought, fight – fought – fought।
✖ buying – present participle (V-ing), continuous tense में प्रयोग होता है। buyed – ऐसा कोई रूप नहीं; 'buy' irregular है, इसमें -ed नहीं लगता। buys – third-person singular का वर्तमान काल रूप।
expe:
✔ The forms of 'buy' are buy – bought – bought. The past participle (V3) is 'bought', used with has/have/had and in the passive voice.
📌 Irregular verb – similar pattern: bring – brought – brought, think – thought – thought, fight – fought – fought.
✖ buying – present participle (V-ing), used in continuous tenses. buyed – no such word; 'buy' is irregular and does not take -ed. buys – present tense form for third-person singular.

q: Fill in the blank: ___ Arjun speak English every day?
exp:
✔ Simple Present का प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य: Does/Do + कर्ता + V1? 'Arjun' third-person singular है, इसलिए 'Does' + V1 'speak': "Does Arjun speak English every day?"
📌 Does वाले प्रश्न में मुख्य क्रिया V1 में रहती है: 'Does he play?' ('plays' नहीं)। Do → I/we/you/they/बहुवचन; Does → he/she/it/एकवचन संज्ञा।
✖ Do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Arjun' के साथ नहीं। Is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं। Has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं।
expe:
✔ Simple Present question: Does/Do + subject + V1? 'Arjun' is third-person singular, so 'Does' + V1 'speak': "Does Arjun speak English every day?"
📌 In questions with Does, the main verb stays in V1: 'Does he play?' (not 'plays'). Do → I/we/you/they/plural; Does → he/she/it/singular noun.
✖ Do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'Arjun'. Is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is. Has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1.

q: Fill in the blank: Arjun ___ the match the day before yesterday.
exp:
✔ भूतकाल की दो घटनाएँ: जो पहले पूरी हुई उसमें Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) (had + V3), बाद वाली में Simple Past ('yesterday')। अतः 'watched' सही है: "Arjun watched the match the day before yesterday."
📌 'before' → पहले वाली घटना had + V3 में; 'after' वाले उपवाक्य में had + V3 आता है: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' सभी कर्ताओं के साथ आता है।
✖ watches – Simple Present; भूतकालीन घटनाओं वाले वाक्य में उपयुक्त नहीं। will watch – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। has watched – Present Perfect; भूत को वर्तमान से जोड़ता है, दूसरी भूतकालीन घटना से नहीं।
expe:
✔ Two past actions: the one completed first takes Past Perfect (had + V3), the later one Simple Past ('yesterday'). So 'watched' is correct: "Arjun watched the match the day before yesterday."
📌 'Before' → earlier action in had + V3; 'after' → had + V3 comes in the 'after' clause: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' is used with all subjects.
✖ watches – Simple Present; does not fit a sentence about past events. will watch – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. has watched – Present Perfect; links the past with the present, not with another past action.

q: Fill in the blank: Look! Sanjay ___ these sums.

✖ was solving – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। are solving – 'are' बहुवचन कर्ता/you के साथ आता है; 'Sanjay' के साथ 'is' चाहिए। solves – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'Look!' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'Sanjay' takes 'is', so 'is solving' is correct: "Look! Sanjay is solving these sums."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.

q: Fill in the blank: The workers ___ the parcel next week.

q: Fill in the blank: There ___ a few cars near the gate.

expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'a few cars near the gate' is plural, so 'are' is used: "There are a few cars near the gate."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.

q: Fill in the blank: ___ Pooja check the accounts on Mondays?
exp:
✔ Simple Present का प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य: Does/Do + कर्ता + V1? 'Pooja' third-person singular है, इसलिए 'Does' + V1 'check': "Does Pooja check the accounts on Mondays?"
📌 Does वाले प्रश्न में मुख्य क्रिया V1 में रहती है: 'Does he play?' ('plays' नहीं)। Do → I/we/you/they/बहुवचन; Does → he/she/it/एकवचन संज्ञा।
✖ Do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Pooja' के साथ नहीं। Is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं। Has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं।
expe:
✔ Simple Present question: Does/Do + subject + V1? 'Pooja' is third-person singular, so 'Does' + V1 'check': "Does Pooja check the accounts on Mondays?"
📌 In questions with Does, the main verb stays in V1: 'Does he play?' (not 'plays'). Do → I/we/you/they/plural; Does → he/she/it/singular noun.
✖ Do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'Pooja'. Is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is. Has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1.

✖ been opening – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए। opening – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता। open – मूल रूप (V1) I/we/you/they या बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'My brother' के साथ नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'regularly' shows a habitual/repeated action → Simple Present. The subject 'My brother' is third-person singular, so V1 + s/es = 'opens': "My brother opens the door regularly."
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ been opening – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it. opening – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were. open – base form (V1) is used with I/we/you/they or plural subjects, not with 'My brother'.

q: Fill in the blank: Last year, Meena ___ photographs.

📌 Past markers: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2. With such words Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is wrong. In Simple Past the verb form is the same for all subjects.

q: Fill in the blank: Ajay ___ in this office since last year.
exp:
✔ 'since last year' बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब तक जारी है → Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) (has/have + V3)। अतः 'has worked' सही है: "Ajay has worked in this office since last year."
📌 'Since' + समय-बिंदु (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + समयावधि (for two years)। चल रहे कार्य के लिए Present Perfect Continuous भी आता है: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ works – Simple Present; 'since' के साथ भूत से अब तक की अवधि नहीं बता सकता। worked – Simple Past; समाप्त कार्य बताता है, अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं। is working – Present Continuous; 'since' के साथ अब तक की अवधि के लिए प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ 'since last year' shows an action that began in the past and still continues → Present Perfect (has/have + V3). So 'has worked' is correct: "Ajay has worked in this office since last year."
📌 'Since' + point of time (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + period of time (for two years). For a continuing activity, Present Perfect Continuous is also used: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ works – Simple Present; cannot express a period from the past up to now with 'since'. worked – Simple Past; shows a finished action, not one continuing till now. is working – Present Continuous; not used with 'since' for a period up to now.

q: Fill in the blank: While Lata ___ the kitchen, a guest arrived.
exp:
✔ 'While' भूतकाल में चल रहे लंबे कार्य को बताता है, जिसे Simple Past की छोटी घटना ('a guest arrived') ने बीच में रोका → Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) (was/were + V-ing): "While Lata was cleaning the kitchen, a guest arrived."
📌 नियम: लंबा कार्य → Past Continuous; बीच में आने वाली घटना → Simple Past। I/He/She/It/एकवचन → was; We/You/They/बहुवचन → were। उदाहरण: 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ has cleaned – Present Perfect; भूतकालीन उपवाक्य से मेल नहीं खाता। will clean – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। is cleaning – Present Continuous; दूसरा उपवाक्य भूतकाल में है, अतः भूतकाल चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'While' marks a longer action in progress in the past, interrupted by a shorter Simple Past action ('a guest arrived') → Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing): "While Lata was cleaning the kitchen, a guest arrived."
📌 Pattern: longer action → Past Continuous; interrupting action → Simple Past. I/He/She/It/singular → was; We/You/They/plural → were. E.g. 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ has cleaned – Present Perfect; does not match a past-time clause. will clean – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. is cleaning – Present Continuous; the other clause is in the past, so tense must be past.

q: Fill in the blank: Pooja ___ the car before the teacher came.
exp:
✔ भूतकाल की दो घटनाएँ: जो पहले पूरी हुई उसमें Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) (had + V3), बाद वाली में Simple Past ('the teacher came')। अतः 'had driven' सही है: "Pooja had driven the car before the teacher came."
📌 'before' → पहले वाली घटना had + V3 में; 'after' वाले उपवाक्य में had + V3 आता है: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' सभी कर्ताओं के साथ आता है।
✖ has driven – Present Perfect; भूत को वर्तमान से जोड़ता है, दूसरी भूतकालीन घटना से नहीं। drives – Simple Present; भूतकालीन घटनाओं वाले वाक्य में उपयुक्त नहीं। will drive – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ।
expe:
✔ Two past actions: the one completed first takes Past Perfect (had + V3), the later one Simple Past ('the teacher came'). So 'had driven' is correct: "Pooja had driven the car before the teacher came."
📌 'Before' → earlier action in had + V3; 'after' → had + V3 comes in the 'after' clause: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' is used with all subjects.
✖ has driven – Present Perfect; links the past with the present, not with another past action. drives – Simple Present; does not fit a sentence about past events. will drive – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time.

q: Fill in the blank: Kavita gave up ___ chess.
exp:
✔ क्रिया 'give up' के बाद हमेशा gerund (V-ing) आता है, infinitive (to + V1) नहीं। अतः 'playing' सही है: "Kavita gave up playing chess."
📌 Gerund (V-ing) लेने वाली क्रियाएँ: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep। उदाहरण: 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ played – past/past participle रूप; 'gave up' के कर्म के रूप में प्रयोग नहीं होता। play – मूल रूप (V1); 'gave up' के तुरंत बाद नहीं आ सकता। to play – to-infinitive; 'give up' के बाद infinitive नहीं आता।
expe:
✔ The verb 'give up' is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), not by an infinitive. So 'playing' is correct: "Kavita gave up playing chess."
📌 Verbs + gerund: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep. E.g. 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ played – past/past participle form; not used as the object of 'gave up'. play – base form (V1); cannot follow 'gave up' directly. to play – to-infinitive; 'give up' does not take an infinitive.

q: Fill in the blank: Harish should ___ the fees.
exp:
✔ modal verb 'should' के बाद बिना 'to' का मूल रूप (bare infinitive, V1) आता है। अतः 'collect' सही है: "Harish should collect the fees."
📌 Bare infinitive इनके बाद आता है: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, तथा make/let/see/hear + object। उदाहरण: 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ to collect – to-infinitive; 'should' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता। collecting – -ing रूप; 'should' के बाद नहीं आता। collects – s-रूप; 'should' के बाद क्रिया में -s नहीं लगता।
expe:
✔ After the modal verb 'should', the bare infinitive (V1 without 'to') is used. So 'collect' is correct: "Harish should collect the fees."
📌 Bare infinitive follows: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, and make/let/see/hear + object. E.g. 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ to collect – to-infinitive; 'should' is not followed by 'to'. collecting – -ing form; cannot follow 'should'. collects – s-form; after 'should' the verb never takes -s.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: She has swept the floor.
exp:
✔ "She has swept the floor." में संरचना has/have + V3 – हाल ही में पूरा हुआ कार्य जिसका प्रभाव वर्तमान में है है। अतः यह Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) है।
📌 Present Perfect के साथ just, already, yet, ever, never, since/for आते हैं, पर निश्चित भूतकाल (yesterday, last year) नहीं।
✖ Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) – संरचना had + V3। Present Perfect Continuous (पूर्ण-निरंतर वर्तमान) – संरचना has/have been + V-ing। Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) – संरचना is/am/are + V-ing।
expe:
✔ "She has swept the floor." follows the structure has/have + V3 – an action just completed whose result is relevant now. Hence it is Present Perfect.
📌 Present Perfect takes words like just, already, yet, ever, never, since/for, but not definite past time (yesterday, last year).
✖ Past Perfect – structure had + V3. Present Perfect Continuous – structure has/have been + V-ing. Present Continuous – structure is/am/are + V-ing.

q: Which of the following verb forms (V1 – V2 – V3) is correct?
exp:
✔ 'sink – sank – sunk' सही V1 – V2 – V3 क्रम है: V2 'sank' Simple Past में और V3 'sunk' has/have/had तथा passive voice में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 इसी तरह के irregular रूप: ring – rang – rung, drink – drank – drunk। Irregular verbs में V2/V3 -ed लगाकर नहीं बनते।
✖ go – went – goed – 'goed' गलत है; सही: go – went – gone। undertake – undertook – undertaked – 'undertaked' गलत है; सही: undertake – undertook – undertaken। withdraw – withdrew – withdrawed – 'withdrawed' गलत है; सही: withdraw – withdrew – withdrawn।
expe:
✔ 'sink – sank – sunk' is the correct V1 – V2 – V3 sequence: V2 'sank' is used in Simple Past and V3 'sunk' with has/have/had and in the passive voice.
📌 Similar irregular pattern: ring – rang – rung, drink – drank – drunk. Irregular verbs never form V2/V3 with -ed.
✖ go – went – goed – 'goed' is wrong; correct: go – went – gone. undertake – undertook – undertaked – 'undertaked' is wrong; correct: undertake – undertook – undertaken. withdraw – withdrew – withdrawed – 'withdrawed' is wrong; correct: withdraw – withdrew – withdrawn.

q: Fill in the blank: Every boy ___ given a book.
exp:
✔ 'Every' + एकवचन संज्ञा के साथ एकवचन क्रिया आती है। Past passive: was + V3 → "Every boy was given a book."
📌 Each, every, either, neither, everyone, everybody के साथ एकवचन क्रिया: 'Every student has a book.' / 'Each of them is ready.'
✖ have – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। were – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। are – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है।
expe:
✔ 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb. Past passive: was + V3 → "Every boy was given a book."
📌 Each, every, either, neither, everyone, everybody take a singular verb: 'Every student has a book.' / 'Each of them is ready.'
✖ have – plural verb; the subject here is singular. were – plural verb; the subject here is singular. are – plural verb; the subject here is singular.

q: Fill in the blank: My sister ___ in this school since March.
exp:
✔ 'since March' बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब तक जारी है → Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) (has/have + V3)। अतः 'has taught' सही है: "My sister has taught in this school since March."
📌 'Since' + समय-बिंदु (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + समयावधि (for two years)। चल रहे कार्य के लिए Present Perfect Continuous भी आता है: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ teaches – Simple Present; 'since' के साथ भूत से अब तक की अवधि नहीं बता सकता। is teaching – Present Continuous; 'since' के साथ अब तक की अवधि के लिए प्रयोग नहीं होता। taught – Simple Past; समाप्त कार्य बताता है, अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'since March' shows an action that began in the past and still continues → Present Perfect (has/have + V3). So 'has taught' is correct: "My sister has taught in this school since March."
📌 'Since' + point of time (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + period of time (for two years). For a continuing activity, Present Perfect Continuous is also used: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ teaches – Simple Present; cannot express a period from the past up to now with 'since'. is teaching – Present Continuous; not used with 'since' for a period up to now. taught – Simple Past; shows a finished action, not one continuing till now.

q: Fill in the blank: While Naveen ___ the windows, the power failed.
exp:
✔ 'While' भूतकाल में चल रहे लंबे कार्य को बताता है, जिसे Simple Past की छोटी घटना ('the power failed') ने बीच में रोका → Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) (was/were + V-ing): "While Naveen was opening the windows, the power failed."
📌 नियम: लंबा कार्य → Past Continuous; बीच में आने वाली घटना → Simple Past। I/He/She/It/एकवचन → was; We/You/They/बहुवचन → were। उदाहरण: 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ will open – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। has opened – Present Perfect; भूतकालीन उपवाक्य से मेल नहीं खाता। is opening – Present Continuous; दूसरा उपवाक्य भूतकाल में है, अतः भूतकाल चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'While' marks a longer action in progress in the past, interrupted by a shorter Simple Past action ('the power failed') → Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing): "While Naveen was opening the windows, the power failed."
📌 Pattern: longer action → Past Continuous; interrupting action → Simple Past. I/He/She/It/singular → was; We/You/They/plural → were. E.g. 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ will open – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. has opened – Present Perfect; does not match a past-time clause. is opening – Present Continuous; the other clause is in the past, so tense must be past.

exp:

✖ has spoken – Present Perfect; भूत को वर्तमान से जोड़ता है, दूसरी भूतकालीन घटना से नहीं। speaks – Simple Present; भूतकालीन घटनाओं वाले वाक्य में उपयुक्त नहीं। will speak – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ।
