q: Fill in the blank: Geeta promised ___ the poor.
exp:
✔ क्रिया 'promise' के बाद to-infinitive (to + V1) आता है। अतः 'to help' सही है: "Geeta promised to help the poor."
📌 to-infinitive लेने वाली क्रियाएँ: promise, learn, afford, decide, hope, want, agree, refuse, plan, wish, offer। उदाहरण: 'She decided to leave.' / 'They agreed to help.'
✖ help – बिना 'to' का मूल रूप; 'promise' के बाद 'to' चाहिए। to helping – यहाँ 'to' + V-ing गलत है; infinitive का रूप to + V1 होता है। helping – gerund; 'promise' के बाद gerund नहीं आता।
expe:
✔ The verb 'promise' is followed by a to-infinitive (to + V1). So 'to help' is correct: "Geeta promised to help the poor."
📌 Verbs + to-infinitive: promise, learn, afford, decide, hope, want, agree, refuse, plan, wish, offer. E.g. 'She decided to leave.' / 'They agreed to help.'
✖ help – bare infinitive (V1 without 'to'); 'promise' needs 'to'. to helping – 'to' + V-ing is wrong here; an infinitive is to + V1. helping – gerund; 'promise' does not take a gerund.

q: Fill in the blank: Meena had better ___ dinner.
exp:
✔ 'had better' के बाद बिना 'to' का मूल रूप (bare infinitive, V1) आता है। अतः 'cook' सही है: "Meena had better cook dinner."
📌 Bare infinitive इनके बाद आता है: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, तथा make/let/see/hear + object। उदाहरण: 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ cooking – -ing रूप; 'had better' के बाद नहीं आता। to cook – to-infinitive; 'had better' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता। cooked – past/past participle रूप; 'had better' के बाद V1 चाहिए।
expe:
✔ After 'had better', the bare infinitive (V1 without 'to') is used. So 'cook' is correct: "Meena had better cook dinner."
📌 Bare infinitive follows: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, and make/let/see/hear + object. E.g. 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ cooking – -ing form; cannot follow 'had better'. to cook – to-infinitive; 'had better' is not followed by 'to'. cooked – past/past participle form; 'had better' needs V1.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: My father is writing an essay.
exp:
✔ "My father is writing an essay." में संरचना is/am/are + V-ing – वर्तमान में चल रहा कार्य है। अतः यह Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) है।
📌 संकेत शब्द: now, at present, at the moment, Look!, Listen!। State verbs (know, like, believe) सामान्यतः continuous रूप में नहीं आते।
✖ Present Perfect Continuous (पूर्ण-निरंतर वर्तमान) – संरचना has/have been + V-ing। Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान) – संरचना V1 / V1+s/es। Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) – संरचना was/were + V-ing।
expe:
✔ "My father is writing an essay." follows the structure is/am/are + V-ing – an action going on at present. Hence it is Present Continuous.
📌 Signal words: now, at present, at the moment, Look!, Listen!. State verbs (know, like, believe) are usually not used in continuous form.
✖ Present Perfect Continuous – structure has/have been + V-ing. Simple Present – structure V1 / V1+s/es. Past Continuous – structure was/were + V-ing.

q: Which of the following verb forms (V1 – V2 – V3) is correct?
exp:
✔ 'know – knew – known' सही V1 – V2 – V3 क्रम है: V2 'knew' Simple Past में और V3 'known' has/have/had तथा passive voice में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 इसी तरह के irregular रूप: grow – grew – grown, throw – threw – thrown, blow – blew – blown। Irregular verbs में V2/V3 -ed लगाकर नहीं बनते।
✖ freeze – frozen – froze – V2 और V3 उलटे हैं; सही: freeze – froze – frozen। forgive – forgiven – forgave – V2 और V3 उलटे हैं; सही: forgive – forgave – forgiven। do – done – did – V2 और V3 उलटे हैं; सही: do – did – done।
expe:
✔ 'know – knew – known' is the correct V1 – V2 – V3 sequence: V2 'knew' is used in Simple Past and V3 'known' with has/have/had and in the passive voice.
📌 Similar irregular pattern: grow – grew – grown, throw – threw – thrown, blow – blew – blown. Irregular verbs never form V2/V3 with -ed.
✖ freeze – frozen – froze – V2 and V3 are swapped; correct: freeze – froze – frozen. forgive – forgiven – forgave – V2 and V3 are swapped; correct: forgive – forgave – forgiven. do – done – did – V2 and V3 are swapped; correct: do – did – done.

q: Fill in the blank: One of the students ___ absent today.
exp:
✔ 'One of the + बहुवचन संज्ञा' में कर्ता 'One' (एकवचन) है, इसलिए एकवचन क्रिया 'is' आएगी: "One of the students is absent today."
📌 'One of' के बाद संज्ञा बहुवचन पर क्रिया एकवचन होती है: 'One of my friends is a doctor.'
✖ are – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। were – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। have – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है।
expe:
✔ In 'One of the + plural noun', the subject is 'One' (singular), so the singular verb 'is' is used: "One of the students is absent today."
📌 'One of' is always followed by a plural noun but a singular verb: 'One of my friends is a doctor.'
✖ are – plural verb; the subject here is singular. were – plural verb; the subject here is singular. have – plural verb; the subject here is singular.

q: Fill in the blank: The players ___ in this office since 2012.
exp:
✔ 'since 2012' बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब तक जारी है → Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) (has/have + V3)। अतः 'have worked' सही है: "The players have worked in this office since 2012."
📌 'Since' + समय-बिंदु (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + समयावधि (for two years)। चल रहे कार्य के लिए Present Perfect Continuous भी आता है: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ worked – Simple Past; समाप्त कार्य बताता है, अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं। are working – Present Continuous; 'since' के साथ अब तक की अवधि के लिए प्रयोग नहीं होता। work – Simple Present; 'since' के साथ भूत से अब तक की अवधि नहीं बता सकता।
expe:
✔ 'since 2012' shows an action that began in the past and still continues → Present Perfect (has/have + V3). So 'have worked' is correct: "The players have worked in this office since 2012."
📌 'Since' + point of time (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + period of time (for two years). For a continuing activity, Present Perfect Continuous is also used: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ worked – Simple Past; shows a finished action, not one continuing till now. are working – Present Continuous; not used with 'since' for a period up to now. work – Simple Present; cannot express a period from the past up to now with 'since'.

q: Fill in the blank: While Kavita ___ fresh milk, a guest arrived.
exp:
✔ 'While' भूतकाल में चल रहे लंबे कार्य को बताता है, जिसे Simple Past की छोटी घटना ('a guest arrived') ने बीच में रोका → Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) (was/were + V-ing): "While Kavita was selling fresh milk, a guest arrived."
📌 नियम: लंबा कार्य → Past Continuous; बीच में आने वाली घटना → Simple Past। I/He/She/It/एकवचन → was; We/You/They/बहुवचन → were। उदाहरण: 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ has sold – Present Perfect; भूतकालीन उपवाक्य से मेल नहीं खाता। is selling – Present Continuous; दूसरा उपवाक्य भूतकाल में है, अतः भूतकाल चाहिए। will sell – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ।
expe:
✔ 'While' marks a longer action in progress in the past, interrupted by a shorter Simple Past action ('a guest arrived') → Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing): "While Kavita was selling fresh milk, a guest arrived."
📌 Pattern: longer action → Past Continuous; interrupting action → Simple Past. I/He/She/It/singular → was; We/You/They/plural → were. E.g. 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ has sold – Present Perfect; does not match a past-time clause. is selling – Present Continuous; the other clause is in the past, so tense must be past. will sell – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time.

q: Fill in the blank: Gopal ___ old watches before the bell rang.
exp:
✔ भूतकाल की दो घटनाएँ: जो पहले पूरी हुई उसमें Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) (had + V3), बाद वाली में Simple Past ('the bell rang')। अतः 'had repaired' सही है: "Gopal had repaired old watches before the bell rang."
📌 'before' → पहले वाली घटना had + V3 में; 'after' वाले उपवाक्य में had + V3 आता है: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' सभी कर्ताओं के साथ आता है।
✖ repairs – Simple Present; भूतकालीन घटनाओं वाले वाक्य में उपयुक्त नहीं। will repair – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। has repaired – Present Perfect; भूत को वर्तमान से जोड़ता है, दूसरी भूतकालीन घटना से नहीं।
expe:
✔ Two past actions: the one completed first takes Past Perfect (had + V3), the later one Simple Past ('the bell rang'). So 'had repaired' is correct: "Gopal had repaired old watches before the bell rang."
📌 'Before' → earlier action in had + V3; 'after' → had + V3 comes in the 'after' clause: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' is used with all subjects.
✖ repairs – Simple Present; does not fit a sentence about past events. will repair – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. has repaired – Present Perfect; links the past with the present, not with another past action.

q: Fill in the blank: Rekha gave up ___ by bus.
exp:
✔ क्रिया 'give up' के बाद हमेशा gerund (V-ing) आता है, infinitive (to + V1) नहीं। अतः 'travelling' सही है: "Rekha gave up travelling by bus."
📌 Gerund (V-ing) लेने वाली क्रियाएँ: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep। उदाहरण: 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ to travel – to-infinitive; 'give up' के बाद infinitive नहीं आता। travel – मूल रूप (V1); 'gave up' के तुरंत बाद नहीं आ सकता। travelled – past/past participle रूप; 'gave up' के कर्म के रूप में प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ The verb 'give up' is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), not by an infinitive. So 'travelling' is correct: "Rekha gave up travelling by bus."
📌 Verbs + gerund: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep. E.g. 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ to travel – to-infinitive; 'give up' does not take an infinitive. travel – base form (V1); cannot follow 'gave up' directly. travelled – past/past participle form; not used as the object of 'gave up'.

q: Fill in the blank: My father should ___ the ball.
exp:
✔ modal verb 'should' के बाद बिना 'to' का मूल रूप (bare infinitive, V1) आता है। अतः 'throw' सही है: "My father should throw the ball."
📌 Bare infinitive इनके बाद आता है: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, तथा make/let/see/hear + object। उदाहरण: 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ throwing – -ing रूप; 'should' के बाद नहीं आता। to throw – to-infinitive; 'should' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता। throws – s-रूप; 'should' के बाद क्रिया में -s नहीं लगता।
expe:
✔ After the modal verb 'should', the bare infinitive (V1 without 'to') is used. So 'throw' is correct: "My father should throw the ball."
📌 Bare infinitive follows: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, and make/let/see/hear + object. E.g. 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ throwing – -ing form; cannot follow 'should'. to throw – to-infinitive; 'should' is not followed by 'to'. throws – s-form; after 'should' the verb never takes -s.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Sunita has collected the fees.
exp:
✔ "Sunita has collected the fees." में संरचना has/have + V3 – हाल ही में पूरा हुआ कार्य जिसका प्रभाव वर्तमान में है है। अतः यह Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) है।
📌 Present Perfect के साथ just, already, yet, ever, never, since/for आते हैं, पर निश्चित भूतकाल (yesterday, last year) नहीं।
✖ Present Perfect Continuous (पूर्ण-निरंतर वर्तमान) – संरचना has/have been + V-ing। Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) – संरचना is/am/are + V-ing। Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) – संरचना had + V3।
expe:
✔ "Sunita has collected the fees." follows the structure has/have + V3 – an action just completed whose result is relevant now. Hence it is Present Perfect.
📌 Present Perfect takes words like just, already, yet, ever, never, since/for, but not definite past time (yesterday, last year).
✖ Present Perfect Continuous – structure has/have been + V-ing. Present Continuous – structure is/am/are + V-ing. Past Perfect – structure had + V3.

q: Which of the following verb forms (V1 – V2 – V3) is correct?
exp:
✔ 'grow – grew – grown' सही V1 – V2 – V3 क्रम है: V2 'grew' Simple Past में और V3 'grown' has/have/had तथा passive voice में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 इसी तरह के irregular रूप: know – knew – known, throw – threw – thrown, blow – blew – blown। Irregular verbs में V2/V3 -ed लगाकर नहीं बनते।
✖ come – came – comed – 'comed' गलत है; सही: come – came – come। take – took – taked – 'taked' गलत है; सही: take – took – taken। give – gived – given – 'gived' गलत है; सही: give – gave – given।
expe:
✔ 'grow – grew – grown' is the correct V1 – V2 – V3 sequence: V2 'grew' is used in Simple Past and V3 'grown' with has/have/had and in the passive voice.
📌 Similar irregular pattern: know – knew – known, throw – threw – thrown, blow – blew – blown. Irregular verbs never form V2/V3 with -ed.
✖ come – came – comed – 'comed' is wrong; correct: come – came – come. take – took – taked – 'taked' is wrong; correct: take – took – taken. give – gived – given – 'gived' is wrong; correct: give – gave – given.

q: Fill in the blank: Each of the players ___ submitted the form.
exp:
✔ 'Each of the + बहुवचन संज्ञा' में वास्तविक कर्ता 'Each' (एकवचन) है, इसलिए एकवचन क्रिया 'has' आएगी: "Each of the players has submitted the form."
📌 Each/Either/Neither/One of + बहुवचन संज्ञा → एकवचन क्रिया: 'Neither of the boys was present.'
✖ were – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। have – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। are – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है।
expe:
✔ In 'Each of the + plural noun', the real subject is 'Each' (singular), so the singular verb 'has' is used: "Each of the players has submitted the form."
📌 Each/Either/Neither/One of + plural noun → singular verb: 'Neither of the boys was present.'
✖ were – plural verb; the subject here is singular. have – plural verb; the subject here is singular. are – plural verb; the subject here is singular.

q: Fill in the blank: They ___ in Ujjain since Diwali.
exp:
✔ 'since Diwali' बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब तक जारी है → Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) (has/have + V3)। अतः 'have been' सही है: "They have been in Ujjain since Diwali."
📌 'Since' + समय-बिंदु (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + समयावधि (for two years)। चल रहे कार्य के लिए Present Perfect Continuous भी आता है: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ were – Simple Past; समाप्त कार्य बताता है, अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं। will be – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। are – Simple Present; 'since' के साथ भूत से अब तक की अवधि नहीं बता सकता।
expe:
✔ 'since Diwali' shows an action that began in the past and still continues → Present Perfect (has/have + V3). So 'have been' is correct: "They have been in Ujjain since Diwali."
📌 'Since' + point of time (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + period of time (for two years). For a continuing activity, Present Perfect Continuous is also used: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ were – Simple Past; shows a finished action, not one continuing till now. will be – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. are – Simple Present; cannot express a period from the past up to now with 'since'.

q: Fill in the blank: The girls ___ the shoes when a dog started barking.
exp:
✔ कार्य चल रहा था तभी दूसरी छोटी भूतकालीन घटना हुई ('when a dog started barking') → Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) (was/were + V-ing): "The girls were polishing the shoes when a dog started barking."
📌 नियम: लंबा कार्य → Past Continuous; बीच में आने वाली घटना → Simple Past। I/He/She/It/एकवचन → was; We/You/They/बहुवचन → were। उदाहरण: 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ will polish – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। are polishing – Present Continuous; दूसरा उपवाक्य भूतकाल में है, अतः भूतकाल चाहिए। have polished – Present Perfect; भूतकालीन उपवाक्य से मेल नहीं खाता।
expe:
✔ The action was in progress when another short past action happened ('when a dog started barking') → Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing): "The girls were polishing the shoes when a dog started barking."
📌 Pattern: longer action → Past Continuous; interrupting action → Simple Past. I/He/She/It/singular → was; We/You/They/plural → were. E.g. 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ will polish – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. are polishing – Present Continuous; the other clause is in the past, so tense must be past. have polished – Present Perfect; does not match a past-time clause.

q: Fill in the blank: My uncle ___ the dishes before the guests arrived.
exp:
✔ भूतकाल की दो घटनाएँ: जो पहले पूरी हुई उसमें Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) (had + V3), बाद वाली में Simple Past ('the guests arrived')। अतः 'had washed' सही है: "My uncle had washed the dishes before the guests arrived."
📌 'before' → पहले वाली घटना had + V3 में; 'after' वाले उपवाक्य में had + V3 आता है: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' सभी कर्ताओं के साथ आता है।
✖ has washed – Present Perfect; भूत को वर्तमान से जोड़ता है, दूसरी भूतकालीन घटना से नहीं। will wash – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। washes – Simple Present; भूतकालीन घटनाओं वाले वाक्य में उपयुक्त नहीं।
expe:
✔ Two past actions: the one completed first takes Past Perfect (had + V3), the later one Simple Past ('the guests arrived'). So 'had washed' is correct: "My uncle had washed the dishes before the guests arrived."
📌 'Before' → earlier action in had + V3; 'after' → had + V3 comes in the 'after' clause: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' is used with all subjects.
✖ has washed – Present Perfect; links the past with the present, not with another past action. will wash – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. washes – Simple Present; does not fit a sentence about past events.

q: Fill in the blank: The boy learnt ___ the army.
exp:
✔ क्रिया 'learn' के बाद to-infinitive (to + V1) आता है। अतः 'to join' सही है: "The boy learnt to join the army."
📌 to-infinitive लेने वाली क्रियाएँ: promise, learn, afford, decide, hope, want, agree, refuse, plan, wish, offer। उदाहरण: 'She decided to leave.' / 'They agreed to help.'
✖ joining – gerund; 'learn' के बाद gerund नहीं आता। join – बिना 'to' का मूल रूप; 'learn' के बाद 'to' चाहिए। to joining – यहाँ 'to' + V-ing गलत है; infinitive का रूप to + V1 होता है।
expe:
✔ The verb 'learn' is followed by a to-infinitive (to + V1). So 'to join' is correct: "The boy learnt to join the army."
📌 Verbs + to-infinitive: promise, learn, afford, decide, hope, want, agree, refuse, plan, wish, offer. E.g. 'She decided to leave.' / 'They agreed to help.'
✖ joining – gerund; 'learn' does not take a gerund. join – bare infinitive (V1 without 'to'); 'learn' needs 'to'. to joining – 'to' + V-ing is wrong here; an infinitive is to + V1.

q: Fill in the blank: Seema would rather ___ a new book than wait here.
exp:
✔ 'would rather' के बाद बिना 'to' का मूल रूप (bare infinitive, V1) आता है। अतः 'choose' सही है: "Seema would rather choose a new book than wait here."
📌 Bare infinitive इनके बाद आता है: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, तथा make/let/see/hear + object। उदाहरण: 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ chosen – past/past participle रूप; 'would rather' के बाद V1 चाहिए। to choose – to-infinitive; 'would rather' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता। choosing – -ing रूप; 'would rather' के बाद नहीं आता।
expe:
✔ After 'would rather', the bare infinitive (V1 without 'to') is used. So 'choose' is correct: "Seema would rather choose a new book than wait here."
📌 Bare infinitive follows: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, and make/let/see/hear + object. E.g. 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ chosen – past/past participle form; 'would rather' needs V1. to choose – to-infinitive; 'would rather' is not followed by 'to'. choosing – -ing form; cannot follow 'would rather'.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: The boys were arranging the books when we came.
exp:
✔ "The boys were arranging the books when we came." में संरचना was/were + V-ing – भूतकाल में किसी समय चल रहा कार्य है। अतः यह Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) है।
📌 Past Continuous प्रायः when/while के साथ Simple Past से जुड़ता है: 'I was sleeping when he called.'
✖ Past Perfect Continuous (पूर्ण-निरंतर भूत) – संरचना had been + V-ing। Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) – संरचना is/am/are + V-ing। Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) – संरचना had + V3।
expe:
✔ "The boys were arranging the books when we came." follows the structure was/were + V-ing – an action in progress at a point in the past. Hence it is Past Continuous.
📌 Past Continuous is often paired with Simple Past using when/while: 'I was sleeping when he called.'
✖ Past Perfect Continuous – structure had been + V-ing. Present Continuous – structure is/am/are + V-ing. Past Perfect – structure had + V3.

q: Which of the following verb forms (V1 – V2 – V3) is correct?
exp:
✔ 'wear – wore – worn' सही V1 – V2 – V3 क्रम है: V2 'wore' Simple Past में और V3 'worn' has/have/had तथा passive voice में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 इसी तरह के irregular रूप: swear – swore – sworn, tear – tore – torn। Irregular verbs में V2/V3 -ed लगाकर नहीं बनते।
✖ know – knew – knowed – 'knowed' गलत है; सही: know – knew – known। take – taken – took – V2 और V3 उलटे हैं; सही: take – took – taken। drink – drank – drinked – 'drinked' गलत है; सही: drink – drank – drunk।
expe:
✔ 'wear – wore – worn' is the correct V1 – V2 – V3 sequence: V2 'wore' is used in Simple Past and V3 'worn' with has/have/had and in the passive voice.
📌 Similar irregular pattern: swear – swore – sworn, tear – tore – torn. Irregular verbs never form V2/V3 with -ed.
✖ know – knew – knowed – 'knowed' is wrong; correct: know – knew – known. take – taken – took – V2 and V3 are swapped; correct: take – took – taken. drink – drank – drinked – 'drinked' is wrong; correct: drink – drank – drunk.

q: Fill in the blank: Every player ___ given a book.
exp:
✔ 'Every' + एकवचन संज्ञा के साथ एकवचन क्रिया आती है। Past passive: was + V3 → "Every player was given a book."
📌 Each, every, either, neither, everyone, everybody के साथ एकवचन क्रिया: 'Every student has a book.' / 'Each of them is ready.'
✖ were – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। have – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। are – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है।
expe:
✔ 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb. Past passive: was + V3 → "Every player was given a book."
📌 Each, every, either, neither, everyone, everybody take a singular verb: 'Every student has a book.' / 'Each of them is ready.'
✖ were – plural verb; the subject here is singular. have – plural verb; the subject here is singular. are – plural verb; the subject here is singular.

q: Fill in the blank: Sunita ___ in this office since January.
exp:
✔ 'since January' बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब तक जारी है → Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) (has/have + V3)। अतः 'has worked' सही है: "Sunita has worked in this office since January."
📌 'Since' + समय-बिंदु (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + समयावधि (for two years)। चल रहे कार्य के लिए Present Perfect Continuous भी आता है: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ is working – Present Continuous; 'since' के साथ अब तक की अवधि के लिए प्रयोग नहीं होता। worked – Simple Past; समाप्त कार्य बताता है, अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं। works – Simple Present; 'since' के साथ भूत से अब तक की अवधि नहीं बता सकता।
expe:
✔ 'since January' shows an action that began in the past and still continues → Present Perfect (has/have + V3). So 'has worked' is correct: "Sunita has worked in this office since January."
📌 'Since' + point of time (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + period of time (for two years). For a continuing activity, Present Perfect Continuous is also used: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ is working – Present Continuous; not used with 'since' for a period up to now. worked – Simple Past; shows a finished action, not one continuing till now. works – Simple Present; cannot express a period from the past up to now with 'since'.

q: Fill in the blank: While Vijay ___ vegetables, the phone rang.
exp:
✔ 'While' भूतकाल में चल रहे लंबे कार्य को बताता है, जिसे Simple Past की छोटी घटना ('the phone rang') ने बीच में रोका → Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) (was/were + V-ing): "While Vijay was growing vegetables, the phone rang."
📌 नियम: लंबा कार्य → Past Continuous; बीच में आने वाली घटना → Simple Past। I/He/She/It/एकवचन → was; We/You/They/बहुवचन → were। उदाहरण: 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ is growing – Present Continuous; दूसरा उपवाक्य भूतकाल में है, अतः भूतकाल चाहिए। will grow – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। has grown – Present Perfect; भूतकालीन उपवाक्य से मेल नहीं खाता।
expe:
✔ 'While' marks a longer action in progress in the past, interrupted by a shorter Simple Past action ('the phone rang') → Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing): "While Vijay was growing vegetables, the phone rang."
📌 Pattern: longer action → Past Continuous; interrupting action → Simple Past. I/He/She/It/singular → was; We/You/They/plural → were. E.g. 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ is growing – Present Continuous; the other clause is in the past, so tense must be past. will grow – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. has grown – Present Perfect; does not match a past-time clause.

q: Fill in the blank: Manoj ___ heavy boxes before the guests arrived.
exp:
✔ भूतकाल की दो घटनाएँ: जो पहले पूरी हुई उसमें Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) (had + V3), बाद वाली में Simple Past ('the guests arrived')। अतः 'had carried' सही है: "Manoj had carried heavy boxes before the guests arrived."
📌 'before' → पहले वाली घटना had + V3 में; 'after' वाले उपवाक्य में had + V3 आता है: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' सभी कर्ताओं के साथ आता है।
✖ will carry – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। carries – Simple Present; भूतकालीन घटनाओं वाले वाक्य में उपयुक्त नहीं। has carried – Present Perfect; भूत को वर्तमान से जोड़ता है, दूसरी भूतकालीन घटना से नहीं।
expe:
✔ Two past actions: the one completed first takes Past Perfect (had + V3), the later one Simple Past ('the guests arrived'). So 'had carried' is correct: "Manoj had carried heavy boxes before the guests arrived."
📌 'Before' → earlier action in had + V3; 'after' → had + V3 comes in the 'after' clause: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' is used with all subjects.
✖ will carry – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. carries – Simple Present; does not fit a sentence about past events. has carried – Present Perfect; links the past with the present, not with another past action.

q: Fill in the blank: Vijay postponed ___ television.
exp:
✔ क्रिया 'postpone' के बाद हमेशा gerund (V-ing) आता है, infinitive (to + V1) नहीं। अतः 'watching' सही है: "Vijay postponed watching television."
📌 Gerund (V-ing) लेने वाली क्रियाएँ: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep। उदाहरण: 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ watched – past/past participle रूप; 'postponed' के कर्म के रूप में प्रयोग नहीं होता। watch – मूल रूप (V1); 'postponed' के तुरंत बाद नहीं आ सकता। to watch – to-infinitive; 'postpone' के बाद infinitive नहीं आता।
expe:
✔ The verb 'postpone' is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), not by an infinitive. So 'watching' is correct: "Vijay postponed watching television."
📌 Verbs + gerund: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep. E.g. 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ watched – past/past participle form; not used as the object of 'postponed'. watch – base form (V1); cannot follow 'postponed' directly. to watch – to-infinitive; 'postpone' does not take an infinitive.

q: Fill in the blank: Usha should ___ the drum.
exp:
✔ modal verb 'should' के बाद बिना 'to' का मूल रूप (bare infinitive, V1) आता है। अतः 'beat' सही है: "Usha should beat the drum."
📌 Bare infinitive इनके बाद आता है: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, तथा make/let/see/hear + object। उदाहरण: 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ beating – -ing रूप; 'should' के बाद नहीं आता। beats – s-रूप; 'should' के बाद क्रिया में -s नहीं लगता। to beat – to-infinitive; 'should' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता।
expe:
✔ After the modal verb 'should', the bare infinitive (V1 without 'to') is used. So 'beat' is correct: "Usha should beat the drum."
📌 Bare infinitive follows: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, and make/let/see/hear + object. E.g. 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ beating – -ing form; cannot follow 'should'. beats – s-form; after 'should' the verb never takes -s. to beat – to-infinitive; 'should' is not followed by 'to'.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: I have sung a song.
exp:
✔ "I have sung a song." में संरचना has/have + V3 – हाल ही में पूरा हुआ कार्य जिसका प्रभाव वर्तमान में है है। अतः यह Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) है।
📌 Present Perfect के साथ just, already, yet, ever, never, since/for आते हैं, पर निश्चित भूतकाल (yesterday, last year) नहीं।
✖ Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) – संरचना is/am/are + V-ing। Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान) – संरचना V1 / V1+s/es। Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) – संरचना had + V3।
expe:
✔ "I have sung a song." follows the structure has/have + V3 – an action just completed whose result is relevant now. Hence it is Present Perfect.
📌 Present Perfect takes words like just, already, yet, ever, never, since/for, but not definite past time (yesterday, last year).
✖ Present Continuous – structure is/am/are + V-ing. Simple Present – structure V1 / V1+s/es. Past Perfect – structure had + V3.

q: Which of the following verb forms (V1 – V2 – V3) is correct?
exp:
✔ 'forbid – forbade – forbidden' सही V1 – V2 – V3 क्रम है: V2 'forbade' Simple Past में और V3 'forbidden' has/have/had तथा passive voice में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 Irregular verbs में V2/V3 -ed लगाकर नहीं बनते।
✖ arise – arisen – arose – V2 और V3 उलटे हैं; सही: arise – arose – arisen। break – breaked – broken – 'breaked' गलत है; सही: break – broke – broken। do – doed – done – 'doed' गलत है; सही: do – did – done।
expe:
✔ 'forbid – forbade – forbidden' is the correct V1 – V2 – V3 sequence: V2 'forbade' is used in Simple Past and V3 'forbidden' with has/have/had and in the passive voice.
📌 Irregular verbs never form V2/V3 with -ed.
✖ arise – arisen – arose – V2 and V3 are swapped; correct: arise – arose – arisen. break – breaked – broken – 'breaked' is wrong; correct: break – broke – broken. do – doed – done – 'doed' is wrong; correct: do – did – done.

q: Fill in the blank: The police ___ searching for the thief.
exp:
✔ 'Police' ऐसी संज्ञा है जो हमेशा बहुवचन में प्रयोग होती है, इसलिए 'are' सही है: "The police are searching for the thief."
📌 हमेशा बहुवचन संज्ञाएँ: police, cattle, people, poultry → बहुवचन क्रिया ('The cattle are grazing')। 'searching' के साथ be-क्रिया (continuous) चाहिए।
✖ has – 'has + V-ing' कोई सही रूप नहीं; साथ ही police बहुवचन है। was – एकवचन क्रिया; 'police' के साथ बहुवचन क्रिया आती है। is – एकवचन क्रिया; 'police' के साथ बहुवचन क्रिया आती है।
expe:
✔ 'Police' is a collective noun always used as plural, so 'are' is correct: "The police are searching for the thief."
📌 Always-plural nouns: police, cattle, people, poultry → plural verb ('The cattle are grazing'). 'Searching' needs a be-verb (continuous).
✖ has – 'has + V-ing' is not a valid form; also police is plural. was – singular verb; 'police' takes a plural verb. is – singular verb; 'police' takes a plural verb.

q: Fill in the blank: The student ___ in Khandwa since 2012.
exp:
✔ 'since 2012' बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब तक जारी है → Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) (has/have + V3)। अतः 'has lived' सही है: "The student has lived in Khandwa since 2012."
📌 'Since' + समय-बिंदु (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + समयावधि (for two years)। चल रहे कार्य के लिए Present Perfect Continuous भी आता है: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ lived – Simple Past; समाप्त कार्य बताता है, अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं। lives – Simple Present; 'since' के साथ भूत से अब तक की अवधि नहीं बता सकता। is living – Present Continuous; 'since' के साथ अब तक की अवधि के लिए प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ 'since 2012' shows an action that began in the past and still continues → Present Perfect (has/have + V3). So 'has lived' is correct: "The student has lived in Khandwa since 2012."
📌 'Since' + point of time (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + period of time (for two years). For a continuing activity, Present Perfect Continuous is also used: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ lived – Simple Past; shows a finished action, not one continuing till now. lives – Simple Present; cannot express a period from the past up to now with 'since'. is living – Present Continuous; not used with 'since' for a period up to now.

q: Fill in the blank: Rahul ___ the notice when the bell rang.
exp:
✔ कार्य चल रहा था तभी दूसरी छोटी भूतकालीन घटना हुई ('when the bell rang') → Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) (was/were + V-ing): "Rahul was typing the notice when the bell rang."
📌 नियम: लंबा कार्य → Past Continuous; बीच में आने वाली घटना → Simple Past। I/He/She/It/एकवचन → was; We/You/They/बहुवचन → were। उदाहरण: 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ is typing – Present Continuous; दूसरा उपवाक्य भूतकाल में है, अतः भूतकाल चाहिए। has typed – Present Perfect; भूतकालीन उपवाक्य से मेल नहीं खाता। will type – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ।
expe:
✔ The action was in progress when another short past action happened ('when the bell rang') → Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing): "Rahul was typing the notice when the bell rang."
📌 Pattern: longer action → Past Continuous; interrupting action → Simple Past. I/He/She/It/singular → was; We/You/They/plural → were. E.g. 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ is typing – Present Continuous; the other clause is in the past, so tense must be past. has typed – Present Perfect; does not match a past-time clause. will type – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time.

✖ worked – past/past participle रूप; 'avoided' के कर्म के रूप में प्रयोग नहीं होता। work – मूल रूप (V1); 'avoided' के तुरंत बाद नहीं आ सकता। to work – to-infinitive; 'avoid' के बाद infinitive नहीं आता।

q: Fill in the blank: The teacher made the student ___ history.
exp:
✔ causative 'make' + object के बाद बिना 'to' का मूल रूप (bare infinitive, V1) आता है। अतः 'study' सही है: "The teacher made the student study history."

✖ studying – -ing रूप; 'made' के बाद नहीं आता। to study – to-infinitive; 'made' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता। studied – past/past participle रूप; 'made' के बाद V1 चाहिए।
expe:
✔ After causative 'make' + object, the bare infinitive (V1 without 'to') is used. So 'study' is correct: "The teacher made the student study history."
📌 Bare infinitive follows: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, and make/let/see/hear + object. E.g. 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ studying – -ing form; cannot follow 'made'. to study – to-infinitive; 'made' is not followed by 'to'. studied – past/past participle form; 'made' needs V1.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Nisha is repairing the bicycle.
exp:
✔ "Nisha is repairing the bicycle." में संरचना is/am/are + V-ing – वर्तमान में चल रहा कार्य है। अतः यह Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) है।
📌 संकेत शब्द: now, at present, at the moment, Look!, Listen!। State verbs (know, like, believe) सामान्यतः continuous रूप में नहीं आते।
✖ Present Perfect Continuous (पूर्ण-निरंतर वर्तमान) – संरचना has/have been + V-ing। Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान) – संरचना V1 / V1+s/es। Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) – संरचना was/were + V-ing।
expe:
✔ "Nisha is repairing the bicycle." follows the structure is/am/are + V-ing – an action going on at present. Hence it is Present Continuous.
📌 Signal words: now, at present, at the moment, Look!, Listen!. State verbs (know, like, believe) are usually not used in continuous form.
✖ Present Perfect Continuous – structure has/have been + V-ing. Simple Present – structure V1 / V1+s/es. Past Continuous – structure was/were + V-ing.

q: Which of the following verb forms (V1 – V2 – V3) is correct?
exp:
✔ 'swear – swore – sworn' सही V1 – V2 – V3 क्रम है: V2 'swore' Simple Past में और V3 'sworn' has/have/had तथा passive voice में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 इसी तरह के irregular रूप: wear – wore – worn, tear – tore – torn। Irregular verbs में V2/V3 -ed लगाकर नहीं बनते।
✖ bite – bitten – bit – V2 और V3 उलटे हैं; सही: bite – bit – bitten। drive – driven – drove – V2 और V3 उलटे हैं; सही: drive – drove – driven। run – run – ran – V2 और V3 उलटे हैं; सही: run – ran – run।
expe:
✔ 'swear – swore – sworn' is the correct V1 – V2 – V3 sequence: V2 'swore' is used in Simple Past and V3 'sworn' with has/have/had and in the passive voice.
📌 Similar irregular pattern: wear – wore – worn, tear – tore – torn. Irregular verbs never form V2/V3 with -ed.
✖ bite – bitten – bit – V2 and V3 are swapped; correct: bite – bit – bitten. drive – driven – drove – V2 and V3 are swapped; correct: drive – drove – driven. run – run – ran – V2 and V3 are swapped; correct: run – ran – run.

q: Fill in the blank: One of the children ___ won a medal.
exp:
✔ 'One of the + बहुवचन संज्ञा' में कर्ता 'One' (एकवचन) है, इसलिए एकवचन क्रिया 'has' आएगी: "One of the children has won a medal."
📌 'One of' के बाद संज्ञा बहुवचन पर क्रिया एकवचन होती है: 'One of my friends is a doctor.'
✖ have – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। were – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। are – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है।
expe:
✔ In 'One of the + plural noun', the subject is 'One' (singular), so the singular verb 'has' is used: "One of the children has won a medal."
📌 'One of' is always followed by a plural noun but a singular verb: 'One of my friends is a doctor.'
✖ have – plural verb; the subject here is singular. were – plural verb; the subject here is singular. are – plural verb; the subject here is singular.

✔ क्रिया 'finish' के बाद हमेशा gerund (V-ing) आता है, infinitive (to + V1) नहीं। अतः 'working' सही है: "Arjun finished working late."
📌 Gerund (V-ing) लेने वाली क्रियाएँ: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep। उदाहरण: 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ to work – to-infinitive; 'finish' के बाद infinitive नहीं आता। worked – past/past participle रूप; 'finished' के कर्म के रूप में प्रयोग नहीं होता। work – मूल रूप (V1); 'finished' के तुरंत बाद नहीं आ सकता।
expe:
✔ The verb 'finish' is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), not by an infinitive. So 'working' is correct: "Arjun finished working late."
📌 Verbs + gerund: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep. E.g. 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ to work – to-infinitive; 'finish' does not take an infinitive. worked – past/past participle form; not used as the object of 'finished'. work – base form (V1); cannot follow 'finished' directly.

q: Fill in the blank: Pooja need not ___ the kitchen.
exp:
✔ modal 'need not' के बाद बिना 'to' का मूल रूप (bare infinitive, V1) आता है। अतः 'clean' सही है: "Pooja need not clean the kitchen."
📌 Bare infinitive इनके बाद आता है: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, तथा make/let/see/hear + object। उदाहरण: 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ to clean – to-infinitive; 'need not' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता। cleaned – past/past participle रूप; 'need not' के बाद V1 चाहिए। cleaning – -ing रूप; 'need not' के बाद नहीं आता।
expe:
✔ After the modal 'need not', the bare infinitive (V1 without 'to') is used. So 'clean' is correct: "Pooja need not clean the kitchen."
📌 Bare infinitive follows: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, and make/let/see/hear + object. E.g. 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ to clean – to-infinitive; 'need not' is not followed by 'to'. cleaned – past/past participle form; 'need not' needs V1. cleaning – -ing form; cannot follow 'need not'.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Ravi has repaired the radio.
exp:
✔ "Ravi has repaired the radio." में संरचना has/have + V3 – हाल ही में पूरा हुआ कार्य जिसका प्रभाव वर्तमान में है है। अतः यह Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) है।
📌 Present Perfect के साथ just, already, yet, ever, never, since/for आते हैं, पर निश्चित भूतकाल (yesterday, last year) नहीं।
✖ Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) – संरचना had + V3। Present Perfect Continuous (पूर्ण-निरंतर वर्तमान) – संरचना has/have been + V-ing। Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान) – संरचना V1 / V1+s/es।
expe:
✔ "Ravi has repaired the radio." follows the structure has/have + V3 – an action just completed whose result is relevant now. Hence it is Present Perfect.
📌 Present Perfect takes words like just, already, yet, ever, never, since/for, but not definite past time (yesterday, last year).
✖ Past Perfect – structure had + V3. Present Perfect Continuous – structure has/have been + V-ing. Simple Present – structure V1 / V1+s/es.

q: Which of the following verb forms (V1 – V2 – V3) is correct?
exp:
✔ 'wear – wore – worn' सही V1 – V2 – V3 क्रम है: V2 'wore' Simple Past में और V3 'worn' has/have/had तथा passive voice में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 इसी तरह के irregular रूप: swear – swore – sworn, tear – tore – torn। Irregular verbs में V2/V3 -ed लगाकर नहीं बनते।
✖ freeze – froze – freezed – 'freezed' गलत है; सही: freeze – froze – frozen। forget – forgeted – forgotten – 'forgeted' गलत है; सही: forget – forgot – forgotten। swim – swimed – swum – 'swimed' गलत है; सही: swim – swam – swum।
expe:
✔ 'wear – wore – worn' is the correct V1 – V2 – V3 sequence: V2 'wore' is used in Simple Past and V3 'worn' with has/have/had and in the passive voice.
📌 Similar irregular pattern: swear – swore – sworn, tear – tore – torn. Irregular verbs never form V2/V3 with -ed.
✖ freeze – froze – freezed – 'freezed' is wrong; correct: freeze – froze – frozen. forget – forgeted – forgotten – 'forgeted' is wrong; correct: forget – forgot – forgotten. swim – swimed – swum – 'swimed' is wrong; correct: swim – swam – swum.

q: Fill in the blank: One of the players ___ absent today.
exp:
✔ 'One of the + बहुवचन संज्ञा' में कर्ता 'One' (एकवचन) है, इसलिए एकवचन क्रिया 'is' आएगी: "One of the players is absent today."
📌 'One of' के बाद संज्ञा बहुवचन पर क्रिया एकवचन होती है: 'One of my friends is a doctor.'
✖ were – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। have – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है। are – बहुवचन क्रिया; यहाँ कर्ता एकवचन है।
expe:
✔ In 'One of the + plural noun', the subject is 'One' (singular), so the singular verb 'is' is used: "One of the players is absent today."
📌 'One of' is always followed by a plural noun but a singular verb: 'One of my friends is a doctor.'
✖ were – plural verb; the subject here is singular. have – plural verb; the subject here is singular. are – plural verb; the subject here is singular.

q: Fill in the blank: Anil ___ very happy since last year.
exp:
✔ 'since last year' बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब तक जारी है → Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) (has/have + V3)। अतः 'has been' सही है: "Anil has been very happy since last year."
📌 'Since' + समय-बिंदु (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + समयावधि (for two years)। चल रहे कार्य के लिए Present Perfect Continuous भी आता है: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ was – Simple Past; समाप्त कार्य बताता है, अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं। is – Simple Present; 'since' के साथ भूत से अब तक की अवधि नहीं बता सकता। will be – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ।
expe:
✔ 'since last year' shows an action that began in the past and still continues → Present Perfect (has/have + V3). So 'has been' is correct: "Anil has been very happy since last year."
📌 'Since' + point of time (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + period of time (for two years). For a continuing activity, Present Perfect Continuous is also used: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ was – Simple Past; shows a finished action, not one continuing till now. is – Simple Present; cannot express a period from the past up to now with 'since'. will be – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time.

q: Fill in the blank: Sunita ___ the notes when someone knocked at the door.
exp:
✔ कार्य चल रहा था तभी दूसरी छोटी भूतकालीन घटना हुई ('when someone knocked at the door') → Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) (was/were + V-ing): "Sunita was preparing the notes when someone knocked at the door."
📌 नियम: लंबा कार्य → Past Continuous; बीच में आने वाली घटना → Simple Past। I/He/She/It/एकवचन → was; We/You/They/बहुवचन → were। उदाहरण: 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ has prepared – Present Perfect; भूतकालीन उपवाक्य से मेल नहीं खाता। is preparing – Present Continuous; दूसरा उपवाक्य भूतकाल में है, अतः भूतकाल चाहिए। will prepare – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ।
expe:
✔ The action was in progress when another short past action happened ('when someone knocked at the door') → Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing): "Sunita was preparing the notes when someone knocked at the door."
📌 Pattern: longer action → Past Continuous; interrupting action → Simple Past. I/He/She/It/singular → was; We/You/They/plural → were. E.g. 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ has prepared – Present Perfect; does not match a past-time clause. is preparing – Present Continuous; the other clause is in the past, so tense must be past. will prepare – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time.

q: Fill in the blank: The boy ___ the project before it got dark.
exp:
✔ भूतकाल की दो घटनाएँ: जो पहले पूरी हुई उसमें Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) (had + V3), बाद वाली में Simple Past ('it got dark')। अतः 'had finished' सही है: "The boy had finished the project before it got dark."
📌 'before' → पहले वाली घटना had + V3 में; 'after' वाले उपवाक्य में had + V3 आता है: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' सभी कर्ताओं के साथ आता है।
✖ will finish – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। has finished – Present Perfect; भूत को वर्तमान से जोड़ता है, दूसरी भूतकालीन घटना से नहीं। finishes – Simple Present; भूतकालीन घटनाओं वाले वाक्य में उपयुक्त नहीं।
expe:
✔ Two past actions: the one completed first takes Past Perfect (had + V3), the later one Simple Past ('it got dark'). So 'had finished' is correct: "The boy had finished the project before it got dark."
📌 'Before' → earlier action in had + V3; 'after' → had + V3 comes in the 'after' clause: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' is used with all subjects.
✖ will finish – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. has finished – Present Perfect; links the past with the present, not with another past action. finishes – Simple Present; does not fit a sentence about past events.

q: Fill in the blank: Shalini avoided ___ the exam.
exp:
✔ क्रिया 'avoid' के बाद हमेशा gerund (V-ing) आता है, infinitive (to + V1) नहीं। अतः 'taking' सही है: "Shalini avoided taking the exam."
📌 Gerund (V-ing) लेने वाली क्रियाएँ: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep। उदाहरण: 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ to take – to-infinitive; 'avoid' के बाद infinitive नहीं आता। taken – past/past participle रूप; 'avoided' के कर्म के रूप में प्रयोग नहीं होता। take – मूल रूप (V1); 'avoided' के तुरंत बाद नहीं आ सकता।
expe:
✔ The verb 'avoid' is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), not by an infinitive. So 'taking' is correct: "Shalini avoided taking the exam."
📌 Verbs + gerund: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep. E.g. 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ to take – to-infinitive; 'avoid' does not take an infinitive. taken – past/past participle form; not used as the object of 'avoided'. take – base form (V1); cannot follow 'avoided' directly.

q: Fill in the blank: My father should ___ the parcel.
exp:
✔ modal verb 'should' के बाद बिना 'to' का मूल रूप (bare infinitive, V1) आता है। अतः 'deliver' सही है: "My father should deliver the parcel."
📌 Bare infinitive इनके बाद आता है: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, तथा make/let/see/hear + object। उदाहरण: 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ delivers – s-रूप; 'should' के बाद क्रिया में -s नहीं लगता। delivering – -ing रूप; 'should' के बाद नहीं आता। to deliver – to-infinitive; 'should' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता।
expe:
✔ After the modal verb 'should', the bare infinitive (V1 without 'to') is used. So 'deliver' is correct: "My father should deliver the parcel."
📌 Bare infinitive follows: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, and make/let/see/hear + object. E.g. 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ delivers – s-form; after 'should' the verb never takes -s. delivering – -ing form; cannot follow 'should'. to deliver – to-infinitive; 'should' is not followed by 'to'.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Suresh is checking the accounts.
exp:
✔ "Suresh is checking the accounts." में संरचना is/am/are + V-ing – वर्तमान में चल रहा कार्य है। अतः यह Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) है।
📌 संकेत शब्द: now, at present, at the moment, Look!, Listen!। State verbs (know, like, believe) सामान्यतः continuous रूप में नहीं आते।
✖ Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान) – संरचना V1 / V1+s/es। Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) – संरचना was/were + V-ing। Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) – संरचना has/have + V3।
expe:
✔ "Suresh is checking the accounts." follows the structure is/am/are + V-ing – an action going on at present. Hence it is Present Continuous.
📌 Signal words: now, at present, at the moment, Look!, Listen!. State verbs (know, like, believe) are usually not used in continuous form.
✖ Simple Present – structure V1 / V1+s/es. Past Continuous – structure was/were + V-ing. Present Perfect – structure has/have + V3.

q: Which of the following verb forms (V1 – V2 – V3) is correct?
exp:
✔ अनियमित क्रिया (irregular verb) 'come' का सही V1–V2–V3 क्रम 'come – came – come' है।
📌 Irregular verbs में -ed नहीं लगता। V2 का प्रयोग Simple Past में और V3 का प्रयोग has/have/had तथा Passive Voice में होता है। ध्यान दें: 'come' में V1 और V3 एक जैसे हैं।
✖ swear – sweared – sworn गलत – सही: swear – swore – sworn; know – knowed – known गलत – सही: know – knew – known; break – broke – breaked गलत – सही: break – broke – broken।
expe:
✔ 'come – came – come' is the correct V1–V2–V3 (base – past – past participle) sequence of the irregular verb 'come'.
📌 Irregular verbs do not take -ed. V2 is used in Simple Past (He came...), V3 with has/have/had and in the Passive (It has come... / had come). Note: in 'come' the V1 and V3 forms are the same.
✖ swear – sweared – sworn is wrong – correct: swear – swore – sworn; know – knowed – known is wrong – correct: know – knew – known; break – broke – breaked is wrong – correct: break – broke – broken.

q: Fill in the blank: One of the candidates ___ won a medal.
exp:
✔ 'One of the + plural noun' में वास्तविक subject 'one' है, इसलिए singular verb आएगा: 'One of the candidates has won a medal'।
📌 'Each of', 'Every', 'Either of', 'Neither of' के साथ भी singular verb आता है, जैसे 'One of my friends is a doctor.'
✖ 'are' – plural verb; 'have' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ With 'One of the + plural noun', the real subject is 'one', so a singular verb is needed: 'One of the candidates has won a medal'.
📌 'Each of', 'Every', 'Either of', 'Neither of' are also followed by a singular verb, e.g. 'One of my friends is a doctor.'
✖ 'are' – plural verb; 'have' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

q: Fill in the blank: Ravi ___ very happy since 2018.
exp:
✔ 'since 2018' उस समय-बिंदु को दर्शाता है जहाँ से कार्य/स्थिति अब तक जारी है, अतः Present Perfect (has/have + V3) आएगा: 'Ravi has been very happy since 2018'।
📌 since + समय-बिंदु (since 2018, since Monday); for + समयावधि (for two years)। ऐसे जारी कार्य के लिए Present Perfect Continuous (has been working) भी प्रयोग होता है।
✖ 'was' – Simple Past of 'be'; 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'will be' – Simple Future (will be) → 'since' के साथ जारी कार्य में प्रयोग नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'since 2018' shows a point of time from which the action/state continues up to now, so Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is used: 'Ravi has been very happy since 2018'.
📌 since + point of time (since 2018, since Monday); for + period of time (for two years). Present Perfect Continuous (has been working) can also express such continuing actions.
✖ 'was' – Simple Past of 'be'; 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'will be' – Simple Future (will be) → not used with 'since' for a continuing action.

q: Fill in the blank: While Asha ___ a cake, a dog started barking.
exp:
✔ भूतकाल में चल रहा एक लंबा कार्य किसी छोटे भूतकालिक कार्य (Simple Past) से बीच में बाधित हुआ। चल रहे कार्य के लिए Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing) आता है: 'While Asha was making a cake, a dog started barking'।
📌 संरचना: Past Continuous + when + Simple Past, या While + Past Continuous, Simple Past। जैसे 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ 'has made' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'will make' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'is making' – Present Continuous → दूसरे clause के भूतकाल से मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ A longer action that was in progress in the past was interrupted by a short past action (Simple Past). The longer action takes Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing): 'While Asha was making a cake, a dog started barking'.
📌 Pattern: Past Continuous + when + Simple Past, or While + Past Continuous, Simple Past. e.g. 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ 'has made' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'will make' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'is making' – Present Continuous → does not match the past time of the other clause.

q: Fill in the blank: The villagers ___ the windows before we reached there.
exp:
✔ दो भूतकालिक कार्यों में जो पहले पूरा हुआ उसमें Past Perfect (had + V3) और बाद वाले में Simple Past ('we reached there') आता है: 'The villagers had cleaned the windows before we reached there'।
📌 संकेत-शब्द: before, after, already, by the time। जैसे 'The train had left before we reached the station.'
✖ 'will clean' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'have cleaned' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'clean' – V1 (base form) → दो भूतकालिक कार्यों में पहले वाले कार्य को नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ Of two past actions, the earlier one takes Past Perfect (had + V3) and the later one Simple Past ('we reached there'): 'The villagers had cleaned the windows before we reached there'.
📌 Signal words: before, after, already, by the time. e.g. 'The train had left before we reached the station.' / 'After he had finished, he went home.'
✖ 'will clean' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'have cleaned' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'clean' – V1 (base form) → cannot show the earlier of two past actions.

q: Fill in the blank: Rakesh considered ___ the room.
exp:
✔ क्रिया 'consider' के बाद हमेशा gerund (V-ing) आता है, infinitive नहीं: 'Rakesh considered cleaning the room'।
📌 अन्य verbs जिनके बाद gerund आता है: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, deny, consider, practise, give up, keep, can't help, look forward to।
✖ 'clean' – V1 (base form); 'cleaned' – V2 (Simple Past); 'to clean' – to-infinitive → 'consider' के बाद प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ The verb 'consider' is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), not an infinitive: 'Rakesh considered cleaning the room'.
📌 Other verbs + gerund: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, deny, consider, practise, give up, keep, can't help, look forward to.
✖ 'clean' – V1 (base form); 'cleaned' – V2 (Simple Past); 'to clean' – to-infinitive → not used after 'consider'.

q: Fill in the blank: My brother is looking forward to ___ roses.
exp:
✔ 'look forward to' में 'to' preposition है (infinitive का भाग नहीं), इसलिए इसके बाद gerund (V-ing) आता है: 'My brother is looking forward to growing roses'।
📌 अन्य expressions जिनमें 'to' preposition है और V-ing आता है: object to, be used to, get used to, with a view to, be accustomed to।
✖ 'grows' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'grow' – V1 (base form); 'grown' – V3 (past participle; अकेले प्रयोग नहीं होता) → 'look forward to' के बाद प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, not part of an infinitive, so it is followed by a gerund (V-ing): 'My brother is looking forward to growing roses'.
📌 Other expressions with preposition 'to' + V-ing: object to, be used to, get used to, with a view to, be accustomed to.
✖ 'grows' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'grow' – V1 (base form); 'grown' – V3 (past participle; cannot stand alone) → not used after 'look forward to'.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Amit was studying science when we came.
exp:
✔ वाक्य 'Amit was studying science when we came' में संरचना was/were + V-ing है, अतः यह Past Continuous Tense है।
📌 Past Continuous का प्रयोग भूतकाल में किसी समय चल रहा कार्य के लिए होता है। 'when we came' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Simple Past = V2; Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing; Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing।
expe:
✔ 'Amit was studying science when we came' follows the pattern was/were + V-ing, so it is in the Past Continuous tense.
📌 Past Continuous is used for action in progress at a past moment. The phrase 'when we came' is a signal.

✔ क्रिया 'decide' के बाद to-infinitive (to + V1) आता है: 'My mother decided to sell the car'।
📌 अन्य verbs जिनके बाद to-infinitive आता है: want, decide, hope, agree, refuse, promise, plan, fail, learn, offer, wish, expect।
✖ 'to selling' – 'to + V-ing' (यहाँ गलत रूप); 'sell' – V1 (base form); 'selling' – V-ing (gerund/participle) → 'decide' के बाद 'to + V1' चाहिए।
expe:
✔ The verb 'decide' is followed by a to-infinitive (to + V1): 'My mother decided to sell the car'.
📌 Other verbs + to-infinitive: want, decide, hope, agree, refuse, promise, plan, fail, learn, offer, wish, expect.
✖ 'to selling' – 'to + V-ing' (incorrect form here); 'sell' – V1 (base form); 'selling' – V-ing (gerund/participle) → 'decide' needs 'to + V1'.

q: Fill in the blank: Jyoti should ___ the windows.
exp:
✔ 'should' एक modal auxiliary है; modals के बाद bare infinitive (बिना 'to' वाला V1) आता है: 'Jyoti should clean the windows'।
📌 can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must + V1 (न -s, न 'to')। अपवाद: ought to + V1।
✖ 'cleans' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'cleaning' – V-ing (gerund/participle); 'to clean' – to-infinitive → 'should' के बाद प्रयोग नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'should' is a modal auxiliary; modals are followed by the bare infinitive (V1 without 'to'): 'Jyoti should clean the windows'.
📌 can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must + V1 (no -s, no 'to'). Exception: ought to + V1.
✖ 'cleans' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'cleaning' – V-ing (gerund/participle); 'to clean' – to-infinitive → not used after 'should'.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: We make a kite.
exp:
✔ वाक्य 'We make a kite' में संरचना V1 / V1+s/es है, अतः यह Simple Present Tense है।
📌 Simple Present का प्रयोग आदत, सामान्य सत्य, नियमित कार्य के लिए होता है।
✖ Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing; Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing; Simple Past = V2।
expe:
✔ 'We make a kite' follows the pattern V1 / V1+s/es, so it is in the Simple Present tense.
📌 Simple Present is used for habit, general truth, regular action.
✖ Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing; Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing; Simple Past = V2.

q: Which of the following verb forms (V1 – V2 – V3) is correct?
exp:
✔ अनियमित क्रिया (irregular verb) 'drive' का सही V1–V2–V3 क्रम 'drive – drove – driven' है।
📌 Irregular verbs में -ed नहीं लगता। V2 का प्रयोग Simple Past में और V3 का प्रयोग has/have/had तथा Passive Voice में होता है।
✖ give – given – gave गलत – सही: give – gave – given; do – done – did गलत – सही: do – did – done; mistake – mistook – mistaked गलत – सही: mistake – mistook – mistaken।
expe:
✔ 'drive – drove – driven' is the correct V1–V2–V3 (base – past – past participle) sequence of the irregular verb 'drive'.
📌 Irregular verbs do not take -ed. V2 is used in Simple Past (He drove...), V3 with has/have/had and in the Passive (It has driven... / had driven).
✖ give – given – gave is wrong – correct: give – gave – given; do – done – did is wrong – correct: do – did – done; mistake – mistook – mistaked is wrong – correct: mistake – mistook – mistaken.

q: Fill in the blank: The cattle ___ grazing in the field.
exp:
✔ 'Cattle' हमेशा plural होता है (इसमें -s नहीं लगता), इसलिए plural verb आएगा: 'The cattle are grazing in the field'।
📌 इसी प्रकार police, people, poultry, gentry, clergy हमेशा plural verb लेते हैं, जैसे 'The police have arrived.'
✖ 'was' – singular verb; 'has' – singular verb; 'is' – singular verb → plural subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'Cattle' is always plural (it has no -s form), so a plural verb is used: 'The cattle are grazing in the field'.
📌 Other nouns always plural in sense: police, people, poultry, gentry, clergy – e.g. 'The police have arrived.'
✖ 'was' – singular verb; 'has' – singular verb; 'is' – singular verb → does not agree with a plural subject.

q: Fill in the blank: Harish ___ the diagram for two days and is still at it.
exp:
✔ 'since/for + समय' तथा 'and is still at it' (अभी भी जारी है) बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब भी चल रहा है, अतः Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) आएगा: 'Harish has been drawing the diagram for two days and is still at it'।
📌 since → समय-बिंदु (since morning); for → अवधि (for two days)। Stative verbs (know, like, own) के साथ Present Perfect आता है: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'was drawing' – Past Continuous; 'is drawing' – Present Continuous; 'draws' – V1+s (Simple Present) → भूतकाल से अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'since/for + time' together with 'and is still at it' shows an action that began in the past and is still continuing, so Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) is used: 'Harish has been drawing the diagram for two days and is still at it'.
📌 since → point of time (since morning); for → period (for two days). Stative verbs (know, like, own) take Present Perfect instead: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'was drawing' – Past Continuous; 'is drawing' – Present Continuous; 'draws' – V1+s (Simple Present) → does not show an action continuing from the past till now.

q: Fill in the blank: If the power had come back, he ___ the courtyard.
exp:
✔ If-clause 'the power had come back' Past Perfect (had + V3) में है, अतः यह Type-3 conditional (भूतकाल की अवास्तविक शर्त) है; main clause में 'would have + V3' आएगा: 'If the power had come back, he would have swept the courtyard'।
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'will have swept' – Future Perfect (will have + V3); 'had swept' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'will sweep' – Simple Future (will + V1) → Type-3 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ The if-clause 'the power had come back' is in Past Perfect (had + V3), so this is a Type-3 conditional (unreal past); the main clause takes 'would have + V3': 'If the power had come back, he would have swept the courtyard'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.
✖ 'will have swept' – Future Perfect (will have + V3); 'had swept' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'will sweep' – Simple Future (will + V1) → does not match a Type-3 if-clause.

q: Fill in the blank: I would rather Ravi ___ a bridge now.
exp:
✔ जब 'would rather' के बाद अलग subject हो, तो verb Simple Past (V2) में आता है, भले ही अर्थ वर्तमान/भविष्य का हो: 'I would rather Ravi built a bridge now'।
📌 Subject वही हो तो V1: 'I would rather stay.' ऐसा ही प्रयोग: 'It is high time you went', 'I wish I were…'।
✖ 'builds' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'has built' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'will build' – Simple Future (will + V1) → इस संरचना में प्रयोग नहीं।
expe:
✔ When 'would rather' is followed by a different subject, the verb is in the Simple Past (V2) though the meaning is present/future: 'I would rather Ravi built a bridge now'.
📌 Same subject → V1: 'I would rather stay.' Similar past-subjunctive use: 'It is high time you went', 'I wish I were…'.
✖ 'builds' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'has built' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'will build' – Simple Future (will + V1) → not used in this structure.

q: Fill in the blank: Usha used ___ alone when she was young.
exp:
✔ 'used to + V1' भूतकाल की ऐसी आदत/स्थिति बताता है जो अब नहीं है: 'Usha used to live alone when she was young'।
📌 'be/get used to + V-ing' (आदी होना) से भ्रमित न हों: 'She is used to living alone.' Negative: didn't use to + V1।
✖ 'live' – V1 (base form); 'to living' – 'to + V-ing' (यहाँ गलत रूप); 'living' – V-ing (gerund/participle) → 'used (past habit)' के बाद 'to + V1' चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'used to + V1' expresses a past habit or state that no longer exists: 'Usha used to live alone when she was young'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'be/get used to + V-ing' = be accustomed to: 'She is used to living alone.' Negative: didn't use to + V1.
✖ 'live' – V1 (base form); 'to living' – 'to + V-ing' (incorrect form here); 'living' – V-ing (gerund/participle) → 'used (past habit)' needs 'to + V1'.

q: Fill in the blank: By the time you return, my sister ___ a cake.
exp:
✔ 'By the time you return' भविष्य के उस समय को बताता है जिससे पहले कार्य पूरा हो चुका होगा, अतः Future Perfect (will have + V3) आएगा: 'By the time you return, my sister will have made a cake'।
📌 ध्यान दें: भविष्य के लिए 'by the time' वाले clause में Simple Present आता है ('by the time you return', न कि 'will return')।
✖ 'had made' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'has made' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'was making' – Past Continuous → भविष्य के किसी समय तक कार्य पूरा होना नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'By the time you return' refers to a point in the future before which the action will be complete, so Future Perfect (will have + V3) is used: 'By the time you return, my sister will have made a cake'.
📌 Note: in a 'by the time' clause about the future, Simple Present is used ('by the time you return', not 'will return'). e.g. 'By 2030, we will have built the bridge.'
✖ 'had made' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'has made' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'was making' – Past Continuous → does not show completion before a future time.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: We have been cooking the food for two hours.
exp:
✔ वाक्य 'We have been cooking the food for two hours' में संरचना has/have been + V-ing है, अतः यह Present Perfect Continuous Tense है।
📌 Present Perfect Continuous का प्रयोग भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब तक जारी कार्य (since/for) के लिए होता है। 'for two hours' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing; Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing।
expe:
✔ 'We have been cooking the food for two hours' follows the pattern has/have been + V-ing, so it is in the Present Perfect Continuous tense.
📌 Present Perfect Continuous is used for action begun in the past and still continuing (since/for). The phrase 'for two hours' is a signal.
✖ Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing; Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing.

q: Fill in the blank: Either her friends or Geeta ___ responsible for this loss.
exp:
✔ 'Either…or / Neither…nor' में verb निकटतम subject के अनुसार आता है (Rule of Proximity)। यहाँ निकटतम subject 'Geeta' है, इसलिए 'is' सही है: 'Either her friends or Geeta is responsible for this loss'।
📌 यही नियम 'Not only…but also' और 'or' पर लागू होता है। उदाहरण: 'Neither the teacher nor the students were present.'
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ With 'Either…or / Neither…nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject (Rule of Proximity). The nearer subject is 'Geeta', so 'is' is correct: 'Either her friends or Geeta is responsible for this loss'.
📌 Same rule for 'Not only…but also' and 'or'. Tip: put the plural subject nearer the verb, e.g. 'Neither the teacher nor the students were present.'
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

q: Fill in the blank: If it does not rain, Kishore ___ an essay.
exp:
✔ If-clause 'it does not rain' Simple Present में है, अतः यह Type-1 conditional (वास्तविक/संभव शर्त) है; main clause में 'will + V1' आएगा: 'If it does not rain, Kishore will write an essay'।
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'wrote' – V2 (Simple Past); 'would have written' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional); 'would write' – would + V1 (Type-2 conditional) → Type-1 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ The if-clause 'it does not rain' is in Simple Present, so this is a Type-1 conditional (real/possible future); the main clause takes 'will + V1': 'If it does not rain, Kishore will write an essay'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.
✖ 'wrote' – V2 (Simple Past); 'would have written' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional); 'would write' – would + V1 (Type-2 conditional) → does not match a Type-1 if-clause.

q: Fill in the blank: I would rather Arjun ___ the project now.

q: Fill in the blank: Geeta has got used to ___ in public.
exp:
✔ 'get used to' का अर्थ है 'आदी होना/आदत पड़ जाना'; यहाँ 'to' preposition है, इसलिए gerund (V-ing) आता है: 'Geeta has got used to speaking in public'।
📌 'used to + V1' से भ्रमित न हों – यह भूतकाल की आदत बताता है जो अब नहीं है: 'He used to smoke'।
✖ 'spoke' – V2 (Simple Past); 'to speak' – to-infinitive; 'speak' – V1 (base form) → 'get used to' के बाद प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ 'get used to' means 'be/become accustomed to'; here 'to' is a preposition, so a gerund (V-ing) follows: 'Geeta has got used to speaking in public'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'used to + V1' = past habit no longer true: 'He used to smoke' (he smoked earlier, not now).
✖ 'spoke' – V2 (Simple Past); 'to speak' – to-infinitive; 'speak' – V1 (base form) → not used after 'get used to'.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Anil will have been cooking dinner for two hours by noon.

✖ Simple Present = V1 / V1+s/es; Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing; Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing.

q: Fill in the blank: If the shop is open, Harish ___ the hall.
exp:
✔ If-clause 'the shop is open' Simple Present में है, अतः यह Type-1 conditional (वास्तविक/संभव शर्त) है; main clause में 'will + V1' आएगा: 'If the shop is open, Harish will decorate the hall'।
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।

q: Fill in the blank: My friends wish they ___ birds.
exp:

q: Fill in the blank: Sunita is used to ___ long distances.

q: Fill in the blank: This time next week, Asha ___ science.

✖ 'had been studying' – Past Perfect Continuous; 'was studying' – Past Continuous; 'has studied' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3) → does not show an action in progress at a future moment.

q: Fill in the blank: Neither Sunita nor the students ___ present at the meeting.
exp:
✔ 'Either…or / Neither…nor' में verb निकटतम subject के अनुसार आता है (Rule of Proximity)। यहाँ निकटतम subject 'the students' है, इसलिए 'were' सही है: 'Neither Sunita nor the students were present at the meeting'।
📌 यही नियम 'Not only…but also' और 'or' पर लागू होता है। उदाहरण: 'Neither the teacher nor the students were present.'
✖ 'was' – singular verb; 'has' – singular verb; 'is' – singular verb → plural subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:

📌 Same rule for 'Not only…but also' and 'or'. Tip: put the plural subject nearer the verb, e.g. 'Neither the teacher nor the students were present.'

q: Fill in the blank: Rakesh ___ tea for two days and is still at it.
exp:

📌 since → समय-बिंदु (since morning); for → अवधि (for two days)। Stative verbs (know, like, own) के साथ Present Perfect आता है: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'was making' – Past Continuous; 'is making' – Present Continuous; 'makes' – V1+s (Simple Present) → भूतकाल से अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'since/for + time' together with 'and is still at it' shows an action that began in the past and is still continuing, so Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) is used: 'Rakesh has been making tea for two days and is still at it'.
📌 since → point of time (since morning); for → period (for two days). Stative verbs (know, like, own) take Present Perfect instead: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'was making' – Past Continuous; 'is making' – Present Continuous; 'makes' – V1+s (Simple Present) → does not show an action continuing from the past till now.

expe:

✔ 'used to + V1' expresses a past habit or state that no longer exists: 'Rahul used to live alone when he was young'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'be/get used to + V-ing' = be accustomed to: 'She is used to living alone.' Negative: didn't use to + V1.
✖ 'live' – V1 (base form); 'living' – V-ing (gerund/participle); 'to living' – 'to + V-ing' (incorrect form here) → 'used (past habit)' needs 'to + V1'.
