q: Fill in the blank: Harish as well as the students ___ invited to the party.
exp:
✔ जब दो subjects 'as well as' से जुड़े हों, तो verb पहले subject ('Harish') के अनुसार आता है: 'Harish as well as the students was invited to the party'।
📌 यही नियम 'with, together with, along with, as well as, besides, in addition to' पर लागू होता है, जैसे 'The captain as well as the players was praised.'
✖ 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb; 'have' – plural verb → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ When two subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('Harish'): 'Harish as well as the students was invited to the party'.
📌 Same rule for 'with, together with, along with, as well as, besides, in addition to, including', e.g. 'The captain as well as the players was praised.'
✖ 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb; 'have' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

q: Fill in the blank: Kavita ___ two poems since last night and is still at it.
exp:
✔ 'since/for + समय' तथा 'and is still at it' (अभी भी जारी है) बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब भी चल रहा है, अतः Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) आएगा: 'Kavita has been writing two poems since last night and is still at it'।
📌 since → समय-बिंदु (since morning); for → अवधि (for two days)। Stative verbs (know, like, own) के साथ Present Perfect आता है: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'was writing' – Past Continuous; 'is writing' – Present Continuous; 'writes' – V1+s (Simple Present) → भूतकाल से अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'since/for + time' together with 'and is still at it' shows an action that began in the past and is still continuing, so Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) is used: 'Kavita has been writing two poems since last night and is still at it'.
📌 since → point of time (since morning); for → period (for two days). Stative verbs (know, like, own) take Present Perfect instead: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'was writing' – Past Continuous; 'is writing' – Present Continuous; 'writes' – V1+s (Simple Present) → does not show an action continuing from the past till now.

q: Fill in the blank: If the guests leave early, Sita ___ the notice.
exp:
✔ If-clause 'the guests leave early' Simple Present में है, अतः यह Type-1 conditional (वास्तविक/संभव शर्त) है; main clause में 'will + V1' आएगा: 'If the guests leave early, Sita will type the notice'।
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'typed' – V2 (Simple Past); 'would type' – would + V1 (Type-2 conditional); 'would have typed' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional) → Type-1 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ The if-clause 'the guests leave early' is in Simple Present, so this is a Type-1 conditional (real/possible future); the main clause takes 'will + V1': 'If the guests leave early, Sita will type the notice'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.
✖ 'typed' – V2 (Simple Past); 'would type' – would + V1 (Type-2 conditional); 'would have typed' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional) → does not match a Type-1 if-clause.

q: Fill in the blank: Usha wishes she ___ a bird.
exp:
✔ 'wish' द्वारा अवास्तविक/असंभव इच्छा व्यक्त करने पर past subjunctive आता है; सभी subjects के साथ 'were' प्रयोग होता है: 'Usha wishes she were a bird'।
📌 इसी प्रकार: 'If I were a bird, I would fly.' भूतकाल का पछतावा: wish + had + V3 – 'I wish I had gone.'
✖ 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been); 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'will be' – Simple Future (will be) → इस संरचना में प्रयोग नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'wish' expressing an unreal/impossible present wish takes the past subjunctive; 'were' is used with all subjects: 'Usha wishes she were a bird'.
📌 Similar: 'If I were a bird, I would fly.' Regret about the past: wish + had + V3 – 'I wish I had gone.'
✖ 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been); 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'will be' – Simple Future (will be) → not used in this structure.

q: Fill in the blank: Kishore has got used to ___ in public.
exp:
✔ 'get used to' का अर्थ है 'आदी होना/आदत पड़ जाना'; यहाँ 'to' preposition है, इसलिए gerund (V-ing) आता है: 'Kishore has got used to speaking in public'।
📌 'used to + V1' से भ्रमित न हों – यह भूतकाल की आदत बताता है जो अब नहीं है: 'He used to smoke'।
✖ 'to speak' – to-infinitive; 'spoke' – V2 (Simple Past); 'speak' – V1 (base form) → 'get used to' के बाद प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ 'get used to' means 'be/become accustomed to'; here 'to' is a preposition, so a gerund (V-ing) follows: 'Kishore has got used to speaking in public'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'used to + V1' = past habit no longer true: 'He used to smoke' (he smoked earlier, not now).
✖ 'to speak' – to-infinitive; 'spoke' – V2 (Simple Past); 'speak' – V1 (base form) → not used after 'get used to'.

q: Fill in the blank: By next Monday, Seema ___ a kite.
exp:
✔ 'By next Monday' भविष्य के उस समय को बताता है जिससे पहले कार्य पूरा हो चुका होगा, अतः Future Perfect (will have + V3) आएगा: 'By next Monday, Seema will have made a kite'।
📌 ध्यान दें: भविष्य के लिए 'by the time' वाले clause में Simple Present आता है ('by the time you return', न कि 'will return')।
✖ 'had made' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'has made' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'was making' – Past Continuous → भविष्य के किसी समय तक कार्य पूरा होना नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'By next Monday' refers to a point in the future before which the action will be complete, so Future Perfect (will have + V3) is used: 'By next Monday, Seema will have made a kite'.
📌 Note: in a 'by the time' clause about the future, Simple Present is used ('by the time you return', not 'will return'). e.g. 'By 2030, we will have built the bridge.'
✖ 'had made' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'has made' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'was making' – Past Continuous → does not show completion before a future time.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Anil had been painting a picture for two hours before we came.
exp:
✔ वाक्य 'Anil had been painting a picture for two hours before we came' में संरचना had been + V-ing है, अतः यह Past Perfect Continuous Tense है।
📌 Past Perfect Continuous का प्रयोग किसी भूतकालिक कार्य से पहले कुछ समय से चल रहा कार्य के लिए होता है। 'for two hours' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing; Past Perfect = had + V3; Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing।
expe:
✔ 'Anil had been painting a picture for two hours before we came' follows the pattern had been + V-ing, so it is in the Past Perfect Continuous tense.
📌 Past Perfect Continuous is used for action continuing for a period before another past action. The phrase 'for two hours' is a signal.
✖ Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing; Past Perfect = had + V3; Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing.

q: Fill in the blank: Neither her sisters nor Anita ___ present at the meeting.
exp:
✔ 'Either…or / Neither…nor' में verb निकटतम subject के अनुसार आता है (Rule of Proximity)। यहाँ निकटतम subject 'Anita' है, इसलिए 'was' सही है: 'Neither her sisters nor Anita was present at the meeting'।
📌 यही नियम 'Not only…but also' और 'or' पर लागू होता है। उदाहरण: 'Neither the teacher nor the students were present.'
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ With 'Either…or / Neither…nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject (Rule of Proximity). The nearer subject is 'Anita', so 'was' is correct: 'Neither her sisters nor Anita was present at the meeting'.
📌 Same rule for 'Not only…but also' and 'or'. Tip: put the plural subject nearer the verb, e.g. 'Neither the teacher nor the students were present.'
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

q: Fill in the blank: If the manager had agreed, Ajay ___ the poor.
exp:
✔ If-clause 'the manager had agreed' Past Perfect (had + V3) में है, अतः यह Type-3 conditional (भूतकाल की अवास्तविक शर्त) है; main clause में 'would have + V3' आएगा: 'If the manager had agreed, Ajay would have helped the poor'।
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'had helped' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'will help' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'will have helped' – Future Perfect (will have + V3) → Type-3 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ The if-clause 'the manager had agreed' is in Past Perfect (had + V3), so this is a Type-3 conditional (unreal past); the main clause takes 'would have + V3': 'If the manager had agreed, Ajay would have helped the poor'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.
✖ 'had helped' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'will help' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'will have helped' – Future Perfect (will have + V3) → does not match a Type-3 if-clause.

q: Fill in the blank: Rakesh talks as if he ___ the owner of this shop.
exp:
✔ 'as if / as though' काल्पनिक स्थिति (वास्तव में वे मालिक नहीं हैं) बताने पर सभी subjects के साथ past subjunctive 'were' आता है: 'Rakesh talks as if he were the owner of this shop'।
📌 यही नियम 'wish' के बाद और 'If I were…' में लागू होता है। जैसे 'He behaves as if he were a king.'
✖ 'will be' – Simple Future (will be); 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been) → इस संरचना में प्रयोग नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'as if / as though' describing an imaginary situation (they are not really the owners) takes the past subjunctive 'were' with all subjects: 'Rakesh talks as if he were the owner of this shop'.
📌 Same rule after 'wish' and in Type-2 'If I were…'. e.g. 'He behaves as if he were a king.'
✖ 'will be' – Simple Future (will be); 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been) → not used in this structure.

q: Fill in the blank: Vijay used ___ in heavy traffic when he was young.
exp:
✔ 'used to + V1' भूतकाल की ऐसी आदत/स्थिति बताता है जो अब नहीं है: 'Vijay used to drive in heavy traffic when he was young'।
📌 'be/get used to + V-ing' (आदी होना) से भ्रमित न हों: 'She is used to living alone.' Negative: didn't use to + V1।
✖ 'driving' – V-ing (gerund/participle); 'drive' – V1 (base form); 'to driving' – 'to + V-ing' (यहाँ गलत रूप) → 'used (past habit)' के बाद 'to + V1' चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'used to + V1' expresses a past habit or state that no longer exists: 'Vijay used to drive in heavy traffic when he was young'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'be/get used to + V-ing' = be accustomed to: 'She is used to living alone.' Negative: didn't use to + V1.
✖ 'driving' – V-ing (gerund/participle); 'drive' – V1 (base form); 'to driving' – 'to + V-ing' (incorrect form here) → 'used (past habit)' needs 'to + V1'.

✔ 'By the time you return' refers to a point in the future before which the action will be complete, so Future Perfect (will have + V3) is used: 'By the time you return, he will have read the notice'.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Suresh will have played chess by tomorrow.
exp:
✔ वाक्य 'Suresh will have played chess by tomorrow' में संरचना will/shall have + V3 है, अतः यह Future Perfect Tense है।
📌 Future Perfect का प्रयोग भविष्य के किसी समय तक पूरे हो चुके कार्य (by ...) के लिए होता है। 'by tomorrow' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Past Perfect = had + V3; Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing।
expe:
✔ 'Suresh will have played chess by tomorrow' follows the pattern will/shall have + V3, so it is in the Future Perfect tense.
📌 Future Perfect is used for action completed before a future point (by ...). The phrase 'by tomorrow' is a signal.
✖ Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Past Perfect = had + V3; Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing.

q: Fill in the blank: Neither of the two children ___ selected.
exp:
✔ 'Neither of the + plural noun' (दोनों में से कोई नहीं) के साथ मानक व्याकरण में singular verb आता है: 'Neither of the two children was selected'।
📌 इसी प्रकार 'Either of', 'Each of' singular verb लेते हैं। 'Neither/Either' दो के लिए; दो से अधिक के लिए 'none/any' प्रयोग होता है।
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'Neither of the + plural noun' (not one of the two) takes a singular verb in standard grammar: 'Neither of the two children was selected'.
📌 Similarly 'Either of' and 'Each of' take singular verbs. 'Neither/Either' are used for two persons/things; for more than two use 'none/any'.
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: The workers will be planting trees at this time tomorrow.
exp:
✔ वाक्य 'The workers will be planting trees at this time tomorrow' में संरचना will/shall be + V-ing है, अतः यह Future Continuous Tense है।
📌 Future Continuous का प्रयोग भविष्य में किसी निश्चित समय पर चल रहे कार्य के लिए होता है। 'at this time tomorrow' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing; Simple Present = V1 / V1+s/es; Present Perfect = has/have + V3।
expe:
✔ 'The workers will be planting trees at this time tomorrow' follows the pattern will/shall be + V-ing, so it is in the Future Continuous tense.
📌 Future Continuous is used for action in progress at a future moment. The phrase 'at this time tomorrow' is a signal.
✖ Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing; Simple Present = V1 / V1+s/es; Present Perfect = has/have + V3.

q: Fill in the blank: Her friends as well as Pooja ___ invited to the party.
exp:
✔ जब दो subjects 'as well as' से जुड़े हों, तो verb पहले subject ('Her friends') के अनुसार आता है: 'Her friends as well as Pooja were invited to the party'।
📌 यही नियम 'with, together with, along with, as well as, besides, in addition to' पर लागू होता है, जैसे 'The captain as well as the players was praised.'
✖ 'was' – singular verb; 'has' – singular verb; 'is' – singular verb → plural subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ When two subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('Her friends'): 'Her friends as well as Pooja were invited to the party'.
📌 Same rule for 'with, together with, along with, as well as, besides, in addition to, including', e.g. 'The captain as well as the players was praised.'
✖ 'was' – singular verb; 'has' – singular verb; 'is' – singular verb → does not agree with a plural subject.

q: Fill in the blank: Harish ___ a plan for an hour and is still at it.
exp:
✔ 'since/for + समय' तथा 'and is still at it' (अभी भी जारी है) बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब भी चल रहा है, अतः Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) आएगा: 'Harish has been preparing a plan for an hour and is still at it'।
📌 since → समय-बिंदु (since morning); for → अवधि (for two days)। Stative verbs (know, like, own) के साथ Present Perfect आता है: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'prepares' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'is preparing' – Present Continuous; 'was preparing' – Past Continuous → भूतकाल से अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'since/for + time' together with 'and is still at it' shows an action that began in the past and is still continuing, so Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) is used: 'Harish has been preparing a plan for an hour and is still at it'.
📌 since → point of time (since morning); for → period (for two days). Stative verbs (know, like, own) take Present Perfect instead: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'prepares' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'is preparing' – Present Continuous; 'was preparing' – Past Continuous → does not show an action continuing from the past till now.

q: Fill in the blank: If the money arrives, the boys ___ some apples.
exp:
✔ If-clause 'the money arrives' Simple Present में है, अतः यह Type-1 conditional (वास्तविक/संभव शर्त) है; main clause में 'will + V1' आएगा: 'If the money arrives, the boys will buy some apples'।
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'bought' – V2 (Simple Past); 'would buy' – would + V1 (Type-2 conditional); 'would have bought' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional) → Type-1 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ The if-clause 'the money arrives' is in Simple Present, so this is a Type-1 conditional (real/possible future); the main clause takes 'will + V1': 'If the money arrives, the boys will buy some apples'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.
✖ 'bought' – V2 (Simple Past); 'would buy' – would + V1 (Type-2 conditional); 'would have bought' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional) → does not match a Type-1 if-clause.

q: Fill in the blank: It is high time Shalini ___ the chairs.
exp:
✔ 'It is high time + subject + V2 (Simple Past)' बताता है कि कार्य का समय पहले ही हो चुका है (देर हो रही है): 'It is high time Shalini arranged the chairs'।
📌 विकल्प: 'It is time + to-infinitive' – 'It is time to go.' 'would rather + subject' के बाद भी V2 आता है।
✖ 'arrange' – V1 (base form); 'has arranged' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'will arrange' – Simple Future (will + V1) → इस संरचना में प्रयोग नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'It is high time + subject + V2 (Simple Past)' shows that the action is already overdue: 'It is high time Shalini arranged the chairs'.
📌 Alternative: 'It is time + to-infinitive' – 'It is time to go.' Same past form after 'would rather + subject'.
✖ 'arrange' – V1 (base form); 'has arranged' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'will arrange' – Simple Future (will + V1) → not used in this structure.

q: Fill in the blank: Harish used ___ in public when he was young.
exp:
✔ 'used to + V1' भूतकाल की ऐसी आदत/स्थिति बताता है जो अब नहीं है: 'Harish used to speak in public when he was young'।
📌 'be/get used to + V-ing' (आदी होना) से भ्रमित न हों: 'She is used to living alone.' Negative: didn't use to + V1।
✖ 'to speaking' – 'to + V-ing' (यहाँ गलत रूप); 'speaking' – V-ing (gerund/participle); 'speak' – V1 (base form) → 'used (past habit)' के बाद 'to + V1' चाहिए।
expe:
✔ 'used to + V1' expresses a past habit or state that no longer exists: 'Harish used to speak in public when he was young'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'be/get used to + V-ing' = be accustomed to: 'She is used to living alone.' Negative: didn't use to + V1.
✖ 'to speaking' – 'to + V-ing' (incorrect form here); 'speaking' – V-ing (gerund/participle); 'speak' – V1 (base form) → 'used (past habit)' needs 'to + V1'.

q: Fill in the blank: By this evening, Divya ___ the project.
exp:
✔ 'By this evening' भविष्य के उस समय को बताता है जिससे पहले कार्य पूरा हो चुका होगा, अतः Future Perfect (will have + V3) आएगा: 'By this evening, Divya will have finished the project'।
📌 ध्यान दें: भविष्य के लिए 'by the time' वाले clause में Simple Present आता है ('by the time you return', न कि 'will return')।
✖ 'had finished' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'was finishing' – Past Continuous; 'has finished' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3) → भविष्य के किसी समय तक कार्य पूरा होना नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'By this evening' refers to a point in the future before which the action will be complete, so Future Perfect (will have + V3) is used: 'By this evening, Divya will have finished the project'.
📌 Note: in a 'by the time' clause about the future, Simple Present is used ('by the time you return', not 'will return'). e.g. 'By 2030, we will have built the bridge.'
✖ 'had finished' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'was finishing' – Past Continuous; 'has finished' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3) → does not show completion before a future time.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Manoj had played football before we came.
exp:
✔ वाक्य 'Manoj had played football before we came' में संरचना had + V3 है, अतः यह Past Perfect Tense है।
📌 Past Perfect का प्रयोग दो भूतकालिक कार्यों में पहले पूरा हुआ कार्य के लिए होता है। 'before we came' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing; Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Simple Past = V2।
expe:
✔ 'Manoj had played football before we came' follows the pattern had + V3, so it is in the Past Perfect tense.
📌 Past Perfect is used for the earlier of two past actions. The phrase 'before we came' is a signal.
✖ Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing; Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Simple Past = V2.

q: Fill in the blank: Not only Vikas but also his sisters ___ been punished.
exp:
✔ 'Not only…but also' में verb 'but also' के बाद वाले (निकटतम) subject के अनुसार आता है – यहाँ 'his sisters' (plural): 'Not only Vikas but also his sisters have been punished'।
📌 Rule of Proximity 'Either…or' और 'Neither…nor' पर भी लागू होता है।
✖ 'is' – singular verb; 'has' – singular verb; 'was' – singular verb → plural subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ With 'Not only…but also' the verb agrees with the subject after 'but also' (nearer subject) – here 'his sisters' (plural): 'Not only Vikas but also his sisters have been punished'.
📌 The Rule of Proximity also applies to 'Either…or' and 'Neither…nor'.
✖ 'is' – singular verb; 'has' – singular verb; 'was' – singular verb → does not agree with a plural subject.

q: Fill in the blank: If it did not rain, the villagers ___ vegetables.
exp:
✔ If-clause 'it did not rain' Simple Past में है, अतः यह Type-2 conditional (काल्पनिक/कम संभावित स्थिति) है; main clause में 'would + V1' आएगा: 'If it did not rain, the villagers would buy vegetables'।
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'will have bought' – Future Perfect (will have + V3); 'will buy' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'would have bought' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional) → Type-2 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ The if-clause 'it did not rain' is in Simple Past, so this is a Type-2 conditional (imaginary/unlikely present); the main clause takes 'would + V1': 'If it did not rain, the villagers would buy vegetables'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.
✖ 'will have bought' – Future Perfect (will have + V3); 'will buy' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'would have bought' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional) → does not match a Type-2 if-clause.

q: Fill in the blank: Meena talks as if she ___ the owner of this shop.
exp:
✔ 'as if / as though' काल्पनिक स्थिति (वास्तव में वे मालिक नहीं हैं) बताने पर सभी subjects के साथ past subjunctive 'were' आता है: 'Meena talks as if she were the owner of this shop'।
📌 यही नियम 'wish' के बाद और 'If I were…' में लागू होता है। जैसे 'He behaves as if he were a king.'
✖ 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been); 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'will be' – Simple Future (will be) → इस संरचना में प्रयोग नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'as if / as though' describing an imaginary situation (they are not really the owners) takes the past subjunctive 'were' with all subjects: 'Meena talks as if she were the owner of this shop'.
📌 Same rule after 'wish' and in Type-2 'If I were…'. e.g. 'He behaves as if he were a king.'
✖ 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been); 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'will be' – Simple Future (will be) → not used in this structure.

q: Fill in the blank: Gopal has got used to ___ spicy food.
exp:
✔ 'get used to' का अर्थ है 'आदी होना/आदत पड़ जाना'; यहाँ 'to' preposition है, इसलिए gerund (V-ing) आता है: 'Gopal has got used to eating spicy food'।
📌 'used to + V1' से भ्रमित न हों – यह भूतकाल की आदत बताता है जो अब नहीं है: 'He used to smoke'।
✖ 'to eat' – to-infinitive; 'ate' – V2 (Simple Past); 'eat' – V1 (base form) → 'get used to' के बाद प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ 'get used to' means 'be/become accustomed to'; here 'to' is a preposition, so a gerund (V-ing) follows: 'Gopal has got used to eating spicy food'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'used to + V1' = past habit no longer true: 'He used to smoke' (he smoked earlier, not now).
✖ 'to eat' – to-infinitive; 'ate' – V2 (Simple Past); 'eat' – V1 (base form) → not used after 'get used to'.

q: Fill in the blank: This time next week, my parents ___ the meal.
exp:
✔ 'This time next week' भविष्य के एक निश्चित क्षण को बताता है जब कार्य चल रहा होगा, अतः Future Continuous (will be + V-ing) आएगा: 'This time next week, my parents will be preparing the meal'।
📌 संकेत-शब्द: this time tomorrow/next week, at 5 pm tomorrow। पूर्णता के लिए Future Perfect (will have + V3): 'By tomorrow I will have finished.'
✖ 'had been preparing' – Past Perfect Continuous; 'were preparing' – Past Continuous; 'have prepared' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3) → भविष्य में चल रहे कार्य को नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'This time next week' points to a specific moment in the future at which the action will be in progress, so Future Continuous (will be + V-ing) is used: 'This time next week, my parents will be preparing the meal'.
📌 Signal phrases: this time tomorrow/next week, at 5 pm tomorrow. Compare Future Perfect (will have + V3) for completion: 'By tomorrow I will have finished.'
✖ 'had been preparing' – Past Perfect Continuous; 'were preparing' – Past Continuous; 'have prepared' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3) → does not show an action in progress at a future moment.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Geeta had been baking bread for two hours before we came.
exp:
✔ वाक्य 'Geeta had been baking bread for two hours before we came' में संरचना had been + V-ing है, अतः यह Past Perfect Continuous Tense है।
📌 Past Perfect Continuous का प्रयोग किसी भूतकालिक कार्य से पहले कुछ समय से चल रहा कार्य के लिए होता है। 'for two hours' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Past Perfect = had + V3; Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing; Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing।
expe:
✔ 'Geeta had been baking bread for two hours before we came' follows the pattern had been + V-ing, so it is in the Past Perfect Continuous tense.
📌 Past Perfect Continuous is used for action continuing for a period before another past action. The phrase 'for two hours' is a signal.
✖ Past Perfect = had + V3; Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing; Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing.

q: Fill in the blank: Slow and steady ___ the race.
exp:
✔ जब 'and' से जुड़े दो शब्द एक ही विचार को व्यक्त करें, तो subject singular माना जाता है और verb singular आता है: 'Slow and steady wins the race'।
📌 अन्य उदाहरण: 'Bread and butter is my breakfast', 'Time and tide waits for no man'। यह सार्वभौमिक सत्य है, अतः Simple Present (wins)।
✖ 'win' – V1 (base form); 'have won' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'winning' – V-ing (gerund/participle) → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ When two words joined by 'and' express a single idea, the subject is singular, so the verb is singular: 'Slow and steady wins the race'.
📌 Other examples: 'Bread and butter is my breakfast', 'Time and tide waits for no man'. It is a general truth, so Simple Present (wins).
✖ 'win' – V1 (base form); 'have won' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'winning' – V-ing (gerund/participle) → does not agree with a singular subject.

expe:

q: Fill in the blank: If the manager had agreed, the farmer ___ the chairs.
exp:
✔ If-clause 'the manager had agreed' Past Perfect (had + V3) में है, अतः यह Type-3 conditional (भूतकाल की अवास्तविक शर्त) है; main clause में 'would have + V3' आएगा: 'If the manager had agreed, the farmer would have arranged the chairs'।
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'will arrange' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'had arranged' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'will have arranged' – Future Perfect (will have + V3) → Type-3 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ The if-clause 'the manager had agreed' is in Past Perfect (had + V3), so this is a Type-3 conditional (unreal past); the main clause takes 'would have + V3': 'If the manager had agreed, the farmer would have arranged the chairs'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.
✖ 'will arrange' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'had arranged' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'will have arranged' – Future Perfect (will have + V3) → does not match a Type-3 if-clause.

q: Fill in the blank: Divya wishes she ___ a bird.
exp:
✔ 'wish' द्वारा अवास्तविक/असंभव इच्छा व्यक्त करने पर past subjunctive आता है; सभी subjects के साथ 'were' प्रयोग होता है: 'Divya wishes she were a bird'।
📌 इसी प्रकार: 'If I were a bird, I would fly.' भूतकाल का पछतावा: wish + had + V3 – 'I wish I had gone.'
✖ 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'will be' – Simple Future (will be); 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been) → इस संरचना में प्रयोग नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'wish' expressing an unreal/impossible present wish takes the past subjunctive; 'were' is used with all subjects: 'Divya wishes she were a bird'.
📌 Similar: 'If I were a bird, I would fly.' Regret about the past: wish + had + V3 – 'I wish I had gone.'
✖ 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'will be' – Simple Future (will be); 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been) → not used in this structure.

q: Fill in the blank: Anita has got used to ___ under pressure.
exp:
✔ 'get used to' का अर्थ है 'आदी होना/आदत पड़ जाना'; यहाँ 'to' preposition है, इसलिए gerund (V-ing) आता है: 'Anita has got used to working under pressure'।

✖ 'worked' – V2 (Simple Past); 'work' – V1 (base form); 'to work' – to-infinitive → 'get used to' के बाद प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ 'get used to' means 'be/become accustomed to'; here 'to' is a preposition, so a gerund (V-ing) follows: 'Anita has got used to working under pressure'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'used to + V1' = past habit no longer true: 'He used to smoke' (he smoked earlier, not now).
✖ 'worked' – V2 (Simple Past); 'work' – V1 (base form); 'to work' – to-infinitive → not used after 'get used to'.

q: Fill in the blank: By next March, the student ___ two poems.
exp:
✔ 'By next March' भविष्य के उस समय को बताता है जिससे पहले कार्य पूरा हो चुका होगा, अतः Future Perfect (will have + V3) आएगा: 'By next March, the student will have written two poems'।
📌 ध्यान दें: भविष्य के लिए 'by the time' वाले clause में Simple Present आता है ('by the time you return', न कि 'will return')।
✖ 'wrote' – V2 (Simple Past); 'has written' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'had written' – Past Perfect (had + V3) → भविष्य के किसी समय तक कार्य पूरा होना नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'By next March' refers to a point in the future before which the action will be complete, so Future Perfect (will have + V3) is used: 'By next March, the student will have written two poems'.
📌 Note: in a 'by the time' clause about the future, Simple Present is used ('by the time you return', not 'will return'). e.g. 'By 2030, we will have built the bridge.'
✖ 'wrote' – V2 (Simple Past); 'has written' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'had written' – Past Perfect (had + V3) → does not show completion before a future time.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Ajay has been reading these books for two hours.
exp:
✔ वाक्य 'Ajay has been reading these books for two hours' में संरचना has/have been + V-ing है, अतः यह Present Perfect Continuous Tense है।
📌 Present Perfect Continuous का प्रयोग भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब तक जारी कार्य (since/for) के लिए होता है। 'for two hours' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing; Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing।
expe:
✔ 'Ajay has been reading these books for two hours' follows the pattern has/have been + V-ing, so it is in the Present Perfect Continuous tense.
📌 Present Perfect Continuous is used for action begun in the past and still continuing (since/for). The phrase 'for two hours' is a signal.
✖ Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing; Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing.

q: Fill in the blank: Neither of the two clerks ___ selected.
exp:
✔ 'Neither of the + plural noun' (दोनों में से कोई नहीं) के साथ मानक व्याकरण में singular verb आता है: 'Neither of the two clerks was selected'।
📌 इसी प्रकार 'Either of', 'Each of' singular verb लेते हैं। 'Neither/Either' दो के लिए; दो से अधिक के लिए 'none/any' प्रयोग होता है।
✖ 'were' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'have' – plural verb → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'Neither of the + plural noun' (not one of the two) takes a singular verb in standard grammar: 'Neither of the two clerks was selected'.
📌 Similarly 'Either of' and 'Each of' take singular verbs. 'Neither/Either' are used for two persons/things; for more than two use 'none/any'.
✖ 'were' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'have' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

q: Fill in the blank: Rakesh ___ a picture since Monday and is still at it.
exp:
✔ 'since/for + समय' तथा 'and is still at it' (अभी भी जारी है) बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब भी चल रहा है, अतः Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) आएगा: 'Rakesh has been painting a picture since Monday and is still at it'।
📌 since → समय-बिंदु (since morning); for → अवधि (for two days)। Stative verbs (know, like, own) के साथ Present Perfect आता है: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'is painting' – Present Continuous; 'was painting' – Past Continuous; 'paints' – V1+s (Simple Present) → भूतकाल से अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'since/for + time' together with 'and is still at it' shows an action that began in the past and is still continuing, so Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) is used: 'Rakesh has been painting a picture since Monday and is still at it'.
📌 since → point of time (since morning); for → period (for two days). Stative verbs (know, like, own) take Present Perfect instead: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'is painting' – Present Continuous; 'was painting' – Past Continuous; 'paints' – V1+s (Simple Present) → does not show an action continuing from the past till now.

q: Fill in the blank: If the guests left early, Neha ___ the newspaper.
exp:
✔ If-clause 'the guests left early' Simple Past में है, अतः यह Type-2 conditional (काल्पनिक/कम संभावित स्थिति) है; main clause में 'would + V1' आएगा: 'If the guests left early, Neha would read the newspaper'।
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'would have read' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional); 'will have read' – Future Perfect (will have + V3); 'will read' – Simple Future (will + V1) → Type-2 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ The if-clause 'the guests left early' is in Simple Past, so this is a Type-2 conditional (imaginary/unlikely present); the main clause takes 'would + V1': 'If the guests left early, Neha would read the newspaper'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.
✖ 'would have read' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional); 'will have read' – Future Perfect (will have + V3); 'will read' – Simple Future (will + V1) → does not match a Type-2 if-clause.

q: Fill in the blank: The girl wishes she ___ a bird.
exp:
✔ 'wish' द्वारा अवास्तविक/असंभव इच्छा व्यक्त करने पर past subjunctive आता है; सभी subjects के साथ 'were' प्रयोग होता है: 'The girl wishes she were a bird'।
📌 इसी प्रकार: 'If I were a bird, I would fly.' भूतकाल का पछतावा: wish + had + V3 – 'I wish I had gone.'
✖ 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been); 'will be' – Simple Future (will be) → इस संरचना में प्रयोग नहीं।
expe:
✔ 'wish' expressing an unreal/impossible present wish takes the past subjunctive; 'were' is used with all subjects: 'The girl wishes she were a bird'.
📌 Similar: 'If I were a bird, I would fly.' Regret about the past: wish + had + V3 – 'I wish I had gone.'
✖ 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been); 'will be' – Simple Future (will be) → not used in this structure.

q: Fill in the blank: Usha is used to ___ late at night.
exp:
✔ 'be used to' का अर्थ है 'आदी होना/आदत पड़ जाना'; यहाँ 'to' preposition है, इसलिए gerund (V-ing) आता है: 'Usha is used to reading late at night'।
📌 'used to + V1' से भ्रमित न हों – यह भूतकाल की आदत बताता है जो अब नहीं है: 'He used to smoke'।
✖ 'to read' – to-infinitive; 'reads' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'read' – V1 (base form) → 'be used to' के बाद प्रयोग नहीं होता।
expe:
✔ 'be used to' means 'be/become accustomed to'; here 'to' is a preposition, so a gerund (V-ing) follows: 'Usha is used to reading late at night'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'used to + V1' = past habit no longer true: 'He used to smoke' (he smoked earlier, not now).
✖ 'to read' – to-infinitive; 'reads' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'read' – V1 (base form) → not used after 'be used to'.

q: Fill in the blank: This time tomorrow, Anil ___ the notice.
exp:
✔ 'This time tomorrow' भविष्य के एक निश्चित क्षण को बताता है जब कार्य चल रहा होगा, अतः Future Continuous (will be + V-ing) आएगा: 'This time tomorrow, Anil will be reading the notice'।
📌 संकेत-शब्द: this time tomorrow/next week, at 5 pm tomorrow। पूर्णता के लिए Future Perfect (will have + V3): 'By tomorrow I will have finished.'
✖ 'had been reading' – Past Perfect Continuous; 'has read' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'was reading' – Past Continuous → भविष्य में चल रहे कार्य को नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'This time tomorrow' points to a specific moment in the future at which the action will be in progress, so Future Continuous (will be + V-ing) is used: 'This time tomorrow, Anil will be reading the notice'.
📌 Signal phrases: this time tomorrow/next week, at 5 pm tomorrow. Compare Future Perfect (will have + V3) for completion: 'By tomorrow I will have finished.'
✖ 'had been reading' – Past Perfect Continuous; 'has read' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'was reading' – Past Continuous → does not show an action in progress at a future moment.

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Sunita had opened the door before we came.
exp:
✔ वाक्य 'Sunita had opened the door before we came' में संरचना had + V3 है, अतः यह Past Perfect Tense है।
📌 Past Perfect का प्रयोग दो भूतकालिक कार्यों में पहले पूरा हुआ कार्य के लिए होता है। 'before we came' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing; Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Simple Past = V2।
expe:
✔ 'Sunita had opened the door before we came' follows the pattern had + V3, so it is in the Past Perfect tense.
📌 Past Perfect is used for the earlier of two past actions. The phrase 'before we came' is a signal.
✖ Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing; Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Simple Past = V2.

q: Fill in the blank: Rahul along with the students ___ gone to Betul.
exp:
✔ जब दो subjects 'along with' से जुड़े हों, तो verb पहले subject ('Rahul') के अनुसार आता है: 'Rahul along with the students has gone to Betul'।
📌 यही नियम 'with, together with, along with, as well as, besides, in addition to' पर लागू होता है, जैसे 'The captain as well as the players was praised.'
✖ 'were' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'have' – plural verb → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ When two subjects are joined by 'along with', the verb agrees with the first subject ('Rahul'): 'Rahul along with the students has gone to Betul'.
📌 Same rule for 'with, together with, along with, as well as, besides, in addition to, including', e.g. 'The captain as well as the players was praised.'
✖ 'were' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'have' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

q: Fill in the blank: The boy ___ the house since last night and is still at it.
exp:
✔ 'since/for + समय' तथा 'and is still at it' (अभी भी जारी है) बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब भी चल रहा है, अतः Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) आएगा: 'The boy has been decorating the house since last night and is still at it'।
📌 since → समय-बिंदु (since morning); for → अवधि (for two days)। Stative verbs (know, like, own) के साथ Present Perfect आता है: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'decorates' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'was decorating' – Past Continuous; 'is decorating' – Present Continuous → भूतकाल से अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं दर्शाता।
expe:
✔ 'since/for + time' together with 'and is still at it' shows an action that began in the past and is still continuing, so Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) is used: 'The boy has been decorating the house since last night and is still at it'.
📌 since → point of time (since morning); for → period (for two days). Stative verbs (know, like, own) take Present Perfect instead: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'decorates' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'was decorating' – Past Continuous; 'is decorating' – Present Continuous → does not show an action continuing from the past till now.

q: Fill in the blank: If the guests left early, the girls ___ the project.
exp:
✔ If-clause 'the guests left early' Simple Past में है, अतः यह Type-2 conditional (काल्पनिक/कम संभावित स्थिति) है; main clause में 'would + V1' आएगा: 'If the guests left early, the girls would finish the project'।
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'will finish' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'will have finished' – Future Perfect (will have + V3); 'would have finished' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional) → Type-2 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
expe:
✔ The if-clause 'the guests left early' is in Simple Past, so this is a Type-2 conditional (imaginary/unlikely present); the main clause takes 'would + V1': 'If the guests left early, the girls would finish the project'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.
✖ 'will finish' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'will have finished' – Future Perfect (will have + V3); 'would have finished' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional) → does not match a Type-2 if-clause.

q: Fill in the blank: It is high time Rakesh ___ an essay.
exp:
✔ ‘It is high time’ के बाद subject + V2 (past subjunctive) आता है, भले अर्थ वर्तमान का हो। अतः सही वाक्य: “It is high time Rakesh wrote an essay.”
📌 इसी नियम पर: It is time / It is about time + V2; या It is high time + for + object + to + V1 (It is high time for him to go)।
✖ B) has written (Present Perfect) — high time के बाद यह रूप नहीं आता; C) will write (Simple Future) — high time के बाद यह रूप नहीं आता; D) write (V1 (base form)) — high time के बाद यह रूप नहीं आता
expe:
✔ ‘It is high time’ is followed by subject + V2 (past subjunctive) though the meaning is present. Correct: “It is high time Rakesh wrote an essay.”
📌 Same rule: It is time / It is about time + V2; alternatively It is high time + for + object + to + V1 (It is high time for him to go).
✖ B) has written (Present Perfect) — not used after 'high time'; C) will write (Simple Future) — not used after 'high time'; D) write (V1 (base form)) — not used after 'high time'

q: Fill in the blank: The farmer has got used to ___ late at night.
exp:
✔ ‘be/get used to’ (आदी होना) में ‘to’ preposition है, इसलिए इसके बाद gerund (V-ing) आता है: “The farmer has got used to reading late at night.”
📌 अंतर याद रखें: used to + V1 = past की आदत (He used to smoke); be used to + V-ing = आदी होना (He is used to smoking)। इसी तरह look forward to / object to + V-ing।
✖ A) read (V1 form) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए; C) reads (V1 + s (Simple Present)) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए; D) to read (to + V1 (infinitive)) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए
expe:
✔ In ‘be/get used to’ (= accustomed to), ‘to’ is a preposition, so it takes a gerund (V-ing): “The farmer has got used to reading late at night.”
📌 Contrast: used to + V1 = past habit (He used to smoke); be used to + V-ing = accustomed (He is used to smoking). Likewise look forward to / object to + V-ing.
✖ A) read (V1 form) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing; C) reads (V1 + s (Simple Present)) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing; D) to read (to + V1 (infinitive)) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing

q: Fill in the blank: By the time you return, Rekha ___ the door.
exp:
✔ ‘By the time you return’ भविष्य का एक बिंदु है; उससे पहले पूरा हो चुका कार्य Future Perfect (will have + V3) में आता है: “By the time you return, Rekha will have locked the door.”
📌 By the time + present tense (return), मुख्य clause में will have + V3; By the time + past tense हो तो had + V3 (By the time we came, he had left)।
✖ A) had locked (Past Perfect) — future completion नहीं बताता; B) was locking (Past Continuous) — future completion नहीं बताता; D) has locked (Present Perfect) — future completion नहीं बताता
expe:
✔ ‘By the time you return’ marks a future point; an action completed before it takes the Future Perfect (will have + V3): “By the time you return, Rekha will have locked the door.”
📌 By the time + present (return) → will have + V3 in the main clause; By the time + past → had + V3 (By the time we came, he had left).
✖ A) had locked (Past Perfect) — does not show completion before a future point; B) was locking (Past Continuous) — does not show completion before a future point; D) has locked (Present Perfect) — does not show completion before a future point

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: Rakesh had been baking a cake for two hours before we came.
exp:
✔ वाक्य “Rakesh had been baking a cake for two hours before we came.” में संरचना had been + V-ing है, अतः यह Past Perfect Continuous tense है — भूतकाल में किसी समय से शुरू होकर दूसरी past घटना तक लगातार चलता रहा कार्य।
📌 Perfect Continuous tenses के साथ प्रायः for (अवधि) / since (आरंभ-बिंदु) आता है; Future Perfect के साथ by + future time।
✖ A) Past Perfect = had + V3; B) Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing; C) Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing
expe:
✔ The sentence “Rakesh had been baking a cake for two hours before we came.” uses the structure had been + V-ing, so it is in the Past Perfect Continuous tense — an action that continued for some time up to another past event.
📌 Perfect Continuous tenses usually take for (duration) / since (starting point); Future Perfect usually takes by + future time.
✖ A) Past Perfect = had + V3; B) Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing; C) Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing

q: Fill in the blank: Neither her sisters nor Seema ___ present at the meeting.
exp:
✔ Neither…nor / Either…or में verb निकटतम (दूसरे) subject के अनुसार होती है (Rule of Proximity)। यहाँ निकटतम subject ‘Seema’ एकवचन है, और ‘at the meeting’ से past है — अतः ‘was’।
📌 उदाहरण: Neither the teacher nor the students were present; Either the boys or Ram is to blame। सुझाव: plural subject को nor के बाद रखें।
✖ B) were (plural verb) — निकटतम subject/काल से मेल नहीं; C) are (plural verb) — निकटतम subject/काल से मेल नहीं; D) have (plural verb) — निकटतम subject/काल से मेल नहीं
expe:
✔ With Neither…nor / Either…or, the verb agrees with the nearer (second) subject (rule of proximity). Here ‘Seema’ is singular, and the context is past — so ‘was’.
📌 Examples: Neither the teacher nor the students were present; Either the boys or Ram is to blame. Tip: place the plural subject after nor.
✖ B) were (plural verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense; C) are (plural verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense; D) have (plural verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense

q: Fill in the blank: Deepak ___ a picture since Monday and is still at it.
exp:
✔ ‘since/for … and is still at it’ = कार्य past में शुरू होकर अब भी चल रहा है → Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing): “Deepak has been drawing a picture since Monday and is still at it.”
📌 since + समय-बिंदु (since Monday, since 9 o'clock); for + अवधि (for two hours)। Singular subject → has been, plural/I/you → have been।
✖ A) was drawing (Past Continuous) — since/for वाली जारी क्रिया नहीं बताता; C) draws (V1 + s (Simple Present)) — since/for वाली जारी क्रिया नहीं बताता; D) is drawing (Present Continuous) — since/for वाली जारी क्रिया नहीं बताता
expe:
✔ ‘since/for … and is still at it’ means the action began in the past and is still going on → Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing): “Deepak has been drawing a picture since Monday and is still at it.”
📌 since + point of time (since Monday, since 9 o'clock); for + period (for two hours). Singular subject → has been; plural/I/you → have been.
✖ A) was drawing (Past Continuous) — cannot show an ongoing action with since/for; C) draws (V1 + s (Simple Present)) — cannot show an ongoing action with since/for; D) is drawing (Present Continuous) — cannot show an ongoing action with since/for

q: Fill in the blank: If the shop had been open, Sita ___ the letter.
exp:
✔ ‘If the shop had been open’ — यह Third Conditional है: If + had + V3, … would have + V3 (past की अवास्तविक स्थिति)। अतः “If the shop had been open, Sita would have posted the letter.”
📌 Zero: If + present, present; First: If + present, will + V1; Second: If + V2/were, would + V1; Third: If + had + V3, would have + V3। If-clause में will/would नहीं आता।
✖ A) had posted (Past Perfect) — Third Conditional के pattern से मेल नहीं; B) will have posted (Future Perfect) — Third Conditional के pattern से मेल नहीं; D) will post (Simple Future) — Third Conditional के pattern से मेल नहीं
expe:
✔ ‘If the shop had been open’ is a Third Conditional: If + had + V3, … would have + V3 (unreal past). Hence “If the shop had been open, Sita would have posted the letter.”
📌 Zero: If + present, present; First: If + present, will + V1; Second: If + V2/were, would + V1; Third: If + had + V3, would have + V3. No will/would in the if-clause.
✖ A) had posted (Past Perfect) — does not match the Third Conditional pattern; B) will have posted (Future Perfect) — does not match the Third Conditional pattern; D) will post (Simple Future) — does not match the Third Conditional pattern

q: Fill in the blank: The players wish they ___ birds.
exp:
✔ ‘wish’ के बाद अवास्तविक/काल्पनिक स्थिति के लिए subjunctive ‘were’ आता है — सभी subjects के साथ (I/he/they were): “The players wish they were birds.”
📌 इसी नियम पर: If I were you…; He behaves as though he were a king; I wish I were rich। past की इच्छा: wish + had + V3 (I wish I had gone)।
✖ A) will be (Simple Future) — unreal स्थिति में were चाहिए; B) are (plural verb) — unreal स्थिति में were चाहिए; C) have been (Present Perfect) — unreal स्थिति में were चाहिए
expe:

q: Fill in the blank: Neither Nisha nor the servants ___ present at the meeting.
exp:

expe:
✔ With Neither…nor / Either…or, the verb agrees with the nearer (second) subject (rule of proximity). Here ‘the servants’ is plural, and the context is past — so ‘were’.
📌 Examples: Neither the teacher nor the students were present; Either the boys or Ram is to blame. Tip: place the plural subject after nor.
✖ B) has (singular verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense; C) was (singular verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense; D) is (singular verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense

📌 By the time + present (return) → will have + V3 in the main clause; By the time + past → had + V3 (By the time we came, he had left).
✖ A) had made (Past Perfect) — does not show completion before a future point; C) were making (Past Continuous) — does not show completion before a future point; D) have made (Present Perfect) — does not show completion before a future point

q: Identify the tense of the following sentence: The girls will have finished the work by tomorrow.
exp:
✔ वाक्य “The girls will have finished the work by tomorrow.” में संरचना will have + V3 है, अतः यह Future Perfect tense है — भविष्य के किसी समय से पहले पूरा हो चुका कार्य।
📌 Perfect Continuous tenses के साथ प्रायः for (अवधि) / since (आरंभ-बिंदु) आता है; Future Perfect के साथ by + future time।
✖ A) Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing; B) Present Perfect = has/have + V3; D) Past Perfect = had + V3
expe:
✔ The sentence “The girls will have finished the work by tomorrow.” uses the structure will have + V3, so it is in the Future Perfect tense — an action completed before a future time.
📌 Perfect Continuous tenses usually take for (duration) / since (starting point); Future Perfect usually takes by + future time.
✖ A) Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing; B) Present Perfect = has/have + V3; D) Past Perfect = had + V3

q: Fill in the blank: Ten kilometres ___ a long distance to walk.
exp:
✔ दूरी, समय, धन या वजन की मात्रा (Ten kilometres) को एक इकाई माना जाता है, इसलिए singular verb → ‘is’: “Ten kilometres is a long distance to walk.”
📌 उदाहरण: Five hundred rupees is a big sum; Two hours is enough time।
✖ A) have (plural verb) — मात्रा-सूचक subject के साथ गलत; B) are (plural verb) — मात्रा-सूचक subject के साथ गलत; C) were (plural verb) — मात्रा-सूचक subject के साथ गलत
expe:
✔ An amount of distance, time, money or weight (Ten kilometres) is treated as one unit, so it takes a singular verb → ‘is’: “Ten kilometres is a long distance to walk.”
📌 Examples: Five hundred rupees is a big sum; Two hours is enough time.
✖ A) have (plural verb) — wrong with a quantity treated as one unit; B) are (plural verb) — wrong with a quantity treated as one unit; C) were (plural verb) — wrong with a quantity treated as one unit

q: Fill in the blank: Rohan ___ a song since 9 o'clock and is still at it.
exp:
✔ ‘since/for … and is still at it’ = कार्य past में शुरू होकर अब भी चल रहा है → Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing): “Rohan has been singing a song since 9 o'clock and is still at it.”
📌 since + समय-बिंदु (since Monday, since 9 o'clock); for + अवधि (for two hours)। Singular subject → has been, plural/I/you → have been।
✖ B) sings (V1 + s (Simple Present)) — since/for वाली जारी क्रिया नहीं बताता; C) is singing (Present Continuous) — since/for वाली जारी क्रिया नहीं बताता; D) was singing (Past Continuous) — since/for वाली जारी क्रिया नहीं बताता
expe:
✔ ‘since/for … and is still at it’ means the action began in the past and is still going on → Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing): “Rohan has been singing a song since 9 o'clock and is still at it.”
📌 since + point of time (since Monday, since 9 o'clock); for + period (for two hours). Singular subject → has been; plural/I/you → have been.
✖ B) sings (V1 + s (Simple Present)) — cannot show an ongoing action with since/for; C) is singing (Present Continuous) — cannot show an ongoing action with since/for; D) was singing (Past Continuous) — cannot show an ongoing action with since/for

q: Fill in the blank: If the shop were open, my father ___ these books.
exp:
✔ ‘If the shop were open’ — यह Second Conditional है: If + V2/were, … would + V1 (वर्तमान/भविष्य की काल्पनिक स्थिति)। अतः “If the shop were open, my father would read these books.”
📌 Zero: If + present, present; First: If + present, will + V1; Second: If + V2/were, would + V1; Third: If + had + V3, would have + V3। If-clause में will/would नहीं आता।
✖ A) will have read (Future Perfect) — Second Conditional के pattern से मेल नहीं; C) would have read (would have + V3 (Third Conditional)) — Second Conditional के pattern से मेल नहीं; D) will read (Simple Future) — Second Conditional के pattern से मेल नहीं
expe:
✔ ‘If the shop were open’ is a Second Conditional: If + V2/were, … would + V1 (imaginary present/future). Hence “If the shop were open, my father would read these books.”
📌 Zero: If + present, present; First: If + present, will + V1; Second: If + V2/were, would + V1; Third: If + had + V3, would have + V3. No will/would in the if-clause.
✖ A) will have read (Future Perfect) — does not match the Second Conditional pattern; C) would have read (would have + V3 (Third Conditional)) — does not match the Second Conditional pattern; D) will read (Simple Future) — does not match the Second Conditional pattern

q: Fill in the blank: It is high time Divya ___ the poor.
exp:
✔ ‘It is high time’ के बाद subject + V2 (past subjunctive) आता है, भले अर्थ वर्तमान का हो। अतः सही वाक्य: “It is high time Divya helped the poor.”
📌 इसी नियम पर: It is time / It is about time + V2; या It is high time + for + object + to + V1 (It is high time for him to go)।
✖ A) help (V1 (base form)) — high time के बाद यह रूप नहीं आता; B) has helped (Present Perfect) — high time के बाद यह रूप नहीं आता; D) will help (Simple Future) — high time के बाद यह रूप नहीं आता
expe:
✔ ‘It is high time’ is followed by subject + V2 (past subjunctive) though the meaning is present. Correct: “It is high time Divya helped the poor.”
📌 Same rule: It is time / It is about time + V2; alternatively It is high time + for + object + to + V1 (It is high time for him to go).
✖ A) help (V1 (base form)) — not used after 'high time'; B) has helped (Present Perfect) — not used after 'high time'; D) will help (Simple Future) — not used after 'high time'

q: Fill in the blank: My father has got used to ___ at night.
exp:
✔ ‘be/get used to’ (आदी होना) में ‘to’ preposition है, इसलिए इसके बाद gerund (V-ing) आता है: “My father has got used to working at night.”
📌 अंतर याद रखें: used to + V1 = past की आदत (He used to smoke); be used to + V-ing = आदी होना (He is used to smoking)। इसी तरह look forward to / object to + V-ing।
✖ A) to work (to + V1 (infinitive)) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए; B) worked (V2 / Simple Past) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए; C) work (V1 (base form)) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए
expe:
✔ In ‘be/get used to’ (= accustomed to), ‘to’ is a preposition, so it takes a gerund (V-ing): “My father has got used to working at night.”
📌 Contrast: used to + V1 = past habit (He used to smoke); be used to + V-ing = accustomed (He is used to smoking). Likewise look forward to / object to + V-ing.
✖ A) to work (to + V1 (infinitive)) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing; B) worked (V2 / Simple Past) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing; C) work (V1 (base form)) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing

q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
opts: If Vikas would have tried, he would have washed the dishes.
It is high time Manoj sweeps the floor.
Manoj has grown roses before the guests arrived.
exp:
✔ “Neha repaired old watches yesterday.” — Simple Past + past time — सही। बाकी तीनों वाक्यों में tense/verb की त्रुटि है।
📌 मुख्य नियम: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 के साथ Simple Past (Present Perfect नहीं); before + past घटना से पहले had + V3; If-clause में would नहीं; It is high time + V2।
✖ B) If-clause में would have नहीं, had + V3 चाहिए (had tried); C) ‘It is high time’ के बाद V2 चाहिए: sweeps → swept; D) past घटना से पहले का कार्य Past Perfect में: has grown → had grown
expe:
✔ “Neha repaired old watches yesterday.” — Simple Past with a past time expression — correct. The other three sentences contain tense/verb errors.
📌 Key rules: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 take Simple Past (not Present Perfect); action before a past event → had + V3; no ‘would’ in the if-clause; It is high time + V2.
✖ B) the if-clause needs had + V3 (had tried), not would have; C) ‘It is high time’ needs V2: sweeps → swept; D) an action before another past event needs the Past Perfect: has grown → had grown

q: Fill in the blanks: If Lata ___ more time, she ___ the letter.
exp:
✔ Third Conditional (past की अवास्तविक स्थिति): If + had + V3, … would have + V3। ‘have’ का V3 ‘had’ है, इसलिए ‘had had’: “If Lata had had more time, she would have posted the letter.”
📌 Second Conditional: If she had more time, she would finish (वर्तमान की कल्पना)। If-clause में would नहीं आता।
✖ A) would have, would post — If-clause में would नहीं आता; C) had, would have posted — If-clause में केवल had (V2) है; past की अवास्तविक स्थिति के standard Third Conditional में had + V3 (had had) चाहिए; D) had had, will post — had had के साथ will नहीं, would have + V3 चाहिए
expe:
✔ Third Conditional (unreal past): If + had + V3, … would have + V3. The V3 of ‘have’ is ‘had’, hence ‘had had’: “If Lata had had more time, she would have posted the letter.”
📌 Second Conditional: If she had more time, she would finish (present imagination). Never use ‘would’ in the if-clause.
✖ A) would have, would post — ‘would’ is not used in the if-clause; C) had, would have posted — the if-clause has only ‘had’ (V2); the standard Third Conditional for an unreal past needs had + V3 (had had); D) had had, will post — ‘had had’ needs would have + V3, not will

q: Fill in the blank: Meena said that water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
exp:
✔ Reported speech में reporting verb past हो तब भी सार्वभौमिक सत्य/वैज्ञानिक तथ्य (“water boils at 100 degrees Celsius”) का tense नहीं बदलता — Simple Present रहता है → ‘boils’।
📌 अन्य अपवाद: habitual facts और proverbs भी present में रहते हैं (He said that honesty is the best policy)। सामान्य नियम: past reporting verb → tense एक कदम पीछे।
✖ A) was boiling (Past Continuous) — universal truth में tense नहीं बदलता; B) boiled (V2 / Simple Past) — universal truth में tense नहीं बदलता; D) had boiled (Past Perfect) — universal truth में tense नहीं बदलता
expe:
✔ In reported speech, even after a past reporting verb, a universal truth/scientific fact (“water boils at 100 degrees Celsius”) keeps the Simple Present → ‘boils’.
📌 Other exceptions: habitual facts and proverbs also stay in the present (He said that honesty is the best policy). General rule: past reporting verb → tense moves one step back.
✖ A) was boiling (Past Continuous) — a universal truth is not back-shifted; B) boiled (V2 / Simple Past) — a universal truth is not back-shifted; D) had boiled (Past Perfect) — a universal truth is not back-shifted

q: Fill in the blank: Many a member ___ failed in this exam.
exp:
✔ ‘Many a + singular noun’ (Many a member) अर्थ में बहुवचन होने पर भी singular verb लेता है → ‘has’: “Many a member has failed in this exam.”
📌 इसी तरह Each / Every / More than one + singular noun → singular verb (More than one student has come)।
✖ A) are (plural verb) — Many a के साथ singular verb चाहिए; B) were (plural verb) — Many a के साथ singular verb चाहिए; C) have (plural verb) — Many a के साथ singular verb चाहिए
expe:
✔ ‘Many a + singular noun’ (Many a member) is plural in meaning but takes a singular verb → ‘has’: “Many a member has failed in this exam.”
📌 Likewise Each / Every / More than one + singular noun → singular verb (More than one student has come).
✖ A) are (plural verb) — ‘Many a’ needs a singular verb; B) were (plural verb) — ‘Many a’ needs a singular verb; C) have (plural verb) — ‘Many a’ needs a singular verb

q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
opts: Sanjay had helped the poor before it got dark.
Ajay did not decorated the hall last Sunday.
My uncle has written the report last month.
It is high time my brother prints the posters.
exp:
✔ “Sanjay had helped the poor before it got dark.” — had + V3 … before + past — सही Past Perfect। बाकी तीनों वाक्यों में tense/verb की त्रुटि है।
📌 मुख्य नियम: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 के साथ Simple Past (Present Perfect नहीं); before + past घटना से पहले had + V3; If-clause में would नहीं; It is high time + V2।
✖ B) did not के बाद V1 आता है: decorated → decorate; C) निश्चित past time (‘last month’) के साथ Present Perfect नहीं, Simple Past चाहिए: has written → wrote; D) ‘It is high time’ के बाद V2 चाहिए: prints → printed
expe:
✔ “Sanjay had helped the poor before it got dark.” — had + V3 … before + past — correct Past Perfect. The other three sentences contain tense/verb errors.
📌 Key rules: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 take Simple Past (not Present Perfect); action before a past event → had + V3; no ‘would’ in the if-clause; It is high time + V2.
✖ B) ‘did not’ takes V1: decorated → decorate; C) Present Perfect cannot take a definite past time (‘last month’); use Simple Past: has written → wrote; D) ‘It is high time’ needs V2: prints → printed

q: Fill in the blanks: If Vijay ___ the manager, he ___ the posters at once.
exp:
✔ Second Conditional (वर्तमान की अवास्तविक स्थिति — वह manager नहीं है): If + subject + were, … would + V1। सभी subjects के साथ ‘were’: “If Vijay were the manager, he would print the posters at once.”
📌 उदाहरण: If I were a bird, I would fly। Third Conditional: If he had been the manager, he would have + V3।
✖ A) had been, will print — had been के साथ would have + V3 चाहिए, will नहीं; C) were, will print — were के साथ will नहीं, would चाहिए; D) is, would print — is (First Conditional) के साथ would नहीं, will आता
expe:
✔ Second Conditional (unreal present — he/she is not the manager): If + subject + were, … would + V1, with ‘were’ for every subject: “If Vijay were the manager, he would print the posters at once.”
📌 Example: If I were a bird, I would fly. Third Conditional: If he had been the manager, he would have + V3.
✖ A) had been, will print — ‘had been’ needs would have + V3, not will; C) were, will print — ‘were’ needs would, not will; D) is, would print — ‘is’ (First Conditional) takes will, not would

q: Fill in the blank: Suresh explained that light ___ faster than sound.
exp:

✖ A) had travelled (Past Perfect) — universal truth में tense नहीं बदलता; B) travelled (V2 / Simple Past) — universal truth में tense नहीं बदलता; D) was travelling (Past Continuous) — universal truth में tense नहीं बदलता
expe:

📌 Other exceptions: habitual facts and proverbs also stay in the present (He said that honesty is the best policy). General rule: past reporting verb → tense moves one step back.

q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
opts: If Lata had tried, she would have swept the courtyard.
Priya has delivered the parcel before the teacher came.
It is high time Pooja plants a mango tree.
Anita did not invited the guests two days ago.
exp:
✔ “If Lata had tried, she would have swept the courtyard.” — If + had + V3, would have + V3 — सही Third Conditional। बाकी तीनों वाक्यों में tense/verb की त्रुटि है।
📌 मुख्य नियम: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 के साथ Simple Past (Present Perfect नहीं); before + past घटना से पहले had + V3; If-clause में would नहीं; It is high time + V2।
✖ B) past घटना से पहले का कार्य Past Perfect में: has delivered → had delivered; C) ‘It is high time’ के बाद V2 चाहिए: plants → planted; D) did not के बाद V1 आता है: invited → invite
expe:
✔ “If Lata had tried, she would have swept the courtyard.” — If + had + V3, would have + V3 — correct Third Conditional. The other three sentences contain tense/verb errors.
📌 Key rules: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 take Simple Past (not Present Perfect); action before a past event → had + V3; no ‘would’ in the if-clause; It is high time + V2.
✖ B) an action before another past event needs the Past Perfect: has delivered → had delivered; C) ‘It is high time’ needs V2: plants → planted; D) ‘did not’ takes V1: invited → invite

q: Fill in the blanks: Hardly ___ Manoj reached the station ___ someone called.
exp:
✔ ‘Hardly’ नकारात्मक-अर्थ वाला शब्द है; वाक्य के आरंभ में आने पर inversion होता है (had + subject + V3) और इसके साथ ‘when’ (या before) आता है: “Hardly had Manoj reached the station when someone called.”
📌 जोड़े याद रखें: Hardly/Scarcely … when; No sooner … than। पहली घटना Past Perfect में, दूसरी Simple Past में।
✖ A) did, than — ‘than’ No sooner के साथ आता है; C) has, then — has से past sequence नहीं बनता; D) had, than — ‘than’ No sooner के साथ आता है
expe:
✔ ‘Hardly’ is a negative adverb; at the start of a sentence it causes inversion (had + subject + V3) and pairs with ‘when’ (or before): “Hardly had Manoj reached the station when someone called.”
📌 Remember the pairs: Hardly/Scarcely … when; No sooner … than. The first action is in the Past Perfect, the second in the Simple Past.
✖ A) did, than — ‘than’ pairs with No sooner; C) has, then — ‘has’ does not fit a past sequence; D) had, than — ‘than’ pairs with No sooner

q: Choose the grammatically incorrect sentence:
opts: It is high time Gopal arranges the chairs.
If Rohan had tried, he would have painted the doors.
Pooja had grown wheat before the teacher came.
Deepak invited the guests last year.
exp:

✔ First Conditional (संभावित भविष्य): If + Simple Present, … will + V1। ‘before noon’ भविष्य की संभावना है: “If Sanjay starts early, he will study history before noon.”
📌 If-clause में will नहीं आता (If it rains, we will stay — not ‘If it will rain’)। Unless = If … not।
✖ B) will start, will study — If-clause में will नहीं आता; C) starts, would have studied — present के साथ would have + V3 असंगत; D) started, will study — started (V2) के साथ would + V1 आता, will नहीं
expe:
✔ First Conditional (likely future): If + simple present, … will + V1. ‘Before noon’ refers to a real future possibility: “If Sanjay starts early, he will study history before noon.”
📌 No ‘will’ in the if-clause (If it rains, we will stay — not ‘If it will rain’). Unless = If … not.
✖ B) will start, will study — ‘will’ is not used in the if-clause; C) starts, would have studied — present with would have + V3 is mismatched; D) started, will study — ‘started’ (V2) pairs with would + V1, not will

q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
opts: If Harish would have tried, he would have built a house.

My mother has collected stamps the day before yesterday.
exp:
✔ “It is high time Divya cleaned the kitchen.” — ‘It is high time’ + V2 — सही। बाकी तीनों वाक्यों में tense/verb की त्रुटि है।
📌 मुख्य नियम: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 के साथ Simple Past (Present Perfect नहीं); before + past घटना से पहले had + V3; If-clause में would नहीं; It is high time + V2।
✖ A) If-clause में would have नहीं, had + V3 चाहिए (had tried); B) did not के बाद V1 आता है: printed → print; D) निश्चित past time (‘the day before yesterday’) के साथ Present Perfect नहीं, Simple Past चाहिए: has collected → collected
expe:
✔ “It is high time Divya cleaned the kitchen.” — ‘It is high time’ + V2 — correct. The other three sentences contain tense/verb errors.
📌 Key rules: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 take Simple Past (not Present Perfect); action before a past event → had + V3; no ‘would’ in the if-clause; It is high time + V2.
✖ A) the if-clause needs had + V3 (had tried), not would have; B) ‘did not’ takes V1: printed → print; D) Present Perfect cannot take a definite past time (‘the day before yesterday’); use Simple Past: has collected → collected

q: Fill in the blanks: If Shalini ___ more time, she ___ the courtyard.
exp:
✔ Third Conditional (past की अवास्तविक स्थिति): If + had + V3, … would have + V3। ‘have’ का V3 ‘had’ है, इसलिए ‘had had’: “If Shalini had had more time, she would have swept the courtyard.”
📌 Second Conditional: If she had more time, she would finish (वर्तमान की कल्पना)। If-clause में would नहीं आता।
✖ A) had had, will sweep — had had के साथ will नहीं, would have + V3 चाहिए; B) would have, would sweep — If-clause में would नहीं आता; D) had, would have swept — If-clause में केवल had (V2) है; past की अवास्तविक स्थिति के standard Third Conditional में had + V3 (had had) चाहिए
expe:
✔ Third Conditional (unreal past): If + had + V3, … would have + V3. The V3 of ‘have’ is ‘had’, hence ‘had had’: “If Shalini had had more time, she would have swept the courtyard.”
📌 Second Conditional: If she had more time, she would finish (present imagination). Never use ‘would’ in the if-clause.
✖ A) had had, will sweep — ‘had had’ needs would have + V3, not will; B) would have, would sweep — ‘would’ is not used in the if-clause; D) had, would have swept — the if-clause has only ‘had’ (V2); the standard Third Conditional for an unreal past needs had + V3 (had had)

exp:
✔ Third Conditional (past की अवास्तविक स्थिति): If + had + V3, … would have + V3। ‘have’ का V3 ‘had’ है, इसलिए ‘had had’: “If Manoj had had more time, he would have studied history.”
📌 Second Conditional: If she had more time, she would finish (वर्तमान की कल्पना)। If-clause में would नहीं आता।
✖ A) had had, will study — had had के साथ will नहीं, would have + V3 चाहिए; B) had, would have studied — If-clause में केवल had (V2) है; past की अवास्तविक स्थिति के standard Third Conditional में had + V3 (had had) चाहिए; D) would have, would study — If-clause में would नहीं आता
expe:
✔ Third Conditional (unreal past): If + had + V3, … would have + V3. The V3 of ‘have’ is ‘had’, hence ‘had had’: “If Manoj had had more time, he would have studied history.”
📌 Second Conditional: If she had more time, she would finish (present imagination). Never use ‘would’ in the if-clause.
✖ A) had had, will study — ‘had had’ needs would have + V3, not will; B) had, would have studied — the if-clause has only ‘had’ (V2); the standard Third Conditional for an unreal past needs had + V3 (had had); D) would have, would study — ‘would’ is not used in the if-clause

q: Fill in the blank: The girl told us that honesty ___ the best policy.
exp:
✔ Reported speech में reporting verb past हो तब भी सार्वभौमिक सत्य/वैज्ञानिक तथ्य (“honesty is the best policy”) का tense नहीं बदलता — Simple Present रहता है → ‘is’।
📌 अन्य अपवाद: habitual facts और proverbs भी present में रहते हैं (He said that honesty is the best policy)। सामान्य नियम: past reporting verb → tense एक कदम पीछे।
✖ A) was (singular verb) — universal truth में tense नहीं बदलता; B) had been (Past Perfect) — universal truth में tense नहीं बदलता; C) were (plural verb) — universal truth में tense नहीं बदलता
expe:
✔ In reported speech, even after a past reporting verb, a universal truth/scientific fact (“honesty is the best policy”) keeps the Simple Present → ‘is’.
📌 Other exceptions: habitual facts and proverbs also stay in the present (He said that honesty is the best policy). General rule: past reporting verb → tense moves one step back.
✖ A) was (singular verb) — a universal truth is not back-shifted; B) had been (Past Perfect) — a universal truth is not back-shifted; C) were (plural verb) — a universal truth is not back-shifted

q: Choose the grammatically incorrect sentence:
opts: It is high time Anil solves the puzzle.
Mohan had swept the floor before the teacher came.
If Naveen had tried, he would have decorated the house.
Meena planted a mango tree yesterday.
exp:
✔ “It is high time Anil solves the puzzle.” गलत है — ‘It is high time’ के बाद V2 चाहिए: solves → solved। बाकी तीनों वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से सही हैं।
📌 मुख्य नियम: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 के साथ Simple Past (Present Perfect नहीं); before + past घटना से पहले had + V3; If-clause में would नहीं; It is high time + V2।
✖ B) had + V3 … before + past — सही Past Perfect; C) If + had + V3, would have + V3 — सही Third Conditional; D) Simple Past + past time — सही
expe:
✔ “It is high time Anil solves the puzzle.” is incorrect — ‘It is high time’ needs V2: solves → solved. The other three sentences are grammatically correct.
📌 Key rules: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 take Simple Past (not Present Perfect); action before a past event → had + V3; no ‘would’ in the if-clause; It is high time + V2.
✖ B) had + V3 … before + past — correct Past Perfect; C) If + had + V3, would have + V3 — correct Third Conditional; D) Simple Past with a past time expression — correct

q: Fill in the blanks: If Vijay ___ the manager, he ___ a plan at once.
exp:
✔ Second Conditional (वर्तमान की अवास्तविक स्थिति — वह manager नहीं है): If + subject + were, … would + V1। सभी subjects के साथ ‘were’: “If Vijay were the manager, he would prepare a plan at once.”
📌 उदाहरण: If I were a bird, I would fly। Third Conditional: If he had been the manager, he would have + V3।
✖ A) is, would prepare — is (First Conditional) के साथ would नहीं, will आता; C) were, will prepare — were के साथ will नहीं, would चाहिए; D) had been, will prepare — had been के साथ would have + V3 चाहिए, will नहीं
expe:
✔ Second Conditional (unreal present — he/she is not the manager): If + subject + were, … would + V1, with ‘were’ for every subject: “If Vijay were the manager, he would prepare a plan at once.”
📌 Example: If I were a bird, I would fly. Third Conditional: If he had been the manager, he would have + V3.
✖ A) is, would prepare — ‘is’ (First Conditional) takes will, not would; C) were, will prepare — ‘were’ needs would, not will; D) had been, will prepare — ‘had been’ needs would have + V3, not will

q: Choose the grammatically incorrect sentence:
opts: It is high time Rahul locked the door.

exp:
✔ “Pooja has invited the guests before the teacher came.” गलत है — past घटना से पहले का कार्य Past Perfect में: has invited → had invited। बाकी तीनों वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से सही हैं।
📌 मुख्य नियम: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 के साथ Simple Past (Present Perfect नहीं); before + past घटना से पहले had + V3; If-clause में would नहीं; It is high time + V2।
✖ A) ‘It is high time’ + V2 — सही; B) If + had + V3, would have + V3 — सही Third Conditional; C) did not + V1 — सही

q: Fill in the blanks: If Meena ___ early, she ___ the form before noon.
exp:
✔ First Conditional (संभावित भविष्य): If + Simple Present, … will + V1। ‘before noon’ भविष्य की संभावना है: “If Meena starts early, she will sign the form before noon.”
📌 If-clause में will नहीं आता (If it rains, we will stay — not ‘If it will rain’)। Unless = If … not।
✖ B) starts, would have signed — present के साथ would have + V3 असंगत; C) started, will sign — started (V2) के साथ would + V1 आता, will नहीं; D) will start, will sign — If-clause में will नहीं आता
expe:
✔ First Conditional (likely future): If + simple present, … will + V1. ‘Before noon’ refers to a real future possibility: “If Meena starts early, she will sign the form before noon.”
📌 No ‘will’ in the if-clause (If it rains, we will stay — not ‘If it will rain’). Unless = If … not.
✖ B) starts, would have signed — present with would have + V3 is mismatched; C) started, will sign — ‘started’ (V2) pairs with would + V1, not will; D) will start, will sign — ‘will’ is not used in the if-clause

q: Fill in the blanks: No sooner ___ Rahul entered the room ___ it began to rain.
exp:
✔ ‘No sooner’ के बाद inversion (had + subject + V3) होता है और इसका जोड़ा ‘than’ है: “No sooner had Rahul entered the room than it began to rain.”
📌 जोड़े याद रखें: No sooner … than; Hardly/Scarcely … when। ‘No sooner … when/then’ गलत है।
✖ A) did, then — ‘did’ व ‘then’ गलत जोड़ा है; B) had, when — ‘when’ Hardly/Scarcely के साथ आता है; D) has, than — has से past sequence नहीं बनता
expe:
✔ ‘No sooner’ causes inversion (had + subject + V3) and is always paired with ‘than’: “No sooner had Rahul entered the room than it began to rain.”
📌 Remember the pairs: No sooner … than; Hardly/Scarcely … when. ‘No sooner … when/then’ is wrong.
✖ A) did, then — ‘did’ and ‘then’ are a wrong pairing; B) had, when — ‘when’ pairs with Hardly/Scarcely; D) has, than — ‘has’ does not fit a past sequence

exp:

✖ A) निश्चित past time (‘last year’) के साथ Present Perfect नहीं, Simple Past चाहिए: has bought → bought; B) निश्चित past time (‘yesterday’) के साथ Present Perfect नहीं, Simple Past चाहिए: has drawn → drew; C) ‘It is high time’ के बाद V2 चाहिए: types → typed

q: Fill in the blanks: Scarcely ___ Sunita reached the station ___ the train left.
exp:
✔ ‘Scarcely’ नकारात्मक-अर्थ वाला शब्द है; वाक्य के आरंभ में आने पर inversion होता है (had + subject + V3) और इसके साथ ‘when’ (या before) आता है: “Scarcely had Sunita reached the station when the train left.”
📌 जोड़े याद रखें: Hardly/Scarcely … when; No sooner … than। पहली घटना Past Perfect में, दूसरी Simple Past में।
✖ B) did, then — ‘did’ व ‘then’ गलत जोड़ा है; C) had, than — ‘than’ No sooner के साथ आता है; D) has, than — ‘than’ No sooner के साथ आता है
expe:
✔ ‘Scarcely’ is a negative adverb; at the start of a sentence it causes inversion (had + subject + V3) and pairs with ‘when’ (or before): “Scarcely had Sunita reached the station when the train left.”
📌 Remember the pairs: Hardly/Scarcely … when; No sooner … than. The first action is in the Past Perfect, the second in the Simple Past.
✖ B) did, then — ‘did’ and ‘then’ are a wrong pairing; C) had, than — ‘than’ pairs with No sooner; D) has, than — ‘than’ pairs with No sooner

q: Fill in the blank: Divya wants to become ___ actor.
exp:
